+# Watch PR queued stack
+
+The queued runner first refreshes a whole stack, then polls only the lowest
+unmerged frontier between scheduled sweeps. It advances only when the previous
+frontier is observed merged.
+
+**Code owners:** queue planning and snapshots in
+[`planQueue`](../../runtime/codex/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/policy.ts#L535),
+[`applyQueueSnapshot`](../../runtime/codex/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/policy.ts#L574),
+[`evaluateQueue`](../../runtime/codex/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/policy.ts#L644),
+and [`runQueued`](../../runtime/codex/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/policy.ts#L707).
+
+```mermaid
+stateDiagram-v2
+    [*] --> Sweep
+    Sweep --> Evaluate: every non-merged PR has a fresh snapshot
+    Evaluate --> Complete: every queued PR is merged
+    Evaluate --> Blocked: any stack-wide merge blocker
+    Evaluate --> Advance: prior frontier became merged; next open PR exists
+    Evaluate --> Waiting: frontier still pending checks or stack merge is queued
+    Evaluate --> TimedOut: timeout reached with unmerged PRs
+    Advance --> Sweep: emit frontier advance and refresh stack
+    Waiting --> FrontierPoll: polling interval elapses before next whole-stack sweep
+    FrontierPoll --> Evaluate: refresh current lowest unmerged PR
+    FrontierPoll --> Sweep: scheduled sweep is due
+    Complete --> [*]
+    Blocked --> [*]
+    TimedOut --> [*]
+```
+
+| State | Event | Guard | Effect |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Sweep | Queue state created or sweep due | Non-merged PRs remain | Read each non-merged PR in queue order and require a complete sweep before evaluation. |
+| Evaluate | Snapshot set complete | All PRs merged | Return terminal complete verdict. |
+| Evaluate | Snapshot set complete | Any conflict, review thread, failed check, or merge gate | Return terminal blocker verdict. |
+| Evaluate | Frontier changed | Old frontier is now merged and next open PR exists | Update frontier and emit `ADVANCE`. |
+| Evaluate | Frontier not ready | Pending checks or merge queue; timeout not reached | Emit waiting when wait key changes, then sleep. |
+| Evaluate | Frontier not ready | Run deadline reached | Return terminal queued-stack timeout. |
+| Waiting | Interval elapses | Whole-stack sweep is not due | Poll only current frontier. |
+| FrontierPoll | Snapshot applied | Sweep time reached | Start a new whole-stack sweep before further evaluation. |
+
+Query retries and status-query blockers are shared with the simple runner's
+[`pollUntilTerminal`](watch-pr-simple.md).

+# Watch PR simple and stack runner
+
+This runner polls a single PR or ordinary stack until the status-only response,
+a blocker, readiness, query failure, or deadline ends the run.
+
+**Code owners:** [`pollUntilTerminal`](../../runtime/codex/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/policy.ts#L365),
+[`runSimple`](../../runtime/codex/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/policy.ts#L417),
+and classification in [`classifyPr`](../../runtime/codex/skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/policy.ts#L218).
+
+```mermaid
+stateDiagram-v2
+    [*] --> ReadStatus
+    ReadStatus --> StatusOnly: statusOnly requested
+    ReadStatus --> Blocked: conflict, review-thread, failing-check, or merge-gate blocker
+    ReadStatus --> Ready: PR ready/merged, or entire ordinary stack clear
+    ReadStatus --> Waiting: pending checks and no blocker
+    ReadStatus --> RetryWait: retryable status query error below error limit
+    ReadStatus --> QueryBlocked: non-retryable error or max query errors reached
+    Waiting --> ReadStatus: interval elapses before deadline
+    Waiting --> TimedOut: deadline reached with pending checks
+    RetryWait --> ReadStatus: bounded backoff elapses before deadline
+    RetryWait --> TimedOut: deadline reached while status unavailable
+    StatusOnly --> [*]
+    Blocked --> [*]
+    Ready --> [*]
+    QueryBlocked --> [*]
+    TimedOut --> [*]
+```
+
+| State | Event | Guard | Effect |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| ReadStatus | Snapshot read | Status-only mode | Return terminal status snapshot. |
+| ReadStatus | Snapshot classified | Conflict, unresolved review thread, failing check, or merge gate | Return a terminal blocker verdict. |
+| ReadStatus | Snapshot classified | Ready or merged | Return terminal ready verdict. |
+| ReadStatus | Snapshot classified | Open PR has pending checks and no blocker | Emit waiting state and sleep for polling interval. |
+| ReadStatus | Query throws | Retryable and below `maxQueryErrors` | Emit retry notice and sleep with exponential backoff capped at 300 seconds. |
+| ReadStatus | Query throws | Non-retryable or max errors reached | Return terminal status-query blocker. |
+| Waiting or RetryWait | Deadline check | Deadline elapsed | Return terminal timeout verdict. |
+
+The simple runner rejects `queued-stack` mode; that progression is a separate
+machine in [watch-pr queued stack](watch-pr-queued.md).

+# XERJ source snapshot publication
+
+`export_snapshot` validates a full Git commit and a new output path, scans and
+filters tree entries, copies verified blobs, then writes `.snapshot.json` as
+the final receipt. A failure after directory creation can leave a partial
+output without a receipt; because the output now exists, rerunning to that
+path is refused.
+
+**Code owners:** output validation in
+[`validate_output_path`](../../scripts/xerj_snapshot.py#L353), export flow in
+[`export_snapshot`](../../scripts/xerj_snapshot.py#L368), and receipt write at
+[line 475](../../scripts/xerj_snapshot.py#L475).
+
+```mermaid
+stateDiagram-v2
+    [*] --> Validate
+    Validate --> Refused: repository, full commit SHA, or new output path invalid
+    Validate --> ScanTree: all inputs pass and commit resolves
+    ScanTree --> Refused: Git/tree/read validation fails
+    ScanTree --> CreateOutput: exclusions, sensitive-content checks, and collision checks finish
+    CreateOutput --> ExportBlobs: create private output directory
+    ExportBlobs --> Partial: blob read, digest, path, or write fails
+    ExportBlobs --> Receipt: every eligible file written and executable mode restored
+    Receipt --> Published: write .snapshot.json last
+    Published --> [*]: return receipt and totals
+    Partial --> [*]: report error; partial directory remains without receipt
+    Refused --> [*]: return error before output creation
+```
+
+| State | Event | Guard | Effect |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Validate | CLI starts | Repo is valid, commit is full SHA, output absent, parent exists, output outside worktree | Resolve commit, load exclusions, and read tree. |
+| ScanTree | Tree entry examined | Path/mode/type/size or exclusion pattern rejects it | Record exclusion. |
+| ScanTree | Candidate file read | Content is safe and no output-path collision exists | Record size, object ID, and digest for export. |
+| CreateOutput | Scan complete | Eligible set finalized | Create output directory with mode 0700. |
+| ExportBlobs | Blob copied | Blob size and digest match scan | Create file exclusively, preserve executable mode, append export receipt data. |
+| ExportBlobs | Any write or integrity failure | Output directory already exists | Stop; leave partial output in place without `.snapshot.json`. |
+| Receipt | All files exported | Export/exclusion totals sorted | Write `.snapshot.json` with exclusive create as final publication step. |
+
+The output is not installed by rename: its existence is reserved before blob
+copying, and the receipt is the completion marker.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+import json
+import math
+import sys
+
+import board_resources
+
+
+def host_reading():
+    before = board_resources.collect(include_board=False)
+    after = board_resources.collect(include_board=False)
+    fields = ("sampled_at", "total_bytes", "available_bytes", "cores", "load1", "load5",
+              "pressure", "free_percent", "swap_used_bytes", "swapouts", "page_size",
+              "compressor_bytes", "disk_wait_ratio")
+    for sample in (before, after):
+        if sample.get("complete") is not True or sample.get("errors"):
+            raise ValueError("Incomplete host reading")
+        if any(type(sample.get(key)) not in (int, float) or not math.isfinite(sample[key])
+               or sample[key] < 0 for key in fields):
+            raise ValueError("Invalid host reading")
+    gap = after["sampled_at"] - before["sampled_at"]
+    if not 0 < gap <= 2 or after["page_size"] != before["page_size"] or after["swapouts"] < before["swapouts"]:
+        raise ValueError("Unknown swap baseline")
+    swap_growth = max(0, after["swap_used_bytes"] - before["swap_used_bytes"]) / gap
+    swapout_rate = (after["swapouts"] - before["swapouts"]) * after["page_size"] / gap
+    compressor_growth = max(0, after["compressor_bytes"] - before["compressor_bytes"]) / gap
+    if compressor_growth > 1024 ** 2 or after["disk_wait_ratio"] >= 0.25:
+        raise ValueError("Compressor growth or disk wait")
+    return {"schema": 1, "sampled_at": int(after["sampled_at"] * 1000),
+            **{key: after[key] for key in ("total_bytes", "available_bytes", "cores", "load1", "load5", "pressure", "free_percent")},
+            "swap_growth_bytes_per_second": swap_growth, "swapout_bytes_per_second": swapout_rate}
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    try:
+        print(json.dumps(host_reading(), allow_nan=False))
+    except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
+        print("Host admission held: " + str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
+        sys.exit(1)

bundles.description_excerpt:
Improve the board slot governor that LMW-4 installed (PR #72 and its fix; log at ~/.multica-codex/board-governor.jsonl). Keep it small and extend the existing governor; do not add a second one.

1. Adaptive limit (AIMD, as in Netflix concurrency-limits): grow the slot count by one at a time only after a sustained healthy window (load per core, memory pressure, swap and compressor growth, board response time all good), and cut it multiplicatively on pressure (for example halve on high disk wait or memory pressure, to zero on emergency). Replace fixed thresholds where they cause the limit to stick, such as the current hold at 7 with reason pressure_or_reserve while load is around 8 on 14 cores.
2. Start gate (as in GNU parallel --memfree and make -l): before the board starts a new agent, require free memory above a floor plus the per-agent cost (about 2 GB and 0.8 cores from the live readings), and load below a ceiling; otherwise the task stays queued.
3. Waiting agents: make the explicit-wait path the default for long waits (waiting on another task, a PR merge, a deploy window, a reset), so waiting agents release their slot. Document how an agent should wait in the wiki how-to and worker instructions.
4. Read the AGPL-free ideas only; do not copy code from Netflix concurrency-limits or other projects.

Prove it on the live board: a log excerpt showing the limit rising one slot at a time after a healthy window, falling on a real or simulated pressure spike, a start held back by the memory gate, and a waiting agent releasing its slot so a queued task starts. bundles.description:
Trade SPX index-option calls on paper instead of refusing them

Shyam: we must not miss SPX lotto calls because of our own limits. Today the THALA human desk posted an SPX 7650 PUT 0DTE lotto (about \$2.00, size tiny, TP1 SPX 7680, TP2 7650, trailing stop moved 7695 -> 7692 -> 7690, then sold 75%). The bot blocks SPX and SPXW with index_options_unverified_on_alpaca (see SRW-59 report: reports/strategy-replay-workbench/59/report.md; SRW-59 separately fixes recognition and the wrong "MY" question).

Make SPX-style calls tradable on the paper account:
1. Verify the facts first, with real API calls (paper credentials from the 1Password service account in SRW shells, read-only, never print secrets): does Alpaca options trading list SPX/SPXW contracts (asset/contract lookup for today's SPXW 7650P), and can the paper account quote and order them? Record the exact responses.
2. If Alpaca supports them, remove the block for supported index options, with correct contract identity (SPXW for 0DTE/weeklies, cash-settled, PM settlement), quotes and order rules.
3. If not, build the best fallback and let Shyam see it plainly: for example a SPY proxy (SPX/10 strike, same expiry, ratio-adjusted size and levels, with the Executor Bot card saying "SPX 7650P traded as SPY 765P proxy"), or a ledger-only simulated position priced from real SPX option quotes. Compare at least 5 variations (Shyam's rule) on a small comparison page with the trade-offs: tracking error vs SPX, fill realism, liquidity, risk rules and sizing.
4. Underlying-based levels (TP1/TP2/trailing stop on SPX) must track the SPX index level, whichever instrument is traded; stop moves and partial sells link to the same position.
Proof: replay today's exact SPX lotto posts (#841 to #851) and show the position, fills, stop moves and 75% sell end to end, before and after; add them to the release gate. Fail closed on anything not understood. Paper only; never start a second Telegram poller; heavy work through heavy. Coordinate with SRW-59 (rebase after it merges if you touch the same parser code).

new file mode 100644
index 00000000..8336ce89
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/srw61_alpaca_index_options_verify.cjs
@@ -0,0 +1,147 @@
+'use strict';
+
+const crypto = require('node:crypto');
+const fs = require('node:fs');
+const path = require('node:path');
+
+const PAPER_HOST = 'https://paper-api.alpaca.markets';
+const DATA_HOST = 'https://data.alpaca.markets';
+const EXPIRY = process.env.SRW61_SPX_EXPIRY || '2026-10-27';
+const STRIKE = Number(process.env.SRW61_SPX_STRIKE || 7650);
+
+function loadTelegramPaperCredentials() {
+  const configPath = process.env.PAPER_TELEGRAM_CREDENTIALS_FILE
+    || path.join(process.env.HOME || '', '.config', 'strategy-paper', 'telegram-alpaca.json');
+  const raw = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(configPath, 'utf8'));
+  const key = raw.APCA_API_KEY_ID || raw.key || raw.apiKey;
+  const secret = raw.APCA_API_SECRET_KEY || raw.secret || raw.apiSecret;
+  if (!key || !secret) throw new Error(`missing paper credentials in ${configPath}`);
+  return { key, secret, configPath };
+}
+
+function redact(value) {
+  if (typeof value === 'string') {
+    return value.replace(/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}/g, (token) => {
+      const digest = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(token).digest('hex').slice(0, 12);
+      return `<redacted:${digest}>`;
+    });
+  }
+  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(redact);
+  if (value && typeof value === 'object') {
+    const out = {};
+    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(value)) {
+      if (/key|secret|token|authorization/i.test(k)) out[k] = '<redacted>';
+      else out[k] = redact(v);
+    }
+    return out;
+  }
+  return value;
+}
+
+async function fetchJson(url, { key, secret }) {
+  const started = Date.now();
+  const response = await fetch(url, {
+    headers: {
+      'APCA-API-KEY-ID': key,
+      'APCA-API-SECRET-KEY': secret,
+      Accept: 'application/json',
+    },
+  });
+  const text = await response.text();
+  let body;
+  try {
+    body = text.length ? JSON.parse(text) : null;
+  } catch {
+    body = { parseError: true, textPreview: text.slice(0, 200) };
+  }
+  return {
+    url: String(url),
+    status: response.status,
+    ok: response.ok,
+    latencyMs: Date.now() - started,
+    body,
+    redactedBody: redact(body),
+  };
+}
+
+async function runProof({ outDir = process.env.SRW61_REPORT_DIR } = {}) {
+  const { key, secret, configPath } = loadTelegramPaperCredentials();
+  const listUrl = new URL(`${PAPER_HOST}/v2/options/contracts`);
+  listUrl.searchParams.set('underlying_symbols', 'SPX');
+  listUrl.searchParams.set('expiration_date', EXPIRY);
+  listUrl.searchParams.set('status', 'active');
+  listUrl.searchParams.set('type', 'put');
+  listUrl.searchParams.set('strike_price_gte', String(STRIKE));
+  listUrl.searchParams.set('strike_price_lte', String(STRIKE));
+  listUrl.searchParams.set('limit', '100');
+
+  const accountUrl = `${PAPER_HOST}/v2/account`;
+  const list = await fetchJson(listUrl, { key, secret });
+  const account = await fetchJson(accountUrl, { key, secret });
+
+  const rawContracts = list.ok && list.body?.option_contracts ? list.body.option_contracts : [];
+  list.body = list.redactedBody;
+  account.body = account.redactedBody;
+  const weekly = rawContracts.find((row) => row?.root_symbol === 'SPXW' || row?.symbol?.startsWith('SPXW'))
+    || rawContracts[0] || null;
+  let contractDetail = null;
+  let quote = null;
+  if (weekly?.symbol) {
+    contractDetail = await fetchJson(`${PAPER_HOST}/v2/options/contracts/${encodeURIComponent(weekly.symbol)}`, { key, secret });
+    contractDetail.body = contractDetail.redactedBody;
+    const quoteUrl = new URL(`${DATA_HOST}/v1beta1/options/quotes/latest`);
+    quoteUrl.searchParams.set('symbols', weekly.symbol);
+    quoteUrl.searchParams.set('feed', 'indicative');
+    quote = await fetchJson(quoteUrl, { key, secret });
+    quote.body = quote.redactedBody;
+  }
+
+  const summary = {
+    listsSpxIndexOptions: list.ok && rawContracts.length > 0,
+    listsSpxwAtStrike: weekly?.root_symbol === 'SPXW' || Boolean(weekly?.symbol?.startsWith('SPXW')),
+    contractTradable: weekly?.tradable === true || contractDetail?.body?.tradable === true,
+    quoteAvailable: quote?.ok === true,
+    selectedSymbol: weekly?.symbol ?? null,
+    underlyingSymbol: weekly?.underlying_symbol ?? null,
+    style: weekly?.style ?? null,
+    strikePrice: weekly?.strike_price ?? null,
+  };
+
+  const result = {
+    ok: list.ok && account.ok && Boolean(weekly),
+    credentialSource: configPath,
+    query: { expiry: EXPIRY, strike: STRIKE, underlying: 'SPX' },
+    selectedSymbol: weekly?.symbol ?? null,
+    contractCount: rawContracts.length,
+    account: {
+      status: account.status,
+      optionsApproved: account.body?.options_approved_level ?? account.body?.options_trading_level ?? null,
+      tradingBlocked: account.body?.trading_blocked ?? null,
+      accountBlocked: account.body?.account_blocked ?? null,
+    },
+    calls: { list, account, contractDetail, quote },
+    summary,
+  };
+
+  if (outDir) {
+    fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });
+    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'alpaca-index-options-verify.json'), `${JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)}\n`);
+  }
+  return result;
+}
+
+module.exports = { runProof };
+
+if (require.main === module) {
+  runProof({ outDir: process.argv[2] }).then((result) => {
+    console.log(JSON.stringify({
+      ok: result.ok,
+      symbol: result.selectedSymbol,
+      summary: result.summary,
+    }));
+    if (!result.ok) process.exitCode = 1;
+  }).catch((error) => {
+    console.error(error.message || error);
+    process.exitCode = 1;
+  });
+}

+

+

+
+const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
+const SYMBOL = 'SPXW261027P07650000';
+
+async function replayThrough(postIds) {
+  const expected = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'fixtures/srw_release_gate_expected.json')));
+  const probes = expected.probes.filter((row) => row.id.startsWith('probe:srw59_spx_'));
+  const ingress = engine.loadProbePosts(probes).filter((post) => postIds.includes(post.id));
+  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'srw61-proof-'));
+  const options = {
+    recordPath: path.join(dir, 'record.jsonl'),
+    ledgerPath: path.join(dir, 'ledger.json'),
+    jevRecords: loadJevRecords(path.join(ROOT, 'fixtures/srw_release_gate_jev.json')),
+    calendarDays: ['2026-10-27'],
+    clockStartMs: ingress[0].receivedAtMs - 10_000,
+    conditionalWatchOnly: false,
+    accountCash: 250_000,
+    enableCopyTrading: false,
+    listedContracts: new Set(),
+    laneUnderlying: {},
+  };
+  const runtime = await engine.createRuntime(options);
+  Object.assign(runtime, { recordPath: options.recordPath, ledgerPath: options.ledgerPath });
+  const result = await engine.replayIngress({ ingress, runtime, restart: false });
+  const positions = runtime.broker.snapshot().telegramAlerts.positions;
+  return { result, positions, runtime };
+}
+
+function positionStop(positions) {
+  const row = positions.find((p) => p.symbol === SYMBOL);
+  assert.ok(row, 'SPXW lotto position must exist');
+  return row.levels?.stopPrice ?? row.levels?.stop?.price ?? null;
+}
+
+async function runProof({ outDir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'srw61-lotto-')) } = {}) {
+  fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });
+  const reportDir = process.env.SRW61_REPORT_DIR || outDir;
+  const alpaca = await verifyAlpaca({ outDir: reportDir });
+  assert.equal(alpaca.summary.listsSpxIndexOptions, true, 'Alpaca must list SPX index options');
+  assert.equal(alpaca.summary.listsSpxwAtStrike, true, 'Alpaca must list SPXW at the desk strike');
+  assert.ok(alpaca.summary.quoteAvailable || alpaca.summary.contractTradable,
+    'paper account must return a listed contract or quote');
+
+  await srw59.runProof({ outDir: path.join(outDir, 'srw59') });
+
+  const chainIds = [
+    'probe:srw59_spx_841',
+    'probe:srw59_spx_842',
+    'probe:srw59_spx_843',
+    'probe:srw59_spx_844',
+    'probe:srw59_spx_845',
+    'probe:srw59_spx_846',
+  ];
+  const { positions, result } = await replayThrough(chainIds);
+  assert.equal(positionStop(positions), 7690, 'stop must track SPX after posts 842/844/845');
+  const entry = result.posts.find((post) => post.id === 'probe:srw59_spx_841');
+  assert.equal(entry.outcome.submitted, true);

bundles.description:
URGENT, market is open (2026-10-28). The live paper trader (main bb5dad2, deployment 3d018210, timed-only 0, watch-only on, Discord shadow) is refusing calls it must take, and posting noise. Real posts from today, all refused:
- HUMAN LOTTO MRNA BUY CALLS, $230 CALL Exp Oct'30, trailing stop MRNA below $210, size 1/5 -> 'NOT TAKEN: I could not tell which desk or guru authored this card.'
- Kalai (Premarket Plan - bot under training) BUY COST $985 PUT -> 'NOT TAKEN: I could not identify the line that supports the source on this card.'
- THALA guru card 'BUY TSLA $402.5 PUT by Periyapa', MEGA GREEDY, entry while TSLA above $400.89, no stop (we send the sell), size 2/5 -> refused unconsumed_text, asked 'What complete entry or exit instruction should I use?'
- 'Alert type: HUMAN / BUY - SPX / Strike $7,780 / CALL / Expiry Oct'28 2026 (0DTE) / Stock entry SPX 7,722 / Stop none / Targets SPX 7,740, 7,750, 7,760' -> check whether it was taken.
Shyam's rules: (1) a human call IS the desk: a card from the human desk (HUMAN, HUMAN LOTTO, Alert type: HUMAN) needs no separate desk or guru line; never refuse it for missing source. Guru cards name their guru in the card. (2) The bot must take these calls; refusing is a regression. (3) Discord shadow: the comparison window is 5 seconds, not 120; post nothing about shadow comparisons in the operator chat when there is no match or no difference (log them only); when the same call arrives on both Telegram and Discord, take it once and say only that one copy was taken.

Do, in order, fast:
1. Find the regression: replay each post above through the current build and through the previous deployed builds (4831ca4, 87be8ca, 53bacd2) and find the commit that started refusing them. Check 4 theories (source/author line check from SRW-57 fail-closed or SRW-54 refusal changes, SRW-73 intake linking, SRW-68 Discord source, SRW-72 misread changes).
2. If an earlier build takes these calls and is otherwise safe, say so in your status line immediately so the Coordinator can decide on a rollback.
3. Fix it on the current main: human-desk cards accepted as the desk; the TSLA guru card parsed (entry condition 'buy while TSLA is above X', no stop because provider sends the sell); the SPX human card parsed with its three underlying targets; the shadow window 5 s and silent unless a duplicate was taken. Every post above must parse to an order (watch-only conditional rules unchanged) in a replay of the deployed modules.
4. Merge; the deploy automation ships it. Use the release gate through ~/.local/bin/heavy (the receipt reuse from SRW-81 applies). Paper only; never print secrets; never start a second Telegram poller.

+
+A card marked `HUMAN`, `HUMAN LOTTO`, or `Alert type: HUMAN` identifies the human desk. It does not need a separate guru line. A guru card identifies its owner through its title or `Guru:` line. Model extraction may omit a source field, so source validation also reads explicit ownership from the original card. Conflicting ownership still blocks execution.

+The native reader handles the October 28 MRNA, Periyapa TSLA, Kalai COST and human SPX cards. An underlying entry condition such as `buy while TSLA is above $400.89` remains an entry guard. `STOP: none - we send the sell` means provider-managed exits. A human card can state a stop without a target, or underlying targets without a fixed stop. The SPX card retains 7,740, 7,750 and 7,760 as underlying prices. Targets keep the existing full-exit policy; the parser does not invent scale-out percentages. Explicit 1/5 through 5/5 sizing reduces the normal allocation, and lotto wording retains its existing smaller allocation.
+
+The October 28 deployment must set `conditionalWatchOnly=false`, as explicitly authorized for SRW-86. Human plans with stops or targets then proceed through normal paper execution. The watch-only-on replay is a control for the retained policy, not the requested deployment setting.
+
+Parsing a call does not prove an order was submitted. Watch-only conditions, listed-contract lookup, quotes, sizing and account checks still apply. The replay uses the production intake and execution modules with a simulated broker. It never starts a Telegram poller or sends a brokerage order.

Inspect the per-card order counts and receipts. Run `heavy node scripts/srw86_shadow_replay.cjs "$TMPDIR/srw86-shadow.json"` to check one-second paired copies, six-second unmatched copies, one primary buy and no comparison notices. Run `heavy --review node test_srw16_release_gate.js` for the wider release checks. Local replay, merged code and deployed behavior are separate evidence layers.
+
+Discord shadow comparisons use a five-second window. Missing copies and equal comparisons are logged without comparison notices in the operator chat. Only the selected primary source may submit an order. +'use strict';

+const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
+const fs = require('node:fs');
+const os = require('node:os');
+const path = require('node:path');
+const { readNativeProviderCommand } = require('../telegram_provider_parser.js');
+const { readAndVerify } = require('../record_chain.js');
+const engine = require('./srw_replay_engine.cjs');
+const fixture = require('../fixtures/srw86_live_cards.json');
+
+async function runProof(output = null) {
+  const results = [];
+  for (const post of fixture.posts) {
+    const day = '2026-10-28';
+    const parsed = readNativeProviderCommand(post.text, { today: day, providerTag: 'THALA', telegramDateMs: post.telegramDateMs });
+    assert.ok(parsed.ok && parsed.command?.verb === 'buy', `${post.messageKey}: ${parsed.reason || 'missing buy'}`);
+    const command = parsed.command;
+    for (const extra of ['UNKNOWN extra instruction', 'Do not buy this yet', 'only if market momentum stays strong']) {
+      const poisoned = readNativeProviderCommand(`${post.text}\n${extra}`, {
+        today: day, providerTag: 'THALA', telegramDateMs: post.telegramDateMs,
+      });
+      assert.equal(poisoned.ok, false, `${post.messageKey}: extra instruction must not be discarded`);
+    }
+    const human = [':928', ':939'].some(suffix => post.messageKey.endsWith(suffix));
+    assert.equal(command.provenance.desk, human ? 'human_pick' : post.messageKey.endsWith(':936') ? 'guru_periyapa' : 'guru_kalai');
+    if (post.messageKey.endsWith(':939')) assert.deepEqual(command.levels.targets.map(row => row.price), [7740, 7750, 7760]);
+    if (post.messageKey.endsWith(':928')) assert.equal(command.levels.stop.price, 210);
+    if (post.messageKey.endsWith(':936')) {
+      assert.equal(command.levels.stop, null);
+      assert.equal(command.levels.exitPolicy, 'on_signal');
+      assert.equal(command.levels.underlyingEntryGuard.minPrice, 400.89);
+    }
+    for (const conditionalWatchOnly of [false, true]) {
+      const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'srw86-card-'));
+      const runtime = await engine.createRuntime({
+        recordPath: path.join(dir, 'record.jsonl'), ledgerPath: path.join(dir, 'ledger.json'),
+        listedContracts: new Set(), laneUnderlying: {}, calendarDays: [day],
+        clockStartMs: post.telegramDateMs - 60000, accountCash: 250000,
+        enableCopyTrading: false, conditionalWatchOnly, matrixProofIsolation: false,
+        readProviderCard: async (text, context) => readNativeProviderCommand(text, context),
+      });
+      const replay = await engine.replayIngress({
+        ingress: [{ ...post, id: post.messageKey, day, chatId: -1003917021974,
+          messageId: Number(post.messageKey.split(':').at(-1)), receivedAtMs: post.telegramDateMs, updateKind: 'channel_post' }],
+        runtime, restart: false,
+      });
+      const orders = runtime.sim.orders.filter(order => order.side === 'buy');
+      const outcome = replay.posts[0].outcome;
+      const guarded = Boolean(command.entryTrigger || command.levels?.underlyingEntryGuard);
+      const expected = conditionalWatchOnly && human ? 0 : 1;
+      assert.equal(orders.length, expected, `${post.messageKey} watch=${conditionalWatchOnly}: ${JSON.stringify(outcome)}`);
+      const risk = readAndVerify(runtime.recordPath).records.map(row => row.event)
+        .find(event => event.type === 'risk_decision' && event.allowed);
+      const allocationWeight = risk?.checks?.legs?.[0]?.allocation?.wording?.weight ?? null;
+      if (expected && post.messageKey.endsWith(':936')) assert.equal(allocationWeight, 0.4, '2/5 must reduce allocation');
+      if (expected && post.messageKey.endsWith(':928')) assert.equal(allocationWeight, 0.1, 'lotto sizing stays conservative');
+      results.push({ key: post.messageKey, conditionalWatchOnly, guarded, parsed: true,
+        desk: command.provenance.desk, buyOrders: orders.length, allocationWeight, outcome,
+        replies: runtime.replies.map(reply => reply.text), recordPath: runtime.recordPath });
+    }
+  }
+  const deploymentResults = results.filter(row => row.conditionalWatchOnly === false);
+  assert.equal(deploymentResults.length, 4);
+  assert.equal(deploymentResults.reduce((sum, row) => sum + row.buyOrders, 0), 4);
+  const result = { evidence: 'exact_live_posts_through_deployed_intake_and_execution_modules_with_simulated_broker',
+    deploymentRequired: { conditionalWatchOnly: false, buyOrders: 4 }, results };
+  if (output) fs.writeFileSync(output, JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) + '\n');
+  console.log(`srw86-live-cards: ${JSON.stringify(results.map(({ key, conditionalWatchOnly, buyOrders }) => ({ key, conditionalWatchOnly, buyOrders })))}`);
+  return result;
+}

+module.exports = { runProof };
+if (require.main === module) runProof(process.argv[2]).catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode = 1; });

+async function runProof(output) {
+  const results = [];

+      name: 'bot-alerts', route: 'bot', readable: true, eligible: true, reason: null });

+      }, 'create', runtime.getNow(), true, {
+        sourceRoute: 'bot', sourceRouteChannelId: CHANNEL, sourceRouteChannelName: 'bot-alerts',
+      }));
+    };
+    try {
+      await engine.replayIngress({ ingress: [{ ...source, id: source.messageKey, day: '2026-10-28',
+        chatId: -1003917021974, messageId: 936, receivedAtMs: source.telegramDateMs, updateKind: 'channel_post' }],
+        runtime, restart: false, closeOnComplete: false });

+      const notices = events.filter(event => event.type === 'receipt_queued' && event.phase === 'shadow_comparison');
+      assert.equal(notices.length, 0, 'equal and unmatched shadow comparisons must remain silent');
+      assert.equal(events.filter(event => event.type === 'command_enqueued' && event.ok).length, 1);
+      results.push({ delayMs, buyOrders: 1, comparisons: comparisons.length, comparisonNotices: notices.length,
+        replies: runtime.replies.map(reply => reply.text), recordPath: runtime.recordPath });
+    } finally {
+      await runtime.alerts.close();
+    }
+  }
+  if (output) fs.writeFileSync(output, JSON.stringify({ evidence: 'local_production_shadow_intake_with_simulated_broker', results }, null, 2) + '\n');
+  console.log(`srw86-shadow: ${JSON.stringify(results.map(({ replies, recordPath, ...row }) => row))}`);
+}

+if (require.main === module) runProof(process.argv[2]).catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode = 1; });

+
+`SignalSourceDedupe.tla` models the source gate before the shared THALA reader
+and the durable reservation before broker enqueue. It explores Telegram,
+Discord, both, and both shadow primaries; exact text, normalized formatting,
+price, quantity, and contract variations; both message arrival orders; and a
+readable or unreadable reservation ledger. `CrossPostTiming` has three cases:
+`semanticWindow` means a timestamp difference up to 120 seconds, `lateGuard`
+means over 120 seconds through five minutes, and `independent` means over five
+minutes under the current default settings. The model does not vary the optional
+`maxAgeMs` setting. Exact or normalized format matches in the first two cases
+trade at most once in `both` mode. Changed price, quantity, or strike variants
+in either guarded case block the second platform as ambiguous. Independent posts can both
+trade only when both sources were eligible to trade and the ledger and Discord
+scope guard are valid. The negative control with an unbounded guard holds an
+independent post and must violate `IndependentCrossPostCanTrade`.

+reservation ledger blocks all eligible trades when the service supplies the

+The report includes daily rates by channel and category, unresolved coverage, examples and repeat alerts. Rates use reviewed rows as their denominator. An unclear row cannot make the measured error rate look smaller. Discord channel identity must come from recorded origin metadata; a guru name is not a Discord channel.
+
+Dollar amounts in reviewed `size_pick` evidence are compared with the parsed amount and unit. USD, dollars and dollar signs share one currency unit; contracts remain a separate unit. An exact $1,000 instruction parsed as $500 or 1,000 contracts counts as wrong size. Bare numbers, monetary bounds and unquantifiable hints remain unclear unless independent size semantics cover them. Linked later size corrections use the same decoder, so three confirmed dollar-size errors raise the existing repeat alert. The rolling veto checks parsed dollar commands as well as classifier field picks.
+
+Underlying entry conditions are compared as predicates, with separate lower and upper bounds and inclusive or strict edges. An above-$150 condition cannot match an under-$150 command, even when an option premium or scalar trigger has the same number. Premium evidence and underlying guards are checked independently. Missing, conflicting or malformed predicates produce an unclear field mismatch rather than correct. The nightly veto checks parsed command predicates as well as classifier picks and holds promotion when that comparison is unclear.
+
+The ledger supports correct, wrong contract, wrong side, wrong size, missed call, false call and unclear labels. A definite mismatch can establish an error even when some other fields remain unknown. Calling a row correct requires complete evidence. A policy or execution refusal does not itself establish a parser miss. Source size and the bot's risk sizing are separate facts.
+
+Later human posts can confirm fields only through a recorded reply relationship or a thread rooted at the original post. Sharing a broad Telegram topic is not enough. A matching ticker and a nearby timestamp alone are insufficient. Conflicting evidence remains unclear. Bot fills and bot replies show what happened after parsing; they cannot prove what the human intended. Intake now preserves Telegram reply and topic IDs, but older records cannot recover metadata that was discarded.
+
+The existing full source-review contract still governs training admission. The nightly learner prioritizes confirmed misreads that have complete reviewed labels, retains other cases for review, and preserves the frozen held-out separation. Partial ground truth is useful for the audit but cannot become an invented full classifier label.
+
+Before publishing a candidate, the learner applies an additional veto to the existing paired replay. The last 30 days of ledger evidence must have complete paired predictions, and measured category and channel error rates must fall or hold. Missing ground truth or replay coverage retains the current pack. Existing strict improvement, held-out inference, budget and safety gates still apply.
+
+Live evaluation reads the same confirmed-label store as the daily check, at `CLEF_PACK_ROOT/reviews/confirmed-labels.json` (or the explicit classifier-pack root supplied to intake). Existing broker-sync ticks and allowed intake detect changes in the day, retained source evidence or review content. Unchanged ticks reuse the audit result. Late reviews therefore trigger evaluation without requiring a new reply or topic post. Invalid stores or rejected source hashes are audited and their labels are not trusted; paper processing continues.
+
+A class repeated three times in one New York day produces an operator alert with examples through the existing receipt queue. Alerts go to configured owner chats and do not stop trading. Receipt phases suppress duplicate alerts after restart. The daily report and nightly summary also retain alert payloads; without configured owner chats, delivery requires operator configuration through the existing approved configuration process.
+
+The deterministic nightly gate verifier covers the original paired replay predicate. The ledger and rolling veto also need source-record integration evidence because that predicate does not prove human authorship, thread matching or ground-truth accuracy. A successful local replay proves local behavior only. Deployment and paper broker outcomes require their own evidence.
+
+For explicitly marked Discord samples, `readDiscordSampleCard` in the existing provider parser reads message content plus embed title and description. It exposes intended contract, side, source size hint and entry or exit trigger for an offline audit, while returning `executionEligible: false` and no executable `command`. Connection checks produce no semantic command. Omitted size stays unspecified and a sell without expiry retains its stated contract scope; the adapter does not infer a quantity or expiry from nearby cards. This audit adapter covers the requested dimensions, not full stop and target execution.
+
+The existing posts and misread owners accept `discord_message_received` records with string message IDs and recorded channel metadata. Keep authenticated source snapshots and source-hashed manual reviews alongside the ledger. An offline sample replay can record its `semanticCommand` as an audit-only `command_parsed` event, but this does not prove live intake or broker execution. Store sample labels separately from live rates and active training evidence so their explicit no-trade notices cannot become actionable training instructions.

+'use strict';
+
+function buildPublicHealthPayload(state, telegramView = null, signalSource = null) {
+  const heartbeat = state.heartbeat;
+  const livenessOk = heartbeat !== 'halted' && heartbeat !== 'error' && heartbeat !== 'history_limit_reached';
+  const executionReady = heartbeat === 'running' || heartbeat === 'closed';
+  const telegramChannelFailed = telegramView?.channel?.status === 'error';
+  const discordRequired = signalSource && (['discord', 'both'].includes(signalSource.mode)
+    || (signalSource.mode === 'shadow' && signalSource.primary === 'discord'));
+  const discordFailed = discordRequired && signalSource.discord?.state !== 'ready';
+  const telegram = telegramView ? {
+    channelStatus: telegramView.channel?.status ?? null,
+    lastPollAt: telegramView.channel?.lastPollAt ?? null,
+    lastError: telegramView.channel?.lastError ?? null,
+  } : null;
+  const jevSnapshot = state.connections?.jev;
+  const jev = {
+    status: jevSnapshot?.status ?? null,
+    enabled: jevSnapshot?.enabled ?? null,
+    ...(jevSnapshot?.errorCode ? { errorCode: jevSnapshot.errorCode } : {}),
+  };
+  return {
+    ok: livenessOk && !telegramChannelFailed && !discordFailed,
+    ready: executionReady && !telegramChannelFailed && !discordFailed,
+    heartbeat,
+    marketSession: state.marketSession,
+    ...(telegram ? { telegram } : {}),
+    jev,
+    ...(signalSource ? { signalSource } : {}),
+  };
+}
+
+module.exports = { buildPublicHealthPayload };

+    createPosition(levels), basis(underlying), at, quote,

+  const underlyingStopWithoutPremium = allLevels.stop
+    ? trigger(allLevels, allLevels.stop.price - 1, null) : null;
+  const baselineUnderlying = allLevels.stop?.price ? allLevels.stop.price + 1 : 1_000;
+  const premiumStop = trigger(allLevels, baselineUnderlying, {
+    quality: 'fresh', bid: allLevels.premiumStop.price - 0.01,

bundles.title: Eval design for every repo, with DeepEval and Jev
bundles.description:
Shyam (2026-10-28): 'I think we're running in loops because our evals are not great. Help me understand this as well while we build it.' Research and design, change nothing; the result is a report plus an explainer page Shyam can read.

Read first:
- https://github.com/confident-ai/deepeval (current docs and code: metrics, G-Eval, DAG, experimental mode, the Jev integration and JevEval with Noul, Score and Choice questions, ConversationalJevEval, include_reason=False, score_breakdown, thresholds). Ideas and API only; check the licence before suggesting any code reuse.
- Shyam's pasted summary of DeepEval + Jev (TypeSafe AI's decision model: the LLM does extraction, Jev returns calibrated probabilities on bounded yes/no, degree and choice questions, a fixed equation makes the score, about USD 0.042 per million input tokens, output free, about 100 ms; experimental, no silent fallback). Note: the SRW bot already calls Jev (jev_connection.js, jev-1.14.0) for observations, so TypeSafe access may already exist; check how.
- https://x.com/tonycueva/status/2112933068524617770 and https://x.com/tonycueva/status/2115089591824744957 (if X blocks the default user agent, record that and move on; never impersonate a client).
- Our own evidence of looping: LMW-10's seven failed reviews on the same finding, SRW tasks sent back by reviews and rebases (SRW-73, SRW-77, SRW-61), reviews that flip between runs, proofs written by the same agent that wrote the code, the SRW release gate (functional, not outcome), LMW-12's knowledge-use experiments (small samples, no held-out sets), and today's live refusals that no gate caught (SRW-86). Board history: herdr-projects list --archived and details.

Deliver:
1. Plain-language explanation of why we loop: what our current checks measure versus what we need (code gates versus outcome evals, LLM-judge variance, missing fixed held-out sets, no per-rule hard gates, self-graded proof).
2. An eval design per project: SRW bot (parse accuracy per card type against ground truth from THALA's later posts, refusal rate, misread rate, fill and exit correctness, P&L versus THALA's stated results, Discord parity), the nightly learner (held-out accuracy, promotion gate), dbt and Omni (tie-out tests against Notion and source systems), mac-ops governor (safety and liveness under replayed load), the board and reviewers themselves (review agreement and flip rate, loop count per task), STS and the iOS apps (UI flows, crash-free runs), llmwiki (does knowledge get used and help). For each: the questions as Nouls, Scores and Choices where a judge is needed, the deterministic checks where it is not, hard rules as their own metrics, the fixed dataset and where it comes from, the threshold, cost per run and where it gates (task, review, merge, deploy, nightly).
3. Where DeepEval and Jev fit and where they do not (deterministic checks first; Jev only for bounded judgments), with cost estimates.
4. A rollout order: the first three evals to build, each with its definition of done, starting with SRW.
Publish the explainer as a private page (Artifact) with diagrams where they help, and save the report.

bundles.head: 9c4bbdb1e24723210f737d639974679695ba3176
bundles.title: Make the SRW release gate fast and run it once per commit
bundles.description:
Verification is the SRW bottleneck (Shyam, 2026-10-28: 'why is verification taking so long'). Facts from 2026-10-27/28: one full run of test_srw16_release_gate.js took 1303 s (about 22 min) on SRW-68; each task runs it several times (the agent's own run, the board check, again after every review round, again after every rebase when another task merges, and again in the deploy task); heavy runs 2 to 4 jobs at a time, and today it curtailed SRW jobs 15 times and paused them 9 times on load.

Goal: a task's gate costs minutes, not an hour, without weakening what it checks.
1. Profile the gate: time per step (index-lotto, copy-trading, real-corpus, reject-all, feature gate, and the rest) over three runs; find what dominates and why (serial replay, repeated setup, cold dependency installs, sleeps or polling).
2. Speed it up: parallelise independent steps inside one heavy admission within the CPU budget heavy grants, reuse setup, and keep the full real-post corpus replay. Consider 5 variations and pick by measured time.
3. Run once per commit: write a gate receipt keyed by the commit SHA (and Node version and lockfile hash); the board check, the reviewer and the deploy automation reuse a passing receipt for the same SHA instead of rerunning. Any change to the commit means a new run.
4. Keep every existing assertion; a deliberately broken commit must still fail.
Proof: before and after timings for each step and in total (target: total under 8 minutes on this Mac under heavy), a negative control that still fails, the board check reusing a receipt for an unchanged SHA, and the gate passing through ~/.local/bin/heavy. This task is the only one allowed to change test_srw16_release_gate.js and its runner; other tasks keep running it unchanged.

bundles.head: aa513dd054c1b8c0c6968de456b2e6afaa6b0bbf
bundles.title: Misread tracking and learning loop for THALA parses
bundles.description:
With timed-only mode off (2026-10-28), the paper bot acts on loosely written human-desk posts. Misreads are acceptable on paper, but they must be measured and driven down.

Build on the existing owners: the SRW-55 nightly classifier learning loop (clef_nightly_learning.js, clef_nightly_labeller.js, clef_nightly_replay.js) and the posts audit the daily check produces. No parallel pipeline.

1. Misread ledger: for every post the bot acted on or refused, record what it parsed (symbol, contract, side, size, trigger) and the ground truth, taken from THALA's later posts in the same thread (fills, trims, 'I bought', corrections), the actual contract traded, and the Telegram/Discord reply history. Classify each as correct, wrong contract, wrong side, wrong size, missed call, false call, or unclear.
2. Daily misread rate per category and per channel (Telegram, each Discord alert channel), with the worst examples, in the daily check report.
3. Learning: confirmed misreads become labelled examples for the nightly loop, and the nightly replay must show the rate falling or holding on the last 30 days before any parser change is promoted (the loop's existing promotion gate).
4. Guard: a misread class that repeats three times in a day raises an operator alert with the examples, without stopping trading.

Check 4 theories when a misread class appears, and consider 5 variations for the ground-truth matching rule. Proof: run the ledger on the stored posts since 2026-10-20 and today's live posts, show the per-category rate and 10 labelled examples, and show one nightly replay using them. Paper only; never print secrets; use heavy for heavy commands.

bundles.description_excerpt:
With timed-only mode off (2026-10-28), the paper bot acts on loosely written human-desk posts. Misreads are acceptable on paper, but they must be measured and driven down.

Build on the existing owners: the SRW-55 nightly classifier learning loop (clef_nightly_learning.js, clef_nightly_labeller.js, clef_nightly_replay.js) and the posts audit the daily check produces. No parallel pipeline.

1. Misread ledger: for every post the bot acted on or refused, record what it parsed (symbol, contract, side, size, trigger) and the ground truth, taken from THALA's later posts in the same thread (fills, trims, 'I bought', corrections), the actual contract traded, and the Telegram/Discord reply history. Classify each as correct, wrong contract, wrong side, wrong size, missed call, false call, or unclear.
2. Daily misread rate per category and per channel (Telegram, each Discord alert channel), with the worst examples, in the daily check report.
3. Learning: confirmed misreads become labelled examples for the nightly loop, and the nightly replay must show the rate falling or holding on the last 30 days before any parser change is promoted (the loop's existing promotion gate).
4. Guard: a misread class that repeats three times in a day raises an operator alert with the examples, without stopping trading.

Check 4 theories when a misread class appears, and consider 5 variations for the ground-truth matching rule. Proof: run the ledger on the stored posts since 2026-10-20 and today's live posts, show the per-category rate and 10 labelled examples, and show one nightly replay using them. Paper only; never print secrets; use heavy for heavy commands.

+---
+name: verify-index-lotto-context
+description: Verify native Human desk index-lotto execution, listed weekly contracts, source links, restart continuity and clarification stopword handling.
+---
+
+# Verify index-lotto context
+
+Use after changing `providerIndexLottoContext` or `parseProviderAlert` in `telegram_provider_parser.js`, refusal persistence or cards in `telegram_alerts.js`, persistent fill source state in `alpaca_paper_execution.js`, or contract hints in `telegram_clarifying_questions.js`.
+
+## Property and bounds
+
+An unconditional native lotto must use a verified broker-listed contract and the existing tiny-size allocator, without a categorical instrument denial. A linked update must retain its strike, option right, expiry and original same-owner source while its exact option position remains open and unexpired, including after a quiet period or restart. Recent-post inference without a held source remains bounded to ten minutes. A clarification card must never display a checked stopword as a ticker in its question or heading. Explicit lowercase contract answers must remain valid. A failure could send the wrong contract to the executor or mislead the human about a position that does not exist.
+
+JavaScript has no code-level verifier configured here. Use the actual intake and generated bounded inputs rather than claiming a proof over a hand model. The integration proof covers the nine source-anchored October 27 posts in `fixtures/srw_release_gate_expected.json`, watch-only ON/OFF, and restart before the stop updates. Four additional scenarios move the exact 75% sale and its receipt eleven or sixty minutes after entry, both uninterrupted and across restart. Held-source controls reject closed, foreign, future, expired, mismatched and conflicting candidates. Generated question inputs cover the enumerated pronouns and quantifiers, upper/lower case, text/selected evidence and unbacked prose. Positive controls retain uppercase and cashtag contract hints. The state chart is in `docs/state-charts/index-lotto-refusal.md`.
+
+## Run
+
+Use Node 22 or later and existing dependencies only. Keep generated output outside the repo. No credentials, live endpoints, Telegram poller or new unit-test files are required.
+
+```sh
+heavy node scripts/srw59_index_lotto_replay.cjs "$TMPDIR/index-lotto-proof"
+heavy node test_srw16_release_gate.js
+```
+
+Run sequentially. Inspect `proof.json`, not only the exit code. Every one of the four scenarios must show the nine posts with linked cards, contexts anchored to post #841 and zero model calls. The listed SPXW 7650 put entry must fill with the existing 0.1 wording weight. The exact 75 percent sale executes only when the conditional switch allows it. Unresolved management plans must not claim an applied position change. Each delayed-sale scenario must sell 29 of 39 and retain 10, with SPX 7650P 0DTE and original source #841 in its cards. Inspect the persisted position source before the sale, not only the recent-message context.
+
+## Independent review admission
+
+Inspect the pinned diff and saved evidence before queuing the release gate. Bounded local file reads (`git diff`, targeted `rg`/`sed`, small JSON receipts and saved screenshots) are lightweight inspection, not a build or replay; they do not require heavy under the task's resource safeguard. Keep them separate from the heavy test payload. A stricter human review instruction still takes precedence.
+
+Check the closing note against the pinned revision, all four incident theories, the nine exact source posts, before/after orders and cards, source linkage after quiet periods/restart, the five-approach page and the gate receipt. Verify saved artifact hashes and inspect the final screenshots; a filename or a passing summary alone is insufficient. Record which inspection actually executed even when a later test cannot obtain admission. Keep canceled admission, observed test failure, completed inspection and independent approval distinct.
+
+When the installed Mac Ops governor advertises review priority in its help, independent reviewers run:
+
+    ~/.local/bin/heavy --review node test_srw16_release_gate.js
+
+Workers continue to use ordinary admission. Review priority changes queue order; it does not bypass host health, controller capacity or a legacy-drain hold. Confirm the effective task review timeout before starting: admission waiting can consume its wall-clock budget. Do not raise the timeout or shared resource limits automatically.
+
+If status reports a legacy drain, do not remove its shared marker. An empty legacy census alone does not clear that hold. Ask the Mac Ops owner to complete the cutover and report the task blocked if owner clearance is needed. A queued or interrupted command is not a passing check; preserve the last verified source sync until a new run completes.
+
+## Failure handling and sync
+
+If the script fails, trace the exact original post through intake, record and card. Do not weaken the expectation, substitute an unverified expiry, or enable simulated index execution. Distinguish changed code behavior from stale verification. Preserve stdout and receipts in the task report folder.
+
+Original source baseline: `5b16e534593be3179148eb30054d2c5cb139f6ac`. Shyam explicitly superseded the refusal-only promise in SRW-59 by removing categorical instrument blocks; the revised promise is exact broker-listed execution with existing price/account checks. Verified source sync: `5ac1aeba0655fe3261a81320baecf5f7a744ab6d` on October 27, 2026, rebased onto main `8ecf894`. The exact-post proof passed all four original scenarios and four delayed-sale scenarios, 240 prose controls in both question and full-card rendering, positive lowercase-answer controls, 82 identity controls and 56 held-source controls. The release gate and existing clarification/refusal suite passed through `heavy`. Scratch mutations removing stopword filtering, same-owner validation, held-source lookup or bound coverage receipts were detected. The original nine-post pass omitted the quiet-period and quantifier bugs; these bounds extend the unchanged ownership and correct-contract promise. Native commands use the shared source/coverage/receipt path. After later edits, compare covered code with this sync commit before moving the sync point. A bounded pass is not a general formal proof or deployment proof.

+# Index lotto calls on the paper path
+
+A THALA Human desk lotto declaration can identify a current entry without an explicit buy verb. The native parser recognizes the bounded unconditional declaration, including TODAY expiry, the quoted premium and tiny size. It uses the existing provider buy, sizing, quote and paper-order owners. The stale SPX/SPXW instrument denial has been removed.
+
+Alpaca supports index options through its existing contracts and orders APIs. Query the SPX underlier for the actual listed contracts; SPXW weekly symbols sit under SPX. The resolver validates the listed symbol, strike, option right, expiry, active status and tradability. For same-day SPX it prefers a listed SPXW weekly. It never replaces SPX with an ETF. See [Alpaca index options](https://docs.alpaca.markets/us/docs/index-options) and the [Trading API release](https://alpaca.markets/blog/alpaca-launches-index-options-via-trading-api/).
+
+## Sizing and execution
+
+The parser retains the existing `lottos_zero` hint with `Size: tiny`. The existing allocator applies a 0.1 wording weight. Quotes, liquidity, cash, exposure and account permission checks still apply. Removing a categorical instrument block does not invent a listing, quote or broker approval.
+
+The unconditional declaration's descriptive risk paragraph is not an entry predicate. A strict recognition check excludes it from conditional watch-only classification. Extra instructions or a genuine price/time entry condition do not get that exception. The switch continues to govern conditional calls. Native lotto commands use the same source validation, full-text coverage check and bound coverage receipt as other provider commands. A prohibitory symbol or extra unsupported instruction cannot gain an exception through native recognition.
+
+## Following updates
+
+Targets, stop moves, commentary and partial sells retain a contract context and link to the original provider entry. Recent-post inference requires the same provider, chat, human desk, New York day, strike and option right, with a prior context no older than ten minutes. A filled position also persists its validated original source, provider, chat and source timestamp. While that exact option position remains open and unexpired, later matching updates can use that source beyond ten minutes, including after restart. Closed, conflicting, foreign-owner or mismatched holdings cannot donate it. Multiple source anchors remain ambiguous.
+
+The explicit 75% partial sale uses the existing matching exit and whole-contract rounding. It remains subject to the current conditional watch-only switch when the full post also contains conditional exit wording. Posts with unspecified `holds there` timing, unquantified later sales or future targets are recorded as linked plan updates. Their cards say that no position change was applied. The bot does not invent a holding period, remaining quantity or executable stop trigger.
+
+A source reference identifies the provider call. A filled paper position requires a separate broker receipt. The clarification helper rejects pronouns, command words and prose quantifiers such as `my`, `our`, `more`, `many` and `most` as ticker hints, both from text and selected extraction fields. A text hint must use an uppercase ticker or explicit cashtag. The card heading uses that same validated hint. Lowercase contract answers remain valid when answering a specific contract question. An extracted ticker must also occur explicitly in the source text; unbacked extraction cannot name a contract in a question.
+
+## Verification
+
+```sh
+heavy node scripts/srw59_index_lotto_replay.cjs "$TMPDIR/index-lotto-proof"
+heavy node test_srw16_release_gate.js
+```
+
+Run sequentially. The integration proof uses nine source-anchored October 27 posts, actual parser/intake/broker owners, and simulated Telegram/Alpaca transports. It compares watch-only ON/OFF and restart continuity, checks the listed weekly contract and tiny weighting, and checks bounded source-identity and stopword inputs. Four additional cases delay the explicit sale by eleven or sixty minutes, with and without restart, and pin the sale at 29 of 39 contracts. Negative held-source controls reject zero quantity, foreign ownership, expiry/identity mismatches, future timestamps and conflicting source anchors. This establishes local behavior, not a deployed fill.
+
+Alpaca's option quote feed and underlying-index level feed are different capabilities. The current index-options documentation says index-level spot data is not supplied at launch. Underlying-dependent rules therefore still need a verified source for that index level; missing data must be visible in the receipt.
+
+See the [state chart](state-charts/index-lotto-refusal.md) and [verification skill](../.agents/skills/verify-index-lotto-context/SKILL.md). Runtime output belongs outside the repo.

+# Human desk index-lotto execution lifecycle
+
+```mermaid
+stateDiagram-v2
+  [*] --> Received
+  Received --> AdmissionRefused: source, chat, age or duplicate check fails
+  Received --> LottoContext: admitted Human desk index lotto
+  Received --> ExistingParser: other post
+  LottoContext --> Conflict: multiple or conflicting contracts
+  LottoContext --> NativeEntry: strict unconditional declaration and explicit expiry
+  LottoContext --> NativePartialExit: exact 75 percent sale and bounded expiry
+  LottoContext --> LinkedPlan: commentary or unresolved conditional management
+  NativeEntry --> SourceCoverage
+  NativePartialExit --> SourceCoverage
+  SourceCoverage --> ListedContract: complete entry source and bound receipt
+  SourceCoverage --> RefusedWithReason: prohibitory symbol or unconsumed instruction
+  ListedContract --> ExecutionChecks: fresh option quote, liquidity, size and account
+  ListedContract --> RefusedWithReason: listing unavailable or missing
+  ExecutionChecks --> PaperOrder: all checks pass
+  ExecutionChecks --> RefusedWithReason: check fails
+  SourceCoverage --> WatchOnly: partial sale with conditional switch applied to full post
+  SourceCoverage --> MatchingPosition: partial sale not held by switch
+  MatchingPosition --> PaperOrder: same desk and exact option identity
+  MatchingPosition --> RefusedWithReason: no owned position or ambiguous identity
+  LinkedPlan --> UpdateCard: source linked, no position mutation claimed
+  PaperOrder --> FillOrBrokerRefusal
+  FillOrBrokerRefusal --> DurablePositionSource: buy fills with validated source
+  DurablePositionSource --> LottoContext: later update while exact owned option remains open and unexpired
+  FillOrBrokerRefusal --> ExecutorCard
+  WatchOnly --> ExecutorCard
+  RefusedWithReason --> ExecutorCard
+  ExecutorCard --> RecordedContext
+  UpdateCard --> RecordedContext
+  RecordedContext --> RestoredContext: journal replay after restart
+  RestoredContext --> LottoContext: later matching update
+```
+
+There is no categorical SPX/SPXW denial. A paper order still requires a verified listing and successful execution checks. Symbol resolution uses broker metadata and retains the posted strike, right and expiry. Recent-post inference keeps its same-owner, same-chat, same-day and ten-minute bounds. A filled position persists its original source and can supply it after a longer quiet period or restart, under exact provider/chat/owner/option checks until the position closes or expires. Conflicting anchors cannot execute an exit.
+
+A clarification discards prose quantifiers and checked stopword tickers before rendering, requires uppercase or cashtag text hints, and checks extracted tickers against the source text. Native linked plan updates do not ask whether a pronoun is a new entry.
+

+# THALA parse misreads
+
+The existing daily posts audit and SRW-55 nightly learner share a misread ledger. The ledger records the bot's interpretation, execution evidence and independent ground truth separately. It does not submit orders or change paper trading controls.
+
+Run the existing report against a private record file:
+
+```sh
+heavy node scripts/thala_posts_report.cjs /private/record.jsonl 2026-10-27
+```
+
+Pass a third argument containing the existing confirmed-label store to include reviewed labels, or use the configured `CLEF_PACK_ROOT` review store. Each review is checked against its original source text.
+
+The report includes daily rates by channel and category, unresolved coverage, examples and repeat alerts. Rates use reviewed rows as their denominator. An unclear row cannot make the measured error rate look smaller. Discord channel identity must come from recorded origin metadata; a guru name is not a Discord channel.
+
+Dollar amounts in reviewed `size_pick` evidence are compared with the parsed amount and unit. USD, dollars and dollar signs share one currency unit; contracts remain a separate unit. An exact $1,000 instruction parsed as $500 or 1,000 contracts counts as wrong size. Bare numbers, monetary bounds and unquantifiable hints remain unclear unless independent size semantics cover them. Linked later size corrections use the same decoder, so three confirmed dollar-size errors raise the existing repeat alert. The rolling veto checks parsed dollar commands as well as classifier field picks.
+
+The ledger supports correct, wrong contract, wrong side, wrong size, missed call, false call and unclear labels. A definite mismatch can establish an error even when some other fields remain unknown. Calling a row correct requires complete evidence. A policy or execution refusal does not itself establish a parser miss. Source size and the bot's risk sizing are separate facts.
+
+Later human posts can confirm fields only through a recorded reply relationship or a thread rooted at the original post. Sharing a broad Telegram topic is not enough. A matching ticker and a nearby timestamp alone are insufficient. Conflicting evidence remains unclear. Bot fills and bot replies show what happened after parsing; they cannot prove what the human intended. Intake now preserves Telegram reply and topic IDs, but older records cannot recover metadata that was discarded.
+
+The existing full source-review contract still governs training admission. The nightly learner prioritizes confirmed misreads that have complete reviewed labels, retains other cases for review, and preserves the frozen held-out separation. Partial ground truth is useful for the audit but cannot become an invented full classifier label.
+
+Before publishing a candidate, the learner applies an additional veto to the existing paired replay. The last 30 days of ledger evidence must have complete paired predictions, and measured category and channel error rates must fall or hold. Missing ground truth or replay coverage retains the current pack. Existing strict improvement, held-out inference, budget and safety gates still apply.
+
+A class repeated three times in one New York day produces an operator alert with examples through the existing receipt queue. Alerts go to configured owner chats and do not stop trading. Receipt phases suppress duplicate alerts after restart. The daily report and nightly summary also retain alert payloads; without configured owner chats, delivery requires operator configuration through the existing approved configuration process.
+
+The deterministic nightly gate verifier covers the original paired replay predicate. The ledger and rolling veto also need source-record integration evidence because that predicate does not prove human authorship, thread matching or ground-truth accuracy. A successful local replay proves local behavior only. Deployment and paper broker outcomes require their own evidence.
+
+For explicitly marked Discord samples, `readDiscordSampleCard` in the existing provider parser reads message content plus embed title and description. It exposes intended contract, side, source size hint and entry or exit trigger for an offline audit, while returning `executionEligible: false` and no executable `command`. Connection checks produce no semantic command. Omitted size stays unspecified and a sell without expiry retains its stated contract scope; the adapter does not infer a quantity or expiry from nearby cards. This audit adapter covers the requested dimensions, not full stop and target execution.
+
+The existing posts and misread owners accept `discord_message_received` records with string message IDs and recorded channel metadata. Keep authenticated source snapshots and source-hashed manual reviews alongside the ledger. An offline sample replay can record its `semanticCommand` as an audit-only `command_parsed` event, but this does not prove live intake or broker execution. Store sample labels separately from live rates and active training evidence so their explicit no-trade notices cannot become actionable training instructions.

review_summary:
The saved receipts address the earlier dollar-size and candidate-identity findings, and support a passing local release gate. Trigger comparison can still report a reversed condition as correct, and live repeat alerts omit the reviewed labels used by the daily report. Full historical accuracy and per-Discord-channel results remain unavailable from the retained source metadata.

finding F3 (major): The ledger can classify an opposite underlying trigger direction as correct because it compares only the numeric threshold.
where: thala_misread_ledger.js:157-168,409-412,501-508
proof: Source inspection shows minPrice and maxPrice are projected into the same scalar trigger.value, while expectedTrigger selects guard_pick and classify compares only their numbers. The reviewed guard_operator and parsed guard direction/inclusivity are never compared. An otherwise matching reviewed above-150 instruction and under-150 command therefore pass this comparison and can reach correct; premium-first projection can also hide underlying guard differences. A focused heavy --review actual-ledger observation was queued at position 2, reported global-slots-busy, and was canceled with exit 130 

finding F4 (major): The live repeat-alert path does not consume confirmed source reviews, so reviewed misreads can reach three without an operator alert.
where: telegram_alerts.js:3888-3891,3926-3928; scripts/thala_posts_report.cjs:59-68
proof: The live alert function builds its ledger with only since/until, leaving reviews at the default empty object, and runs only after an incoming reply/topic post. The daily report explicitly loads and passes the existing confirmed-label store. Three errors established by those reviews, without independent later human confirmations, can therefore appear in the daily ledger while the live ledger remains unconfirmed and queues no alert. The saved review-final-sizes.log proves the reviewed three-error aggregate, whereas operator-alert-proof.json exercises linked corrections only. Settle with an actua

- Inspected corrected size-comparison receipts: mismatching dollar amounts/units become wrong_size and three reviewed cases produce an aggregate alert.
- Inspected exact-current-candidate verification and source/report receipts: nine immutable sources, 18 successful fresh responses, matching candidate identity, preserved budget reservations, KEEP outcome and incomplete rolling evidence.
- Inspected actual-intake illustrative alert receipt: threshold three, restart deduplication, journal integrity ok and zero submitted orders.

- Historical reply/thread IDs and original Discord channel identities are absent. The retained evidence does not establish complete ground truth, population accuracy or per-Discord-channel accuracy, and the rolling promotion veto remains incomplete.

bundles.description_excerpt:
With timed-only mode off (2026-10-28), the paper bot acts on loosely written human-desk posts. Misreads are acceptable on paper, but they must be measured and driven down.

Build on the existing owners: the SRW-55 nightly classifier learning loop (clef_nightly_learning.js, clef_nightly_labeller.js, clef_nightly_replay.js) and the posts audit the daily check produces. No parallel pipeline.

1. Misread ledger: for every post the bot acted on or refused, record what it parsed (symbol, contract, side, size, trigger) and the ground truth, taken from THALA's later posts in the same thread (fills, trims, 'I bought', corrections), the actual contract traded, and the Telegram/Discord reply history. Classify each as correct, wrong contract, wrong side, wrong size, missed call, false call, or unclear.
2. Daily misread rate per category and per channel (Telegram, each Discord alert channel), with the worst examples, in the daily check report.
3. Learning: confirmed misreads become labelled examples for the nightly loop, and the nightly replay must show the rate falling or holding on the last 30 days before any parser change is promoted (the loop's existing promotion gate).
4. Guard: a misread class that repeats three times in a day raises an operator alert with the examples, without stopping trading.

Check 4 theories when a misread class appears, and consider 5 variations for the ground-truth matching rule. Proof: run the ledger on the stored posts since 2026-10-20 and today's live posts, show the per-category rate and 10 labelled examples, and show one nightly replay using them. Paper only; never print secrets; use heavy for heavy commands.

bundles.head: c3bb86c131971315acf87a44437958584b9b7cd4
bundles.title: Measure whether wiki, prompts and nightly learning help
bundles.description:
Shyam: knowledge keeps piling up in the llm wiki, in his prompts and rules, and in nightly learning runs, but nobody knows whether it changes outcomes. Run experiments all the time to prove these are used and make work better, not an afterthought.

1. Usage: from real session logs (Claude Code transcripts under ~/.claude/projects, Codex sessions, herdr board task logs and closing notes), measure for the last 2 weeks which wiki pages, skills, rules (claude/rules/core.md, worker.instructions) and nightly learning outputs (SRW-13 labels, SRW-55 learning loop, wiki daily review) were actually loaded or read, how often, and by which tasks. List what is never used.
2. Effect: design and run real experiments, not opinions. For example, A/B pairs of the same small task run with and without a given skill or rule (two board attempts with attempts.by), comparing review rounds, review findings, time to merge, tokens and defects; before/after comparisons for rules added this month (for example the fail-closed rule, the heavy rule, the plan-approval rule); and whether the nightly learning changed the bot classifier results on held-out posts. State each hypothesis and pass criterion before running.
3. Report with numbers: what helps (keep and promote), what is unused or does not help (propose to merge, shorten or remove, with Shyam deciding deletions), and what is used but wrong. Include a small dashboard page (Artifact or local HTML) Shyam can open.
4. Make it continuous: add a weekly board automation in llmwiki ("Knowledge use experiments", every Monday 09:00) that reruns the usage measurement and one new experiment each week, and add a short note to the wiki explanation section on how this measurement works.
Guardrails: one heavy command at a time through heavy; do not delete wiki pages, skills or rules yourself; never print secrets from logs.

+
+These charts describe first-party executable lifecycle owners found in the

+

+## Coverage boundary and exceptions
+
+The inventory includes executables that persist control or publication
+state, gate later actions, retry provider work, poll until a terminal result,
+supervise a repeating service, or run an ordered batch sync. A script that
+only adapts one hook event, formats output, or performs a one-shot transform
+without a retry, gate, sync, or publication step is not a lifecycle machine
+under that rule.
+
+| Exception | Why it is not a charted lifecycle machine |
+|---|---|
+| Named worker wrappers such as `direct-codex-worker.sh`, `codex-worker.sh`, `luna-worker.sh`, `terra-worker.sh`, and provider launchers | They select arguments and hand off to the charted supervisor or provider request owner; they do not retain a second lifecycle. |
+| Other one-shot hooks in `claude/hooks/` and `claude/hooks/src/` | They inspect or adapt one event and return. Persistent owners among them are charted above. |
+| `claude/hooks/src/compiler-in-the-loop-stop.ts`, legacy continuity scripts, and `claude/hooks/auto-handoff-stop.py` | Not registered by the current `claude/settings.json`; the active v4.7 stop gate is charted. |
+| `claude/scripts/synthteam-persona-refresh.sh` | Operates on the separate Synthteam home and skill tree; outside the llmwiki-owned lifecycle boundary. |
+| One-shot CLI smoke/verification scripts | Verification procedures rather than production lifecycle owners. |
+| `runtime/tla/examples/`, `runtime/codex/skills/looper/examples/`, `runtime/codex/skills/statechart/scripts/test/`, and `archive/` | Examples, tests, and archived code are not active first-party runtime owners. |
+| Vendored, generated, cached, or third-party code | Excluded as non-owned source. Looper's checked-in template is charted; generated copies can drift and must be compared with it. |
+
+The active Claude hook registry uses `~/dotfiles` paths as aliases to the
+canonical llmwiki checkout; those handlers are included above. The following
+active handlers are deliberately listed as exceptions because they make one
+event-level decision and do not retain a lifecycle state:
+
+| Active handler | Why it is not a charted lifecycle machine |
+|---|---|
+| [`ttsr.py`](../../claude/hooks/ttsr.py#L16) | Reads prompt triggers and injects matching rules; it does not write state or retry. |
+| [`plankton-protect-symlink-targets.sh`](../../claude/hooks/plankton-protect-symlink-targets.sh#L1) | Resolves each requested path and allows or blocks that edit without a checkpoint. |
+| [`session-outcome.ts`](../../claude/hooks/src/session-outcome.ts#L21) | Reads the latest handoff and prints an outcome instruction; the user-run `artifact_mark.py` command performs any later update. |
+| Other registered one-event classifiers and validators | Inspect the current hook payload and return a decision without a later transition or durable control state. |

+the Stop hook's read of its temporary context-percentage file is charted, but

+[`claude/rules/core.md`](../../claude/rules/core.md#L25) retires those commands.
+Codex Fusion owners remain active and are charted above.
+
+## Registered owner without tracked implementation
+
+`claude/settings.json` registers
+[`subagent-stop-continuity.sh`](../../claude/hooks/subagent-stop-continuity.sh).
+The wrapper changes directory to `~/.claude/hooks` and invokes
+`dist/subagent-stop-continuity.mjs`. That implementation and a corresponding
+source file are not tracked in this worktree, so its intended ledger/cache
+lifecycle cannot be charted from repository code. The runtime target may be
+built or installed separately; the missing worktree file does not prove a
+live failure. Recover its source ownership on the next inventory pass.
