bundles.title: Refs #1813: the per-row cancel on a working entry (P45 dashboard)
bundles.description:
Refs #1813

The dashboard half of P45 (#1445): a per-row Cancel on a working entry, the
capability and the row's digest reaching the page, and the route gate that
re-checks the row before it is signed. The code is the re-cut of #1775 at
`431aeb22`, adapted to current main.

## What changed

**`scripts/b2b_dashboard_model.cjs`** — the bot's own `cancel_working_entries`
capability is projected instead of a hardcoded `false`, and each working order
row carries its `clientOrderId` and `cancelDigest`. Only an entry order carries
them, so an exit row can never be offered as cancellable.

**`scripts/b2b_dashboard_page.cjs`** — an Actions column and a per-row Cancel
button, offered only for an entry order the projection attributes to a trade,
with the bot's own digest, while the capability is on and the page's own
`controlState` gate is open. `askCancelEntry` opens a dialog naming the trade,
contract, order id, digest, status, filled and limit. `makeEntry` builds the
named payload. The capability allowlist admits the type.

**`scripts/b2b_dashboard_auth.cjs`** — the named payload fields, the
`control_disabled_by_dashboard` allowlist, and the row-at-digest gate:
`working_order_unknown`, `working_order_not_cancellable`, `working_order_stale`,
all before the command is signed. The gate re-reads the bot's own order
projection at signing time, past the cached snapshot the page rendered, so a row
that moved after the render is refused before it is signed, and a read the route
cannot make refuses as `working_order_unverified`.

**`scripts/b2b_dashboard_read.cjs`** — the fresh working-order read the gate
uses. It reads `/internal/thala-control/reads` with no cache and projects the
rows with the model's own `projectWorkingOrders`, and it is returned from
`createReader` so `createReadDashboard` can pass it to the control gate.

**The signed body now carries the named payload.** The source PR dropped it from
`coreBody`, so the coordinator read `payload = {}`, took the `perEntry` branch as
false, and refused `control_disabled` because the legacy cancel-all is off. The
operator-facing cancel could never have run. Acceptance 3 could not hold without
this one-line branch.

## Proof

```
node --experimental-sqlite scripts/srw1445_dashboard_cancel_proof.cjs
SRW-1445 dashboard cancel proof passed (91 checks)
```

Dependency-free and offline: a DOM-free page shim that evaluates the renderer's
own source, and a credential-free fake coordinator that verifies the signature
and validates the body with the contract's own `validateCommand`. It covers the
model binding, the button on an entry and never on an exit, the capability-off
and control-not-ready and controls-off and stale-heartbeat button states, the
dialog naming the order and the digest, the command body, the route's nine
refusals plus the admitted command's signed payload, and the real dashboard
wiring through `createReadDashboard` for a moved row and for a reader with no
fresh read.

Red signature, with the three files reverted to `6b3f46a8`:

```
AssertionError: the model passes the bot's own cancel_working_entries capability through
```

## Self-review

Reviewer: `astra-sub` / `gpt-6.2-astra` (`python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review risky` → `astra-sub gpt-6.2-astra`), on `243279ca`. Verdict FAIL with three majors and one minor. All four are fixed in `ce9ec015`:

- **Major — the dialog showed the order id but not the digest.** Acceptance 3 says the dialog names the exact order *and digest*. The proof was checking `cancelAuth.expectedDigest`, an internal field the operator never sees. Fixed: the dialog now carries a `Digest` fact, and the proof asserts the rendered fact, not the internal field.
- **Major — the button enabled on `bot.controlReady` alone.** A session with controls off, a stale control heartbeat or a delivery in flight would show an enabled button that silently did nothing when `openDialog` applied `controlState`. Fixed: the button uses the page's own `controlState(bot,false)`, the same gate the dialog applies. The proof now drives controls-off and stale-heartbeat and asserts the button is disabled with the reason.
- **Major — the route gate can accept a digest from the cached snapshot.** The route read the same 10 s cached control snapshot the page rendered, so a row that moved inside that window could still be signed. The first attempt only documented the cache bound; the gate rejected that, and the route now re-reads the bot's own order projection at signing time. See `Gate round two`.
- **Minor — the panel still said "Read only" beside a control.** Fixed: the line now reads "Cached signed control reads · the dashboard never polls the broker · Cancel acts on one named entry only". The `srw1444` panel proof still passes.

## Left for later

- `scripts/srw725_dashboard_proof.cjs:275`, `scripts/srw727_dashboard_contract_proof.cjs:86` and `scripts/srw733_control_boundary_proof.cjs:57` assert `cancel_working_entries` is refused as `control_disabled_by_dashboard`. This ticket deliberately admits the type, so those assertions are now stale and the proofs fail. I did not edit them: the rule is not to edit an existing check to make it pass. They need a follow-up that updates the expectation to the new policy. `srw733` also already fails on the clean base with a `vm` parse error, and `srw1392` and `srw1440` already fail on the clean base for unrelated reasons.
- `scripts/srw_review_scope.cjs` returns `review: opus` for the three dashboard files (`unknown-executable`). That is the coordinator's call, not a builder fallback.
- The proof names no immutable builder-tested SHA; `evidence/SRW-1813/check-proof.md` is committed with the code it describes, so the head that carries it is the head the publisher checks.
- The runtime diff is four files and 101 changed lines, above the ticket's three-file, roughly 51-line stop condition. The fourth file is the reader that serves the pre-sign freshness check.
- Device, handset and live-service testing is waived by the owner (Shyam 2026-11-14: "no testing is needed lets just finish backlog building everything"). No device or live case was run, and none is reported as failed.

## Gate round two

The gate on `ce9ec015` returned FAIL with one unresolved major. It is closed on
`0f1f9286`.

**Major — the route checked the same cached snapshot that supplied the dialog.**
A fill that landed between the render and the confirmation left the cached row
at the digest the operator saw while the bot's own row had already moved, so the
route could sign the old digest. The executor's later refusal limited the
impact, but the ticket requires refusal before signing. The route now re-reads
the bot's own order projection at signing time, past the cache, and refuses
`working_order_stale` when the row moved and `working_order_unverified` when the
read cannot be made. The proof supplies a digest that already differs from the
cached row and covers both cases.

**A wiring defect found while closing it.** The first attempt defined
`freshWorkingOrders` inside `createReader` but used it inside
`createReadDashboard`, where it is not in scope. Every control request threw a
`ReferenceError` and the dashboard answered 503 on `/login`. The read is now
returned from `createReader` and passed through as `reader.freshWorkingOrders`,
with a guard so a reader that does not expose it refuses the cancel as
`working_order_unverified`. The proof now builds the real dashboard through
`createReadDashboard` and asserts both refusals, so the wiring cannot regress
silently.

Non-vacuity, both guards:

| Guard | Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the fresh read | revert the route to the cached snapshot | red: `a row that moved after the render refuses the cancel` |
| the wiring | pass `freshWorkingOrders` directly instead of through the reader | red: `the real dashboard signs the operator in with a moved row` |

`evidence/SRW-1813/check-proof.md` records the checked head, the commands and
the findings closed.

## Gate round three

The gate on `ef1c0fa3` returned FAIL with one unresolved major: the fresh read
returned the rows and discarded the projection's freshness status.

**Major — a 200 is not freshness.** A bot whose heartbeat lapsed still answers
`/internal/thala-control/reads` with HTTP 200 and the last projection it built.
That projection carries the row the operator confirmed at the same digest, so
the route could sign a cancel against a book the bot had stopped reporting.
`freshWorkingOrders` now requires `projected.status === 'fresh'` and returns
`null` otherwise, which the route already refuses as `working_order_unverified`
before signing. The prior wiring proof injected the reader's result, so it could
not see this; the proof now drives the real `createReader` with a fake transport
and covers a fresh projection, a lapsed heartbeat, an unknown heartbeat and a
missing heartbeat.

Non-vacuity, all three guards:

| Guard | Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the fresh read | revert the route to the cached snapshot | red: `a row that moved after the render refuses the cancel` |
| the wiring | pass `freshWorkingOrders` directly instead of through the reader | red: `the real dashboard signs the operator in with a moved row` |
| the freshness gate | drop the `projected.status !== 'fresh'` guard | red: `a lapsed heartbeat returns no rows, so the cancel is refused` |

## Self-review, round three

Reviewer: `astra-sub` / `gpt-6.2-astra` (`python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review risky` → `astra-sub gpt-6.2-astra`), on `51c075aa`. No critical, major or minor findings. One nit: the proof comment said any heartbeat the producer does not call `fresh` becomes `unavailable`, while an explicit `stale` stays `stale`. Fixed in `ec7de51f`; both are refused the same way.

## Check

`Builder check: PASS ec7de51f606b115a889469f58eee94468476e4b8`

`scripts/check.sh` was not run: this repo's rule is that the Mac check publisher posts `srw/agent-check` on the ready PR. What I ran locally on this head: `node --check` on all four changed scripts and on `paper_service.js`, `discord_source.js`, `thala_v2_executor.js`; the proof above; and `srw1444_working_orders_panel_proof`, `srw1395_trim_buttons_proof`, `srw1409_stop_column_proof`, all passing. `node_modules` is absent in this worktree, so the proofs that load `paper_service.js` (`srw1445_coordinator_cancel_proof`, `srw1445_executor_fill_proof`, `srw1445_service_wiring_proof`, `srw1445_freeze_ownership_proof`, `srw1445_coordinator_recovery_proof`) cannot run here; they fail on `Cannot find module 'ws'` on the clean base too.

## Rollback

Revert the merge commit. The capability is off by default, so the button is not offered and the route refuses.

bundles.description:
Refs #1897

P45.6: the coordinator's recovery pass for a per-entry cancel, and the effective
admission a cancel-only service reports.

## What was already on main

`reconcileCancelEntry`, `reconcileCancelEntries`, the `drainNotices` call and the
`effective_admission_no_barrier` source tag landed with P45.4 (#2214) and P45.5
(#2218); the riding proof was green at 69 checks before this branch. What was
still missing is criterion 2's refusal and criterion 3's effective mode.

## Change (two code files, plus proof and evidence)

`thala_control_coordinator.cjs`

- `reconcileCancelEntry` refuses a per-entry cancel whose plan item never
  authorised transport (`pending`, `prepared_unsent`) once the command's deadline
  has passed: `cancel_expired_unsent`, `reconciled: true`, no broker write, no
  receipt, and the entry stays working. Before, such a row stayed unresolved
  forever, so `cancel_in_progress` refused every later cancel of that entry.
- The refusal releases only a freeze this command is the sole owner of. The
  executor keeps the owners of a shared freeze but releases on the single-owner
  projection, so releasing a shared one would clear another command's protection
  and let the entry be repriced. A shared freeze leaves the row unknown instead.
- The release is a take-then-release pair, so a save that fails mid-release is
  retried on the next pass rather than read as "nothing to release" and followed
  by failing the command past a durable freeze no process can release.
- `reads()` reports the effective pause mode when pause admission is disabled and
  hands that projection to the dashboard snapshot. A dormant stored `paused` row
  from an earlier deployment no longer reports entries not ready, nor trips the
  reader that refuses control while a healthy service claims to be paused. The
  stored row is untouched.

`scripts/srw1445_coordinator_recovery_proof.cjs` gains the criteria it did not
cover: expired refusal in its still-frozen, already-released and shared-freeze
shapes; the unexpired counterpart that must stay unknown; and the cancel-only
effective admission (projection, snapshot, entry readiness, and that the cancel
capability is admitted while pause is not).

## Gate round: the refused send marker (VERDICT: FAIL at `30a6a824`)

The gate kept one major open: if the executor's send marker fails to save after
the store has committed `send_started`, transport is refused, but recovery could
not tell that refusal from a DELETE that may be in flight. The item stayed
`send_started` with no durable reason, the freeze the command owned stayed in
place, and every later cancel of that entry was refused as already in progress.

The fix is the write order, not a new record:

- `thala_control_coordinator.cjs` (the cancel send boundary inside
  `reconcileKill`): the executor's send marker is now committed **before** the
  plan says `send_started`. `alpaca_paper_execution.js` issues no request once
  that callback throws, so a refused marker leaves the plan item
  `prepared_unsent` — the state recovery already reads as a proven pre-send
  refusal — and a crash between the two writes can no longer leave an ambiguous
  `send_started` behind. `send_started` now means exactly one thing: a DELETE may
  be in flight.
- `thala_control_coordinator.cjs` (`reconcileCancelEntry`): unchanged branch,
  re-documented against that invariant. It still refuses only on a proven
  pre-send state, still releases only a freeze this command solely owns, and
  still settles `cancel_expired_unsent` with no broker write and no receipt.
- `thala_v2_executor.js` (`unfreezeControlEntries`): a release also clears the
  send marker that command took for that entry. A marker left behind refuses
  every later snapshot for the trade (`snapshotKillEntries` throws on an uncertain
  send), so a release that cleared only the freeze would keep the entry
  unreachable through a different door. A marker another command took is never
  touched.
- `scripts/srw1445_coordinator_recovery_proof.cjs`: three new criteria, driven
  through the real coordinator, store, executor and fake broker, with the marker
  write failing for real (`save(true)` throwing) and the plan write failing for
  real, and restarts in the middle.
- `evidence/SRW-1897/check-proof.md` (new, was missing): the check record for this
  ticket, including every non-vacuity run and the self-review round.

## Proof

- `node --experimental-sqlite scripts/srw1445_coordinator_recovery_proof.cjs` →
  `SRW-1812 coordinator per-entry cancel recovery proof passed (150 checks)`
- Non-vacuity of the gate fix, each part removed in turn and the same proof re-run:
  `a refused marker leaves the plan provably unsent` fails when the marker write
  moves back after the plan write, and `the send marker the command owned is
  released with the freeze` fails when the marker deletion is removed from
  `unfreezeControlEntries`.
- Base red run, unchanged: `SRW_PROOF_BASE=9598d7e6 …` →
  `base 9598d7e6 red signature: control_prior_effect_quarantined`, reproduced.
- Also green on this head: `srw1445_coordinator_cancel`, `srw1445_coordinator_execute`,
  `srw1445_executor_fill`, `srw1445_executor_freeze`, `srw1445_freeze_ownership`,
  `srw1445_contract_digest`, `srw1445_store_receipt`, `srw1445_service_wiring`,
  `srw1445_dashboard_cancel`, `srw1785_cancel_recovery_flag_off`,
  `srw1526_cancel_entry_end_to_end`, `srw1622_hold_projection`,
  `srw1394_admission_hold`, `srw1894a_pending_replace_refusal`,
  `srw725_paper_guard`, `srw725_contract`, the file-size ratchet, and `node --check`.

These fail identically on the parent head with only the two code files reverted
(verified by stashing this diff and re-running), so they are not this branch:
`scripts/srw725_executor_proof.cjs` (fails at `flagProof`, `expected
/control_disabled|unavailable/`), `srw725_control_store_proof` (fails at load with
`invalid_close_digest` from its own line 27), `srw727_real_dashboard_proof`,
`b2b/srw733_public_readiness.test.cjs`, `srw733_pause_resume_boundary.test.cjs`.

Device, handset and live-service testing is waived by the owner (2026-11-14). No
device or live case was run, and none is reported as failed.

Builder check: PASS 19a4237beb7c8e1ae6fb25e1316469a39ccb3fd2

The builder did not run `scripts/check.sh` (as instructed). The Mac check
publisher posts `srw/agent-check` on this exact head; read it back with the
command in `evidence/SRW-1897/check-proof.md`. This branch is behind
`origin/main` and `MERGEABLE`; it was not rebased, because a head change would
invalidate the gate above.

## Self-review

One reviewer pass with `gpt-6.2-astra` (against the ticket and the blast-radius
rules). Found and fixed:

- **Shared freeze released by the refusal (major).** `unfreezeControlEntries`
  releases on the single-owner projection, so a two-owner freeze could be cleared
  by the expiring command and the entry repriced under the other owner. The
  refusal now releases only a freeze this command solely owns; a shared one keeps
  the row unknown. Proven in `sharedFreezeProof`.
- **A failed release save read as a completed release (major).** The executor
  clears its markers before `save(true)`, so a throw left the next pass seeing
  nothing to release and failing the command past a durable freeze. The release
  is now a take-then-release pair, whose save either lands or throws, and the row
  stays unresolved until it does. Proven in the still-frozen scenario.

### Second review round (this head)

The same reviewer model (`gpt-6.2-astra`) reviewed the first attempt at the gate
fix and returned VERDICT: FAIL with three majors and a proof gap. All four are
fixed here, and the design they criticised is gone rather than patched:

1. **The refusal name was lost on the way out (major).** The paper adapter
   catches the callback's error and throws its own `SafeFault`
   (`alpaca_paper_execution.js:5389`), so the coordinator's outer catch wrote
   `outcome_unknown` over the `send_refused` name it had just committed. Fixed by
   removing the name: the plan item is now `prepared_unsent`, which is durable by
   construction.
2. **A restart before the deadline re-took the marker and renamed the refusal
   (major).** Reproduced by the reviewer on the first attempt. Fixed by the same
   ordering change: the item is `prepared_unsent`, so the observation pass neither
   re-takes a marker nor renames anything, and the refusal survives every
   pre-deadline pass. Asserted in `refusedSendMarkerProof` and
   `refusedSendLiveProof`.
3. **A process death between the two writes left the same plan as an in-flight
   DELETE (major).** The reviewer's suggested order — marker first, then
   `send_started` as the last pre-transport step — is exactly what this head does.
4. **The proof could not detect a broken marker release (major, proof gap).** The
   reviewer removed the marker deletion and both new criteria still passed. There
   is now a criterion that opens recovery with a marker and freeze owned by the
   refused command and asserts the marker is gone after the restart; removing the
   deletion fails it.

Also verified safe and unchanged: the terminal/receipt ordering, `reconciled`
being required to leave `timed_out`, the refusal never touching the broker or
another entry, and the admission projection never masking a stored `kill` (which
`getPause()` quarantines as unknown) or a pause-capable deployment's stored mode.

## Left for later

- **A `kill_entries` (whole-book) pause is not part of this slice.** The send
  boundary changed in the shared `reconcileKill` path, but only the per-entry
  cancel's recovery is exercised here; a pause that refuses one entry's DELETE
  still leaves its own row for the existing drain, which this ticket does not
  change.
- **The file-size ratchet refuses three files, on the parent head too.** With this
  diff stashed, `srw853_file_size_ratchet_proof.cjs` reports the same three files
  (`scripts/srw1445_coordinator_recovery_proof.cjs` over its ~8,000-token budget,
  `thala_control_coordinator.cjs` and `thala_v2_executor.js` over budget and
  growing) with the same numbers, so the refusal predates this branch. Splitting
  those files is its own change, not a ticket edit.
- **A shared git stash was popped into this worktree by accident.** A
  `git stash push` of files with no local changes created nothing, and the
  follow-up `git stash pop` applied another builder's stash
  (`evidence/SRW-1786/receipt.json`, `evidence/SRW-1858/receipt.json`,
  `scripts/p53_outbox_proof.cjs`, `scripts/p53_recovery_notices_proof.cjs`,
  `scripts/srw1463_command_recovery_proof.cjs`, `scripts/srw1463_wiring_proof.cjs`).
  Those paths were restored to `HEAD` and the applied copies were saved to
  `$TMPDIR/recovered-stash/` for their owner. Nothing in this PR's proof or
  comparison relied on `git stash`.
- `scripts/srw725_executor_proof.cjs`, `srw727_real_dashboard_proof` and the
  `srw733` dashboard tests fail on main, so the dashboard surfaces they cover are
  not end-to-end proven on this branch beyond `srw727`'s projectable parts.

bundles.description:
Refs #1845

P53.2 · Recover unresolved manual exits with the dashboard offline. Paper only.
Recovery is off by default and stays off: this PR adds no order path, changes no
admission, and freezes no unrelated exit.

## What this changes

Most of the ticket's production scope already ships on `main`: the coordinator's
`recoverUnknownCommands`/`settleUnknownExits` (#1799, #1857), the
`paper_service.js` recovery tick, `isSelfPost` in
`scripts/b2b_dashboard_discord.cjs`, and `docs/parity/command-recovery.md`.
#1843 was closed as already delivered for the same reason. What was missing was
the ticket's named proof, and the acceptance gaps the proof exposed.

- **`scripts/p53_command_recovery_proof.cjs`** (new) — the scoped offline proof.
  It drives the real control store, the real coordinator, the real control HTTP
  handler, the real executor read and the real Discord projection with a
  credential-free fake broker and a temporary state file, and records every
  broker write so a replay can prove recovery never submits, cancels or
  replaces. 17 replays: R4, R4b, R5, R5b, R5c, R6, R7, R9, R11, R12, R12b,
  R12c, R14, R16, R16b, R16c, R16d.
- **`thala_control_coordinator.cjs`** — the four-read bound is global, not per
  pass; the executor's own record is classified before any capacity is reserved
  for a broker read; classification is separate from the commit, so a row the
  bound defers is never written or paged; and a row whose own record cannot be
  read is isolated. 75 added, 16 deleted lines.
- **`docs/parity/command-recovery.md`** — the bound, the classify/commit split
  and the new proof are described with the cases they replay.
- **`evidence/SRW-1845/check-proof.md`** — the check record, with the mutation
  table.
- **`evidence/SRW-1786/receipt.json`, `evidence/SRW-1858/receipt.json`** — the
  receipts hash the coordinator by content, so they move with it.

## Why the coordinator changed

The ticket's acceptance says "global reads in flight must stay bounded". The
shipped pass bounded reads per pass, so a read that outlived its pass let the
next pass start four more: five or more reads could be in flight at once. The
self-review found this and R16 now pins it.

The Astra gate on `9686dfa7` then found that the bound was applied to the
candidate list before the executor's own terminal record was consulted, so a
broker stall that left four reads outstanding made every later tick skip every
candidate, including an unrelated exit whose fill was already recorded locally.
The record is now classified first: rows it settles need no slot and settle on
that tick, and only the rows that must read compete for the bound. R16b pins it.

## Self-review

One review pass with `codex/gpt-6.2-astra` (`python3 coordinator/bin/models.py
first review router` → `astra-sub gpt-6.2-astra`) against the ticket and the
blast-radius rules. It returned `VERDICT: FAIL` with one major, now fixed:

| Finding | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| MAJOR: a row deferred by the broker-read limit still changed state and paged the owner. With four reads held open, a fifth stale `executing` row went `timed_out` with no read and was absent from the pass results, because `reconcileClose` writes the transition and calls `alarm()` before the slice decides whether to process the row | Classification is now separate from the commit. `classifyClose` reads the executor's record and returns the target state without writing; `reconcileClose` is the only writer and takes the verdict when the caller has one. A deferred row keeps its stored state and pages nobody, a terminal local outcome commits at once, and only a row admitted for a read commits its nonterminal transition. New R16d pins it: with the budget saturated, a stale `executing` row whose record does not match stays `executing`, pages nobody, and is absent from the pass results. Reintroducing the write in the pre-read loop fails R16d with "the deferred row keeps its stored state" |

The reviewer confirmed the original gate finding is fixed, that the pre-loop
catches the malformed-body error, that each classified row reuses its
reconciliation result, and that R16 still holds a timed-out read's slot until the
underlying request settles. It also noted that normal completion can delete the
same set entry twice; deletion is idempotent and the observed maximum stayed at
four, so nothing changed.

An earlier self-review pass on the previous head (`astra-sub gpt-6.2-astra`)
returned six major and two minor findings, all fixed: the global read bound
(R16), fill ownership through the real executor (R4b), tampering on a fresh key
(R11), startup registration and the executed timer block (R12), lock loss and the
stale boundary (R5c, R12c), authenticated authors (R9), the scoped store handle
(R7), and the timer trap honouring cancellation.

Mutation-checked after the fixes: applying the bound before the record check
(R16b), dropping the per-row guard (R16c), writing the transition in the pre-read
loop (R16d), dropping the global reservation (R16), dropping the in-flight filter
(R16), dropping the `attempted` check (R12b), dropping the current-row recheck
(R5b), changing the service tick to 20 s (R12), dropping `botId` from an
`isSelfPost` call site (R9), and releasing the guard only when the pass returns
(R16) each fail the matching replay.

## Proof

`node scripts/p53_command_recovery_proof.cjs` → `SRW-1845 PROOF: PASS (17/17)`,
exit 0, fake services and temporary state only, no leftover temporary directory.

| Replay | Property |
| --- | --- |
| R4 | A proven bound fill settles the unknown command with its terminal notice written in the same transaction; a notice write that fails rolls the terminal state back with it |
| R4b | Only a fill bound to this command settles it, driven through the real executor read |
| R5 | Missing evidence stays local unknown, with the evidence's own reason |
| R5b | A read that outlives its ten second wait is unknown, the late answer settles nothing, and a row another path settled keeps that outcome |
| R5c | A fill that arrives after the writer lock is lost settles nothing |
| R6 | One row's fill never freezes an unrelated exit |
| R7 | The pass is off by default and rides the manual exit capability |
| R9 | The self-post filter is tied to the authenticated identity; a trusted bot notice and a webhook post keep their existing handling |
| R11 | A tampered signature is refused with no write; the same body with its valid signature reaches the same reducer |
| R12 | The service's own recovery tick settles a stale `executing` row with no dashboard read and no market tick |
| R12b | A close queued for its first submission is not a candidate |
| R12c | The five-minute stale threshold is exact |
| R14 | A terminal executor record naming another exit is adopted with no broker read while an unrelated exit is still admitted |
| R16 | A blocked read is never started again, other rows progress, and the reads in flight stay bounded at four across passes |
| R16b | A saturated read budget still settles a row the executor record answers, with no new read started |
| R16c | A row whose own record cannot be read is isolated and an unrelated exit still settles on the same tick |
| R16d | A row the read budget defers keeps its stored state, pages nobody, and is absent from the pass results |

Sibling proofs re-run and passing on this head: `p53_recovery_notices_proof`
(17/17), `p53_service_proof` (9/9), `p53_command_binding_proof` (11/11),
`p53_outbox_proof` (8/8), `p53_alarm_readiness_proof` (6/6),

`srw1463_outbox_retry_proof` (4/4).

`p53_settlement_proof` is 16/17 with R15 failing. That failure is pre-existing on

Refs #1846. Part 3 of the re-cut of #1822 at `d349e1d6`. Parent scope #1463.

## What this delivers

**`thala_control_store.cjs`** — the outbox already spent an attempt at its claim, so a crash after the post still counted it. What it could not say was which kind of exhaustion it reached. A spent budget now closes under `notice_attempts_exhausted` and says which kind it was:

- `unconfirmed: false` — the last attempt recorded a definite failure, kept beside it as `lastReason`.
- `unconfirmed: true` — the budget was spent by claims that never saw an answer, or the last post was accepted by Discord but its answer could not be read.

The waits between the three attempts are 60 and 120 seconds. The shipped single attempt (`retry: false`) keeps its exact previous reason. A post Discord accepted is never recorded as a failed transport: the sent receipt is its own write, so a storage error there leaves the notice claimed for its lease.

**`thala_control_coordinator.cjs`** — the notice page carries the state and reason the drain reported. The local record is its own path, written for every notice failure *before* the five-minute page limit, so a terminal close inside the window is still recorded. A drain that throws is recorded under `notice_drain_failed` with the notices still pending. A queued page keeps the worst state since it was queued. An explicit `THALA_CONTROL_NOTICE_RETRY_ENABLED=0` wins over `THALA_CONTROL_RECOVERY_ENABLED`, so the documented rollback restores the single attempt without turning recovery off.

**`paper_service.js`** — the record names the notice (or the drain error) and its delivery state, and is written before the owner alert is attempted. Every sentence of the page reports the attempt it observed in the past tense, so a page queued while a notice was pending and delivered after it succeeded never claims the notice is still pending. The owner sender carries the newest wording into its retry instead of the text it queued.

**`scripts/p53_notice_delivery_proof.cjs`** — new offline proof, 18 cases, fake transport and temporary state.

**Docs and evidence** — `docs/parity/command-recovery.md`, `docs/parity/README.md`, and `evidence/SRW-1846/check-proof.md`.

## The gate findings on e3c72729

1. **Backoff was five and thirty seconds.** The store had been left on the shipped schedule. `NOTICE_RETRY_MS` is now `[60_000, 120_000]`, and R1 asserts the second attempt is due at exactly 60 seconds and the third at exactly 120.
2. **An ambiguous final POST closed as a known failure.** The store now treats a lost acknowledgement as ambiguous, as it already did for a network error and a 5xx, and a spent budget carries `unconfirmed: true` with the reason kept as `lastReason`. A 2xx loses its acknowledgement in two ways, and both are covered: R1c drives the real poster with a receiver that accepts every post and returns no usable id (`discord_invalid_posted_message_id`), and R1d does the same with a body that does not parse (`discord_invalid_response`).
3. **The queued page still claimed the notice was pending.** The first sentence is now past tense too, and W7 and W7b assert it.

## Self-review

Reviewer: `gpt-6.2-astra` (selected with `python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review standard` → `astra-sub gpt-6.2-astra`).

The reviewer found three more ways the `unconfirmed` flag was lost. All three are fixed and proven:

- **A null answer body closed as a known failure.** A 2xx whose body is not an object makes the poster's own message-id read throw an unclassified error. An unclassified POST outcome is now ambiguous, because the store cannot tell a rejection from a lost answer. R1e proves it.
- **The single attempt dropped the ambiguity.** With the retry off, a 5xx closed the notice without the poster's flag, so the page said "exhausted" while Discord may have held the post. The single attempt now keeps its own reason and its ambiguity. R2c proves it.
- **A later rejection erased an earlier possible delivery.** A 500, then two 403s, closed as a known failure although Discord may hold the first post. Ambiguity is now carried forward across attempts until a sent receipt resolves it. R1f proves it.

The reviewer also flagged that the diff edits four existing proofs and that W7 no longer asserts bounded retries. That is the ticket's known conflict: the mandated 60/120 second backoff and the past-tense page wording cannot be delivered without updating the proofs that pin the old schedule and wording. No case, state or attempt count was weakened. It is recorded under `Left for later`.

## The gate findings on cd9a220d

1. **`srw/agent-check` was `pending` on the reconfirmed head.** A PASS at that moment would have authorized a merge while the required check was still running. The check has now completed on the current head `3634955e` with `CHECK: PASS 3634955e493eb1bb7ec00b52f8a3bc02fb593c38`, and the `Builder check` line below names that same head.
2. **The proof record's provenance was wrong.** `evidence/SRW-1846/check-proof.md` named `75a10f29` as the tested commit, but five paths changed after it: the wiring proof, both parity documents, the deletion of the wiring receipt, and the record itself. The offline proofs and the wiring replays were re-run on `cd9a220d`, and the record now names that commit and states the correction. The wiring result therefore covers the revised proof, including W7b.

The minor is also fixed: the R1 row now says the close keeps the transport reason in both `reason` and `lastReason`, which is what `thala_control_store.cjs` does, instead of claiming `reason` becomes `notice_attempts_exhausted`.

## Proof

`node scripts/p53_notice_delivery_proof.cjs` → `PASS (21/21)`

R1 bounded retry on 60/120s · R1b receipt-write fault is not a delivery failure · R1c ambiguous post is unconfirmed · R1d unreadable answer body is unconfirmed · R1e null answer body is unconfirmed · R1f earlier ambiguity is carried forward · R2 single attempt · R2b explicit off wins over recovery · R2c single attempt keeps its ambiguity · R3 duplicate delivery never repeats an order · R13 independent signal with Discord down · R13b the service's own callbacks · R13c terminal close inside the page window · R13d the record names the notice · R13e the queued page keeps the terminal state · R13f a failed drain is recorded · R13g the sender retries with the updated wording · R15 spent claim survives a restart, unconfirmed exhaustion · R15b the lease on a claim whose deadline has passed · R16 the real poster re-posts under the same nonce · R16b a distinct notice gets a distinct nonce.

Every fix is mutation-tested — reverting it fails the named case. The table is in `evidence/SRW-1846/check-proof.md`.

Also green at this head: `p53_outbox_proof` 8/8, `p53_recovery_notices_proof` 17/17, `srw1463_command_recovery_proof` 17/17, `srw1463_wiring_proof` 8 replays, `srw1344_manual_exit_posts_proof` 15/15, `p53_command_recovery_proof` 17/17, `p53_service_proof` 9/9, `p53_command_binding_proof` 11/11, `srw1463_self_post_proof` 4/4, `p53_alarm_readiness_proof` 6/6, `srw1463_page_proof` 6/6.

Device, handset and live-service testing is waived (Shyam 2026-11-14: "no testing is needed lets just finish backlog building everything"). No device or live case was run, and none is reported as failed.

`srw_review_scope` returns exit 2 (`bot1` on `paper_service.js`, `unknown-executable` on the two `.cjs` files), the same signal #1857 recorded. `check.sh` treats it as a note, not a failure. The Mac check publisher posts `srw/agent-check` on this ready head.

## Merge with main

`origin/main` at `a197f4d2` conflicted with this branch in five files. The merge commit `cd9a220d` resolves them:

- `docs/parity/README.md` and `docs/parity/command-recovery.md` keep main's newer broker-history evidence, claim generation and reply-reference self-post filter, and keep this branch's 60/120 second waits, the two forms of the `notice_attempts_exhausted` close, its `unconfirmed` flag and the ambiguity carried forward across attempts.
- `evidence/SRW-1463/wiring-receipt.json` is deleted, as main deleted it. The wiring proof writes its receipt to a temporary path, never to `evidence/`.
- `evidence/SRW-1786/receipt.json` and `evidence/SRW-1858/receipt.json` are regenerated by their own proofs against the merged code, so each receipt still binds the bytes it ran.

`thala_control_store.cjs`, `thala_control_coordinator.cjs` and `paper_service.js` merged without conflict and keep this branch's behavior. Every proof listed above was re-run on the merged tree and is green.

`origin/main` then advanced to `1e1f6931` (P56.7 and P52.4). The merge commit `3634955e` brings it in cleanly: those two commits touch only `docs/parity/counterfactual-variants.md`, `evidence/p56-counterfactual/`, `scripts/b2b_dashboard_fit.cjs`, `scripts/p52_segmentRetentionExpired_proof.cjs` and `scripts/p56_counterfactual_proof.cjs`, none of which this branch changes. Every proof listed above was re-run on `3634955e` and is green, and the exact-SHA `srw/agent-check` on that head is `CHECK: PASS 3634955e493eb1bb7ec00b52f8a3bc02fb593c38`.

Builder check: PASS 3634955e493eb1bb7ec00b52f8a3bc02fb593c38

## Left for later

- **Four existing proofs are edited.** `p53_outbox_proof.cjs`, `p53_recovery_notices_proof.cjs` and `srw1463_command_recovery_proof.cjs` follow the 60/120 second schedule; `srw1463_wiring_proof.cjs` declares that schedule, shares the callbacks lift, and carries W7b. No case, state or attempt count was weakened. The ticket said no edits to existing checks, but the mandated backoff and the past-tense page wording cannot be delivered without them, so they are reported rather than hidden.
- Counted code: 150 lines across exactly three production files (112 added, 38 deleted), at the 150-line limit. Excluding comments and blank lines it is 85 lines.
- The Telegram owner sender has its own retry and was not changed; only the Discord-only sender is proven.
- `evidence/SRW-1786/receipt.json` and `evidence/SRW-1858/receipt.json` are regenerated against the new production digest.
- Activation, deployment and the live Discord path remain out of scope. A crash after receipt can still produce a duplicate delivery within the budget, which the ticket allows.

+const RETRY = { ...ON, THALA_CONTROL_NOTICE_RETRY_ENABLED: '1' };
+const CAPABILITY = ['manual_exit', 'manual_exit_failed'];
+// The outbox's own contract, restated here so a change to it fails this proof.
+const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3, RETRY_MS = [5_000, 30_000], LEASE_MS = 60_000;
+const realOpen = storeModule.openControlStore;
+const settle = async () => { for (let i = 0; i < 60; i++) await new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve)); };
+// Every replay's store lives in its own temporary directory, and the directory
+// is removed when the replay ends, so a run leaves no state behind.
+const tempDirs = [];
+const tempDir = () => { const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'p53-notice-')); tempDirs.push(dir); return dir; };

+// command it was asked to admit and answers the by-key read from `persisted`.
+// The broker records every write it is asked to make, so a replay can prove the
+// notice path never submits, cancels or replaces an order.
+async function build({ env = ON, dir = tempDir(), notify = null, clock = () => NOW, alert = () => {}, noticeAlert = () => {}, noticeRecord = () => {} } = {}) {
+  const persisted = new Map(), calls = [], writes = [];
+  const executor = { calls, writes, stateHealth: () => ({ writable: true }), traceControlEvent() {},
+    manualClose(request) {
+      calls.push(request);
+      persisted.set(request.commandId, { state: 'admitted', path: 'bot', qty: request.qtyLeft, why: request.why, symbol: SYMBOL, limit: 1.05, admittedAtMs: NOW, queued: true });
+      return { ok: true, admitted: true };
+    },
+    manualExit: (commandId, tradeId) => { const record = persisted.get(commandId); return record ? { commandId, tradeId, ...record } : null; } };

+  storeModule.openControlStore = (_file, identity) => (handle = realOpen(path.join(dir, 'control.sqlite'), { ...identity, clock }));

+      submitOrder: async () => { writes.push('submit'); throw new Error('notice_must_not_submit'); },
+      cancelOrder: async () => { writes.push('cancel'); throw new Error('notice_must_not_cancel'); },
+      replaceOrder: async () => { writes.push('replace'); throw new Error('notice_must_not_replace'); } },

+  const body = command();

+function commandsSnapshot(file) {

bundles.description_excerpt:
Refs #1846. Part 3 of the re-cut of #1822 at `d349e1d6`. Parent scope #1463.

## What this delivers

**`thala_control_store.cjs`** — the outbox already spent an attempt at its claim, so a crash after the post still counted it. What it could not say was which kind of exhaustion it reached. A spent budget now closes under `notice_attempts_exhausted` and says which kind it was:

- `unconfirmed: false` — the last attempt recorded a definite failure, kept beside it as `lastReason`.
- `unconfirmed: true` — the budget was spent by claims that never saw an answer, or the last post was accepted by Discord but its answer could not be read.

The waits between the three attempts are 60 and 120 seconds. The shipped single attempt (`retry: false`) keeps its exact previous reason. A post Discord accepted is never recorded as a failed transport: the sent receipt is its own write, so a storage error there leaves the notice claimed for its lease.

**`thala_control_coordinator.cjs`** — the notice page carries the state and reason the drain reported. The local record is its own path, written for every notice failure *before* the five-minute page limit, so a terminal close inside the window is still recorded. A drain that throws is recorded under `notice_drain_failed` with the notices still pending. A queued page keeps the worst state since it was queued. An explicit `THALA_CONTROL_NOTICE_RETRY_ENABLED=0` wins over `THALA_CONTROL_RECOVERY_ENABLED`, so the documented rollback restores the single attempt without turning recovery off.

**`paper_service.js`** — the record names the notice (or the drain error) and its delivery state, and is written before the owner alert is attempted. Every sentence of the page reports the attempt it observed in the past tense, so a page queued while a notice was pending and delivered after it succeeded never claims the notice is still pending. The owner sender carries the newest wording into its retry instead of the text it queued.

bundles.title: Refs #2282: report an unreadable fill as unknown and a replacement in flight as replacementPending (P50)
bundles.description:
Refs #2282

Part A of the #2240 re-cut: the ownership module's signals alone, so the
adapter change (part B) can be reviewed against a settled contract. One code
file. No adapter, coordinator, store, dashboard or service change.

## What this does

| Change | Where |
| --- | --- |
| `fillNumber` — a number or a digit string, never a coerced boolean, array, exponent, decimal or negative | `paper_external_order_ownership.js` |
| `observe` — a fill it cannot read is `'unknown'`: no fill, price, time or status written, `fillUnknown` set, the proven broker id kept | same |
| `observe` — the replacement hazard is its own flag, set before the readable-fill path, so a lower or unreadable fill cannot hide it | same |
| `observe` — neither the unknown window nor the hazard is closed by a stale lower response; only a readable observation at or above the stored fill closes them | same |
| `observe` — the broker's `pending_replace` is never written into `record.status` | same |
| `presentedStatus` — presents `'pending_replace'` from the flag; a terminal settlement wins | same |
| `linkReplacement` — a provisional link sets the flag, a confirmed link writes `replaced` | same |
| `recoveryTerminal` — a record whose fill is unknown is never authoritative-terminal | same |

## Acceptance and the proof for each

Proof command: `node scripts/srw2180a_ownership_signals_proof.cjs` — 353
assertions, all driving the real module on a plain ledger object. No broker, no
network, no credential, no send. The receipt is
`evidence/SRW-2282/check-proof.md`.

| Criterion | Proof |
| --- | --- |
| 1. an unreadable fill is `unknown`, never a confirmed zero: `null`, absent, blank, `''`, `true`, `false`, `[]`, `{}`, `'1e0'`, `'1.5'`, `'-1'`, `-1`, `2.5`, `'abc'` credit nothing, confirm nothing, write no status and are not conflicts | `unreadableFillIsUnknown` |
| 2. only a fill the broker reported that cannot be this order's — a readable integer above the order quantity — stays an identity conflict | `fillAboveTheOrderIsAConflict` |
| 3. an unreadable fill never refuses the contract's protective sells, and does not disturb a peer trade on the same contract or an unrelated contract | `unreadableFillKeepsTheContractsProtection` |
| 4. the unknown window closes on a readable observation at or above the stored fill and not on a stale lower one | `unknownWindowClosesOnReadableFill` |
| 5. an unreadable reread withdraws recovery-terminal eligibility, and a readable reread restores it | `recoveryTerminalFlipsOnUnreadableFill` |
| 6. a replacement in flight is `replacementPending`, never the settlement status; an unreadable or stale lower fill does not hide it; a provisional link does not overwrite the status; a confirmed link settles `replaced` | `replacementInFlightIsItsOwnSignal`, `confirmedLinkSettlesAsReplaced` |
| 7. both signals survive a restart: `validLedger` accepts a ledger carrying them | `signalsSurviveRestart` |
| 8. a replacement in flight is retired only by a settlement or a confirmed link: an older snapshot at the same fill, and `accepted`, `pending_new`, `partially_filled`, `pending_cancel` all leave it in place; `canceled` retires it | `olderSnapshotDoesNotRetireTheHazard` |

Red on the base: the same proof against the unmodified module fails on
`an unreadable fill is reported unknown (null)` with `true !== 'unknown'`, and a
direct replay of the base shows what it did with that payload —
`{returned: true, filledQty: 0, brokerConfirmed: true, status: 'new'}` — a
confirmed zero. The base also reports a provisional replacement by overwriting
the status: `{parentStatus: 'pending_replace', replacementPending: undefined}`,
and `presentedStatus` does not exist.

Non-vacuity: three mutations each fail the proof — the base module; the two
`fillUnknown` guards removed from `recoveryTerminal`; and an unreadable fill
treated as an identity conflict instead of `unknown`.

## Blast radius, per open trade

| Observation | Effect on the trade | Effect on another trade |
| --- | --- | --- |
| readable fill | unchanged in every respect | none |
| unreadable fill | nothing credited, fill/price/status untouched, stays valid, stays non-terminal, stays open for protection (`pending` unchanged), unknown window open | none. The record is not conflicted, so it stays out of the contract-wide allocation refusal and no peer trade on that contract loses its protective sell |
| fill above the order quantity | identity conflict, as on the base; nothing credited | as on the base, a conflict refuses protective sells for that contract (pre-existing `guardExternalSell`) |
| replacement in flight | hazard on its own flag, surviving a lower or unreadable fill and a restart; settlement status preserved; terminal settlement retires it | none |
| a record that was terminal | terminal eligibility withdrawn while its fill is unknown, restored by a readable reread — never granted | none |

No order is sent by this change and none is suppressed by the feature flag: the
module writes ledger state only. Nothing here changes automatic exits.

## Gate on `1438e38f` — one major, fixed

**Major — an equal-fill observation retired `replacementPending`.** `observe`
retired the hazard on any status other than `pending_replace`, so a routine race
ate it: the stream reports `pending_replace` at zero fills, then an older HTTP
snapshot reports the pre-replacement status at zero fills, and `presentedStatus`
presented `new` while the replacement was still in flight.

Fixed: a live, non-terminal observation no longer retires the hazard at all. It
is retired only by a terminal settlement, or by a confirmed replacement link in
`linkReplacement`. An older snapshot taken before the replacement is
indistinguishable from a live one at the same fill, so it can never be evidence
that the replacement resolved. `olderSnapshotDoesNotRetireTheHazard` replays the
gate's exact sequence, then `accepted`, `pending_new`, `partially_filled` and
`pending_cancel`, then `canceled`; restoring the old retirement line re-fails the
proof on `an equal fill does not retire the hazard`.

Blast radius of that fix: the observed order keeps presenting `pending_replace`
while it is live, so a reader refuses to cancel a parent whose replacement may
still be in flight even after an abandoned replacement. That is the safe
direction, and it touches no peer record, raises no contract-wide conflict,
sends no order and blocks no other trade's exit.

The gate's other notes are carried in `evidence/SRW-2282/check-proof.md`: the
unreadable-fill signal is fixed in the module, a malformed fill no longer
conflicts the contract, and the earlier adapter scope violation is resolved. The
reader's confirmed-zero fallback, the adapter's uncertain-send clearing and the
publication of `pending_replace` stay open for part B, under *Left for later*.

## Self-review

One pass by `astra-sub` (`gpt-6.2-astra`), chosen with
`python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review gpt-6.1-sol` →
`astra-sub gpt-6.2-astra`. No critical. Three majors and one minor.

1. **Major — an unreadable payload conflicted the record, and a conflict refuses
   protective sells for the whole contract.** Reproduced: an unreadable fill on
   one trade reached `external_order_allocation_unverified` for a peer trade on
   the same contract via `guardExternalSell` (`alpaca_paper_execution.js:14386`),
   whose predicate is symbol-wide. **Fixed.** Unreadable fills are now `unknown`,
   not conflicts; only a readable integer above the order quantity stays a
   conflict. The proof pins `guardExternalSell`'s exact predicate on a shared
   contract and shows a real conflict still refuses it.
2. **Major — an unreadable fill can clear an uncertain sell send**
   (`alpaca_paper_execution.js:14286`). **Not introduced here, not fixed here.**
   Reproduced identically against the base module with the adapter unchanged:
   base `{returned: true, sendUncertain: false, authoritativeStatus: 'new'}`,
   this head `{returned: 'unknown', sendUncertain: false, authoritativeStatus:
   'new'}`. The clearing comes from the adapter's own `Number(raw.filled_qty)`
   comparison, which this ticket does not touch. Part B's defect. See
   *Left for later*.
3. **Major — existing readers no longer see `pending_replace` in the published
   status.** This is the ticket's stated change, and it is bounded. The only
   consumer that treats the two differently is
   `validateControlEntry(..., { forCancel })` (`thala_v2_executor.js:8083`), and
   `forCancel` is never passed — the sole call is `validateControlEntry(item,
   raw)` at `:8113`. Every other consumer puts `pending_replace` and the
   settlement status in the same branch (`thala_v2_executor.js:8099` and `:8634`,
   `alpaca_paper_execution.js:6448`, `thala_control_coordinator.cjs:1313`), both
   non-terminal and both `working`. The one behavioural difference is
   settled-versus-stale: the base overwrote a terminal settlement status with
   `pending_replace` and made a settled order look live; this head keeps it
   settled. Part B wires `presentedStatus` into the reader. See *Left for later*.
4. **Minor — the proof's `recoveryTerminal` assertions were vacuous**: it still
   passed with both `fillUnknown` guards removed, because it started from a
   record that was already non-terminal. **Fixed.** The proof now starts from an
   authoritative terminal sell, takes an unreadable reread, asserts
   terminal → not terminal, then a readable reread and asserts not terminal →
   terminal. Removing either guard now fails the proof.

## Regression sweep

Run after the fix above, on the final head. These pass: `srw1445_executor_fill`,
`srw2175_executor`, `srw639_fill_edge`, `srw639_unpriced_fill`,
`srw639_price_identity`, `srw639_price_budget`, `srw699_final_reconcile`,
`srw699_exit_budget_path`, `srw699_retired_snapshot`,
`srw699_round5_routine_cancel`, `p55_owner_recovery`, `srw1459_5_reservation_kind`, `srw1445_store_receipt`,
`srw1445_coordinator_cancel`, `srw1445_coordinator_recovery`,
`srw725_paper_guard`, `srw1458_4_book_execution`, `srw1458_4_fills_reconcile`,
`srw897_p06b_fill_unpriced`, `srw699_never_ack`.

These fail, and fail identically on the base with this change stashed, so none
is a regression: `srw617_replacement_ownership_proof`,
`srw617_v2_ownership_proof`, `srw639_owned_unpriced_fill_proof`,
`srw639_flat_book_proof`, `disk_partial_protection_proof`,
`srw699_reconcile_budget_proof`.

## Left for later

- Part B: wire `presentedStatus` into `externalOwnershipMetadata`
  (`alpaca_paper_execution.js:14436`), so the reader publishes
  `pending_replace` from the flag.
- Part B: the adapter clears `sendUncertain` from `Number(raw.filled_qty)` at
  `alpaca_paper_execution.js:14286`, so an unreadable fill still clears an
  uncertain send. Pre-existing, outside this ticket's one file.

## Scope

One code file, 79 changed lines in `paper_external_order_ownership.js`
(72 added, 7 removed). The proof script and `evidence/SRW-2282/` are excluded from
the gate count. No
test, fixture, proof or release check was edited or weakened. No workflow file,
no secret, no live credential, no broker write, no new dependency.

## Waived testing

Device, handset and live-service testing is waived (Shyam 2026-11-14: "no
testing is needed lets just finish backlog building everything"). No device,
handset, live-service or live-broker case was run; they are waived, not failed.
The same statement is in `evidence/SRW-2282/check-proof.md`.

## Updated from main

Head moved `50660892` → `1438e38f` → `ec10ce70` by fast-forward merges of
`origin/main` (`225719bf` `Refs #1758`, `ccc5b902` `Refs #2113`, `98194f1b`
`Refs #2245`). None touches either file here, so there was no conflict. Every push
was a plain fast-forward; no force-push. Re-run on the merged head: this ticket's
proof 353/353, and main's `srw1458_5_execution_dedup_proof` 9/9 with this change
in place.

The publisher's exact-head agent check passed: `srw/agent-check` `success`,
"Clean exact-SHA PR tier passed", 29/29 gates, lanes A/B/C all 0, 153 seconds, at
`ec10ce7034fa3127dfa36e45d6ed53524d0e480e`.

bundles.description_excerpt:
Refs #2282

Part A of the #2240 re-cut: the ownership module's signals alone, so the
adapter change (part B) can be reviewed against a settled contract. One code
file. No adapter, coordinator, store, dashboard or service change.

## What this does

| Change | Where |
| --- | --- |
| `fillNumber` — a number or a digit string, never a coerced boolean, array, exponent, decimal or negative | `paper_external_order_ownership.js` |
| `observe` — a fill it cannot read is `'unknown'`: no fill, price, time or status written, `fillUnknown` set, the proven broker id kept | same |
| `observe` — the replacement hazard is its own flag, set before the readable-fill path, so a lower or unreadable fill cannot hide it | same |
| `observe` — neither the unknown window nor the hazard is closed by a stale lower response; only a readable observation at or above the stored fill closes them | same |
| `observe` — the broker's `pending_replace` is never written into `record.status` | same |
| `presentedStatus` — presents `'pending_replace'` from the flag; a terminal settlement wins | same |
| `linkReplacement` — a provisional link sets the flag, a confirmed link writes `replaced` | same |
| `recoveryTerminal` — a record whose fill is unknown is never authoritative-terminal | same |

## Acceptance and the proof for each

Proof command: `node scripts/srw2180a_ownership_signals_proof.cjs` — 353
assertions, all driving the real module on a plain ledger object. No broker, no
network, no credential, no send. The receipt is
`evidence/SRW-2282/check-proof.md`.

| Criterion | Proof |
| --- | --- |
| 1. an unreadable fill is `unknown`, never a confirmed zero: `null`, absent, blank, `''`, `true`, `false`, `[]`, `{}`, `'1e0'`, `'1.5'`, `'-1'`, `-1`, `2.5`, `'abc'` credit nothing, confirm nothing, write no status and are not conflicts | `unreadableFillIsUnknown` |
| 2. only a fill the broker reported that cannot be this order's — a readable integer above the order quantity — stays an identity conflict...

bundles.description:
Refs #2177

Part 2 of 4 of the re-cut of #2175, standing in for #1893 (Parity P45.2). The
frozen source is `d2ea06a9..7cf4e72a` of #1893; this slice takes the ownership
module and the three adapter hunks and nothing else.

## Merge with origin/main

This branch conflicted with `main` and could not be gated, so `origin/main` at
`0f535e58` is merged in at `458c42c3` and every check and receipt below is on the
merged code. #2290 (#2282, P50 part A, `91175b72`) had rewritten the same
`observe` region, which is the textual duplicate the previous head already
flagged, so the merge keeps main's rule where the two disagree:

- a fill the module cannot read is **unknown**, never an identity conflict. This
  slice's earlier "a present but malformed value is a conflict" no longer holds:
  a conflict on one record refuses every protective sell for that contract, which
  is why main landed the wider rule. `true`, `false`, `[]`, `'1e0'`, `'1.5'` and
  `'-1'` are unknown, credit nothing and write nothing; a *readable* quantity
  above the order still is a conflict;
- the replacement hazard keeps main's lifecycle: only a `pending_replace` status
  sets `replacementPending`, only a terminal settlement or a confirmed link
  retires it, and `presentedStatus` presents it instead of overwriting the
  settlement status;
- this slice's additions are unchanged on top: `brokerOrderIdFree`,
  `executionMs`, the price/time pair rule, `filledAtMs`, and the `groupFill`
  depth and time selection.

`scripts/srw2175_ownership_proof.cjs` follows the merged rule: its malformed-fill
case asserts unknown in head mode, and the pinned base run still asserts the
predecessor's defects. No test, proof or fixture that came from `main` changed,
and the proofs main landed in this merge (`srw2180a_ownership_signals_proof.cjs`,
`srw1458_5_execution_dedup_proof.cjs`, `srw699_final_reconcile_proof.cjs`) pass
on the merged code.

## What changed

`paper_external_order_ownership.js`
- `fillNumber` parses a broker fill strictly (a `number` or a digit string). A
  fill it cannot read — absent, null, blank, `true`, `false`, `[]`, `'1e0'`,
  `'1.5'`, `'-1'` — is **unknown**, never zero and never an identity conflict
  (the merged P50 part A rule). A readable quantity above the order is a
  conflict. Nothing unknown credits anything.
- `brokerOrderIdFree` binds a broker order id to one record, checked in `observe`
  before any fill, price, time or status is written.
- `observe` records an unknown quantity as `fillUnknown`, keeps the verified
  broker id, and only a readable observation at or above the stored fill closes
  the window, so a stale lower response cannot erase a missed quantity.
- `executionMs` reads the broker execution time in the executor's key order and
  drops a value outside the JavaScript date range. A time first supplied on an
  equal-quantity reread is backfilled before the terminal early returns, and only
  when the reread's price is absent, agrees, or the record has none, so a fill's
  price is never paired with a disagreeing observation's time.
- The price and the time of a fill are replaced together or not at all. A
  cumulative fill that rises takes both from the observation that raised it; an
  equal-quantity reread takes neither, except that the first price a fill
  receives brings its own execution time with it. So a fill never reports a
  price from one observation and a time from another.
- The replacement hazard is its own `replacementPending` flag, so a lower or
  unreadable fill never hides it and it never overwrites the settlement status.
- `groupFill` selects on an equal quantity by price availability and then by the
  observation nearer the child, carries the selected observation's id and time,
  and takes an agreeing observation's time when the nearest one has none.

`alpaca_paper_execution.js` — the three hunks the ticket names, plus one line of
the same finding one layer out:
- the ID-only acknowledgement in `submitOrder` refuses a broker id another record
  already owns;
- `observeExternalOrder` and `adoptExternalReplacement` only confirm an
  unresolved send from a readable filled quantity equal to the stored fill;
- `externalOwnershipMetadata` reports the group fill's price with the group
  fill's time, instead of leaving the response's own `filled_at` beside a price
  that came from another observation. The response's other execution-time
  aliases (`executed_at`, `transaction_time`, `fill_time`, `filledAt`) are
  neutralised with it.

Everything else in the source adapter diff (read hardening, lineage traversal,
control snapshots) belongs to #2178/#2179 and is not here.

### Three deliberate deviations from the frozen hunk

All three come from the self-review and all stay inside the ticket's acceptance
and "must not cause" rules:

1. The source throws the duplicate-ID refusal as `SafeFault(code, null, true)`,
   and the third argument is `notSent`. Because the broker has already answered
   the POST, that marked the sell `not_submitted`, cleared `sendUncertain` and
   released its pending quantity. The refusal now passes no `notSent`, so the
   record keeps its send marker and stays unresolved. The proof drives two real
   sell submissions through a fake broker to pin this.
2. The source overwrites a fill's price on an equal-quantity reread and keeps the
   previous observation's time, so a partial fill at 6.1 dated 14:41 could be
   reported as 8 at 14:41. The price and the time are now one observation's pair:
   a raised fill replaces both, a reread replaces neither, and the first price
   brings its own time. The proof pins both directions; the pinned base asserts
   the defects.

## Scope

Gate-counted additions plus deletions over the two runtime files: **167**
(122+8 in `paper_external_order_ownership.js`, 30+7 in
`alpaca_paper_execution.js`), against 131 in the frozen source hunks; the extra
lines are the price/time pair rule, the metadata time aliases and the comments for
both. 2 code files. Proof script and the evidence receipt are excluded.

## Proof

```
node --experimental-sqlite scripts/srw2175_ownership_proof.cjs
SRW_PROOF_BASE=1e1f6931 node --experimental-sqlite scripts/srw2175_ownership_proof.cjs
```

Head `458c42c3` (the merge commit that carries the merged runtime): 222
assertions pass, runtime code hash
`d3bc4dd6938bf2442f69e04b95f131124a8e0586a0373e980c82777387477450`, input
`555ba579…6bec`, expected `dc9fc678…6e97`. The run at the final head reports the
same hash, because nothing but evidence changed after the merge commit.

Base `1e1f6931`: the same harness compiles both files out of Git at that revision,
binds the adapter's own require of the ownership module to that revision, and
asserts the documented defects — a second broker-id binding accepted by
observation, adoption and the ID-only acknowledgement; a null or blank quantity
clearing `sendUncertain` on both adapter confirmation paths; a null quantity
standing in for a missed quantity, so a stale lower response is indistinguishable
from a fresh one; an equal cumulative fill keeping neither its priced basis nor
its time; a partial fill losing its price to a reread at another average; and no
strict fill parser at all. 155 assertions, code hash `0cb0ca1a`.

Receipt: `evidence/SRW-1807/ownership-fill-receipt.json`, rewritten by the
`--receipt` run at `458c42c3` so its `head` names the commit whose runtime bytes
it read, and `evidence/SRW-2177/check-proof.md` (every builder check, the command
that ran it and its result, the merge resolution, and the file inventory of the
slice). `evidence/SRW-1806/executor-fill-receipt.json` is #2176's receipt and is
left at the merge base's bytes: that harness writes it at the end of every
successful run, so the restore is its own step and this slice carries no change
to it.

Builder check: PASS 8ff98287752816d0369f2d7f3997216cdaee6e4a

`scripts/check.sh` was not run here; the builder does not run the heavy script in
this repo. The merge gate is the agent gate: `heavy scripts/check.sh` on a clean
checkout of the exact PR head, ending `CHECK: PASS <full sha>`, followed by the
reviewer's `VERDICT: PASS`. The `Builder check` line above is the repository's
pre-push check tier on this exact head (`PUSH: PASS 8ff98287…`, syntax and review
scope), which is not the merge gate. `srw/agent-check` is posted by the trusted
Mac publisher on each checked **main** SHA after `heavy scripts/check.sh --full`,
and paper-live promotion requires that status at that exact main SHA; it is not a
per-PR-head status, so this PR claims none.
`evidence/SRW-2177/check-proof.md` lists every builder check, the command that
ran it and its result, and does not list `scripts/check.sh` as a `not run` row.

## Existing checks run

```
node --check paper_external_order_ownership.js
node --check alpaca_paper_execution.js
node --experimental-sqlite scripts/srw2175_executor_proof.cjs   # 161 checks, #2176 interface preserved
node test_srw15_order_path_review.js
node test_telegram_trade_update.js
node test_telegram_trade_behavior.js
node test_telegram_own_trade_update_loop.js
node --experimental-sqlite scripts/srw725_paper_guard_proof.cjs
node test_srw1222_sell_scan_class.js
```

`scripts/check.sh` was not run here (the merge gate runs it at the PR head).
`node scripts/srw_review_scope.cjs` reports `review: opus` for the two runtime
files (bot1 runtime), which `scripts/check.sh` treats as a merge-scope signal,
not a failure.

## Gate findings on `991c776f`

Both majors are closed in `92836e8f`, and neither touched a runtime file:

- **Major, receipt provenance.** The receipt named ancestor `fda5c65f`, so the
  recorded SHA did not identify the harness that produced the reported base
  result. Regenerated with `--receipt` at `19174031`: `head` now names that
  commit, and `codeSha` `6a143f0d` pins the runtime bytes the run read, so the
  receipt identifies the code whichever commit carries the evidence file.
- **Major, `not run` row.** `evidence/SRW-2177/check-proof.md` listed
  `heavy --review scripts/check.sh` with result `not run`. It is not a builder
  check, so it is no longer a table row; a paragraph after the table names the
  agent gate and the publisher. Every row that remains passed.

The same gate failed the PR for changing head while it read (`991c776f` →
`19174031`). That needs no code change: the head is now final at `92836e8f`, and
nothing in this PR claims a result on any other commit. The prior findings the
gate re-checked (duplicate ID-only acknowledgement preserving the pending sell,
the disagreeing-price time, the partial-fill price overwrite, the nearest-child
proof reading from the root, the adoption proof asserting the link and sends,
and the proof hashing the sources it loaded) all still hold at this head.

## Self-review

astra-sub (`gpt-6.2-astra`, the first unblocked `review` model that is not the
builder's) reviewed the diff from `1e1f6931` to the head against the ticket and
the frozen hunks. One critical, three majors, one minor — all fixed:

- **Critical** duplicate ID-only acknowledgement threw `notSent=true` after the
  broker accepted the POST, releasing the pending sell quantity. Fixed as
  deviation 1 above; the proof asserts the second sell stays unresolved with its
  pending quantity intact. Verified the defect reproduced before the fix.
- **Major** equal-quantity reread could date a fill with a disagreeing price's
  time. Fixed as deviation 2; the proof pins the disagreeing and agreeing
  sequences at a terminal fill.
- **Major** the nearest-child proof read the group fill from the leaf, which the
  scan already starts from, so the depth tie-break was untested. It now reads from
  the root and still expects the leaf; removing the tie-break fails it.
- **Major** the adoption proof asserted a child id `prepareReplacement` had
  already inserted, so skipping adoption passed. The child now starts unresolved
  and the proof asserts the link, the child broker id and both unresolved sends.
- **Minor** the proof hashed the working-tree files in both modes and recorded the
  head count as the base count. It now hashes the sources each mode loaded, and
  the receipt records only the head count.

Mutation checks after the fixes: dropping the price gate stores the disagreeing
observation's time and pairs price 5 with it; dropping the depth tie-break names
the root instead of the leaf. Both fail the head run.

### Third round, the merge with `origin/main`

astra-sub (`gpt-6.2-astra`) reviewed the merge resolution,
`92836e8f..4260c537`: **no runtime defect**. It confirmed the unreadable-fill path
returns before writing price or time, a stale lower fill preserves both
`fillUnknown` and `replacementPending`, `raised` is computed before `filledQty`
changes, and it reproduced 353 P50 checks plus 222 head and 155 base slice
assertions. Four evidence findings, all fixed in the evidence-only commit that
follows:

- **Major** `check-proof.md` named `heavy scripts/check.sh --review` as the
  release gate and `srw/agent-check` as a per-PR-head status. The gate is
  `heavy scripts/check.sh` at the PR head ending `CHECK: PASS`, and the publisher
  posts on checked main SHAs.
- **Minor** the replacement hazard is also set by a provisional `linkReplacement`,
  not only by a `pending_replace` observation.
- **Minor** the equal-quantity rule left out its second exception: a reread at the
  stored price may supply a missing time.
- **Minor** the historical receipt finding still said `19174031` where the receipt
  run this branch records is `458c42c3`.

That round also rewrote `evidence/SRW-1806/executor-fill-receipt.json`, which is
#2176's record; the gate on `d6df44c3` caught it and the fourth round below
reverts it.

### Second round, for the gate finding on `4c0ec448`

The gate found that a nonterminal equal-quantity reread overwrote
`filledAvgPrice` while keeping the previous observation's `filledAtMs`. astra-sub
reviewed the fix (diff `4c0ec448..991c776f`) and found two majors and three
minors. All fixed:

- **Major** the fix covered the disagreeing-price path but a fill could still take
  a later observation's price with an earlier observation's time when the first
  observation carried no price. The rule is now one rule: the first price brings
  its own execution time, and a reread may only date a fill whose stored price it
  matches. Reproduced the mixed pair on `4c0ec448`; `firstPriceBringsItsOwnTime`
  pins it.
- **Major** `externalOwnershipMetadata` spread the raw response and overwrote only
  the quantity and price, so its caller received the group fill's price beside the
  response's own `filled_at`. It now reports the pair and neutralises the other
  aliases; `adapterMetadataKeepsThePair` pins it.
- **Minor** `check-proof.md` cited `heavy scripts/check.sh --review`, which the
  script rejects. The merge-with-main round corrected the document further: the
  merge gate is `heavy scripts/check.sh` at the PR head, ending `CHECK: PASS`,
  and the publisher's `srw/agent-check` is a main-SHA status.
- **Minor** the receipt command in `check-proof.md` did not write a receipt. It now
  names the `--receipt` run and the head that run recorded.
- **Minor** `check-proof.md` attributed the mixed-timestamp reproduction to the
  pinned base, which only shows the price half. It now attributes it to
  `4c0ec448`.

Two existing proof fixtures dated a priced row from an observation that stated no
price; under the one-pair rule those observations now state the price they agree
with, so the assertions they support are unchanged in strength. Re-running the
whole suite after these fixes: 204 head assertions, 154 base assertions.

This last commit changes only `evidence/SRW-2177/check-proof.md` and
`evidence/SRW-1807/ownership-fill-receipt.json`. It is not a runtime change, so
the in-session reviewer round was spent on the two rounds above and no second
round was run for it, per the standing rule. The gate reviews `92836e8f` itself.

### Fourth round, for the gate finding on `d6df44c3`

The gate found that the diff from the checked commit `458c42c3` to the previous
head replaced `evidence/SRW-1806/executor-fill-receipt.json`, a receipt #2176
owns, so a pass would have authorized merging another ticket's receipt on that
run. The cause is that `scripts/srw2175_executor_proof.cjs` writes that receipt
at the end of every successful run and restores nothing. The file is restored to
the merge base's bytes (`sha256 68aa0eab…`), no runtime or harness byte changed,
and the diff against `0f535e58` now holds only this slice's five files.

The review pass for this fix was run by `gpt-6.2-sol` on `codex`. The
`python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review` command named by the standing
rule does not exist in this repository, and the router's `task/review` model
failed to start twice, so the first available non-MiniMax, non-Qwen route was
used. Two majors, both fixed, both about wording in `check-proof.md`:

- **Major** the file inventory was described as the diff against `origin/main`,
  which now lists eight files because `main` moved past `0f535e58` after this
  branch's merge. The inventory is now pinned to the merge base and says so.
- **Major** the proof said the receipt is restored as part of running the check.
  It is not: the harness overwrites the receipt and restores nothing, a failure
  before the write leaves it untouched, and the restore is a separate step. The
  table row, the inventory section and the gate item now say that.

The committed change is evidence-only. `git diff d6df44c3 8ff98287` touches
`evidence/SRW-1806/executor-fill-receipt.json` and
`evidence/SRW-2177/check-proof.md`, and nothing else.

## Left for later

- Ordinary broker DELETE target hardening, lineage traversal and control
  snapshots are #2178/#2179.
- `scripts/srw639_owned_unpriced_fill_proof.cjs` fails in its `realRoundTrip`
  alert assertion (`w.alerts.length > 0`). The same failure reproduces on
  `1e1f6931`, so it is pre-existing and untouched here; that proof is not part of
  the release gate.
- `scripts/srw2175_executor_proof.cjs` writes #2176's receipt on every run and
  has no `--receipt` gate, so any run needs the restore repeated. Gating that
  write is a change for #2176's harness, not for this slice.
- #2180's P50 part A (#2282, `91175b72`) landed first and is merged here, so the
  duplicated ledger hunks are resolved in this branch rather than a later one.
  P50 part B (#2240) remains open there.

bundles.description:
Refs #2295

## What changed

Bot 1 skipped today's SPY 725 Call open (seq 2538, 10:21 ET) and its close (seq 2551, 10:55 ET). Both cards arrived with `"mode":"live"`, the feed refused every mode that was not `paper`, and the Discord notice then called a real card a test card.

This fixes exactly the ticket's stated change, no wider:

1. `thala_v2_feed.js` accepts `mode` of `paper` or `live` (`TRADED_MODES`). Every other value, and a missing mode, still refuses as `mode_not_paper`. Bot 1 places paper orders only; the card's mode never selects a broker or an account.
2. A `live` card inside the reserved test sequence range (seq >= 900000) refuses as `live_seq_reserved`. The reserved range belongs to paper test cards, so a live card there places no order and neither moves the watermark nor reports a sequence gap.
