bundles.title: Refs #2278: refuse a resolved pending_replace on the ordinary cancel path (re-cut of #2230 part A)
bundles.description:
Refs #2278

Re-cut part A of #2230 after four gate rounds. One code file
(`thala_v2_executor.js`), 137 changed lines. The coordinator recovery scenarios
and their end-to-end proof are part B (#1830); nothing here touches the
coordinator, the store, the dashboard or a service.

## What this does

| Change | Where |
| --- | --- |
| the ordinary entry DELETE refuses a broker-reported `pending_replace`, with or without a control send marker | `safeCancel`, ordinary branch |
| the ordinary DELETE also refuses a parent while the durable local `replacementPending` marker is set, which covers a replace whose outcome is unknown | same |
| the cancel path's read is its own retained per-trade observation: not ready within a tick → refuse the pass and re-run when it lands; failed or rate-limited → no status, so the DELETE still runs | `cancelEntryObservation`, `readCancelEntry` |
| the marked entry's control read catches only the broker GET; `resolveControlEntry` stays outside the catch | `readCancelEntry` |
| a failed control GET falls back to the authenticated read, which still refuses `pending_replace`/`replaced_by`/`replacementPending` and only this trade's own entry, and books no fill | `safeCancel`, marked branch |
| a failed durable save during replacement adoption restores the parent identity and the ownership rows it added, then rethrows, so no later cancel can name a child the disk never recorded | `resolveControlEntry` |

## Acceptance and the proof for each

Proof command: `node scripts/srw1894a_pending_replace_refusal_proof.cjs` —
42 assertions driving the real executor and a credential-free fake broker
(`node --experimental-sqlite`). Check log: `evidence/SRW-2278/check-proof.md`;
the exact head every run belongs to is the `Builder check` line below.

| Criterion | Proof |
| --- | --- |
| the ordinary path refuses a resolved `pending_replace` with the control plane off, and sends no order while refusing | `controlOffRefusal` |
| the same refusal with the control plane on and no send marker | `controlOnRefusal` |
| the same refusal with the executor's own `entryControlsEnabled` set | `executorFlagRefusal` |
| the durable local marker refuses a parent the broker still reports `new` | `replacementPendingRefusal` |
| a live entry is still cancelled, on the same tick | `liveEntryCancels` |
| an unreadable status never blocks a routine cancel | `unreadableGuardStillCancels` |
| a failed control GET falls back and still cancels a live entry | `markedFallbackCancels` |
| the same fallback still refuses a replacement in flight | `markedFallbackRefuses` |
| a failed adoption write authorizes no DELETE at all, leaves the parent identity in memory, reports the write failure, and the child identity never reaches disk — once for the cancel path, once on the expiry tick where the fill read adopts first | `adoptionWriteFailure`, `adoptionWriteFailureOnExpiry` |
| one trade's refused cancel does not block another trade's cancel | `isolation` |

Red on the base: `SRW_PROOF_BASE=91175b72 node --experimental-sqlite
scripts/srw1894a_pending_replace_refusal_proof.cjs` reports
`ordinary_canceled_pending_replace|ordinary_canceled_pending_replace_control_on|ordinary_canceled_pending_replace_executor_flag|ordinary_ignored_replacement_pending|marked_read_failure_stranded`
— the base deleted the parent on every ordinary path, ignored the durable
marker, and stranded a marked entry whose control read failed.

## Gate round 4 (head `edc3c6ce` to this head)

The gate on `edc3c6ce` returned `VERDICT: FAIL` with two majors. Both are fixed.

| Finding | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| MAJOR, `thala_v2_executor.js:3750`: a delayed control GET can overwrite a newer, durably adopted replacement. The GET outlived the control boundary the pass held, so a read that landed after reconciliation adopted a newer child wrote the older authenticated child back to disk, and the DELETE then followed the wrong order. | The outstanding GET is now only a broker read. `readCancelEntry` returns the raw row, and `resolveControlEntry` runs where the result is consumed, inside `cancel()` and so inside `withControlEntryBoundary`, and only while the read still names the entry the cancel is for. A read whose entry moved along its chain is dropped, and the deferred pass re-reads the chain. |
| MAJOR proof gap, `scripts/srw1894a_pending_replace_refusal_proof.cjs:230`: the isolation replay used two well-formed entries and never a partial persisted one. A target with no `id` and no cached read made `cancelEntryObservation` read a property of a missing cache entry (the retained-read test compared `undefined` with `undefined`, so the next line threw), so that entry could only fail the cancel path, never decide it. | The lookup reads the retained entry only when one is retained. An entry with no broker order id names no order to read or DELETE, so `cancel()` refuses it at its start: no read, no request, no thrown fault, that entry only, and the tick and every other trade keep running. The fill path also skips its id-less fallback GET. The proof now holds both control reads until a newer child is adopted and releases them in the order that used to rewrite the ledger and then cancel the older child, and it drives a partial persisted entry alone and beside a working entry in the same tick. |

The self-review for this round found two more defects in the same area; both are
fixed before this push. The fill read had the identical late-adoption write: a
released fill GET rewrote the ledger to the older child, and the cancel path then
sent a DELETE for it. And a partial entry whose control GET failed reached
`broker.getOrder(undefined)` in the fill path, recording a 404 fault against the
trade. `readControlEntry` now refuses a read whose entry moved
(`control_entry_read_stale`) before it adopts, and the fill fallback is skipped
when there is no broker id to name.

## Self-review

Round 4, before this push: one pass with astra-sub / `gpt-6.2-astra`, chosen with
`python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review standard` (the first unblocked
review entry that is not the builder's own model), against the new commit. It
returned `VERDICT: FAIL` and reproduced a critical (the fill read's late
adoption) and a major (the id-less fallback GET) against the fake broker, with
the checkout left clean. Both are fixed, the ticket proof covers both scenarios
and fails on the previous head (case: a fill read that lands late never writes
the older child back; it observed `-r1` where the newer child is `-r1-r1`), and
every check below was rerun on the new head. It raised no minor findings.

Round 3: one pass with a different model — astra-sub / `gpt-6.2-astra`, chosen with
`python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review gpt-6.1-sol` — at head
`144219e6`, returned `VERDICT: FAIL` with five majors. All five are fixed:

- **MAJOR, fixed** — a failed adoption write could still be followed by a
  DELETE of the child, because the fill poll's catch read the persistence error
  as a read failure and the child then existed in memory only. Fixed on the
  durable side: `resolveControlEntry` now restores the parent identity and the
  ownership rows on a failed `save(true)` and rethrows, so no later cancel — in
  that tick or a retry — can name a child the disk never recorded
  (`025d8f82`). `adoptionWriteFailureOnExpiry` drives exactly that same-tick
  sequence.
- **MAJOR, fixed** — slow successful GETs could starve the cancel: the fill poll
  and the cancel guard shared one cached read keyed by the entry, so the poll
  consumed every answer and the guard deferred forever. The cancel path now owns
  its own retained read (`cancelEntryObservation`), so one landed read is used
  by the cancel, not by the poll.
- **MAJOR, fixed** — the marked entry's fallback GET blocked protection for
  every later trade, because it was awaited unbounded inside the serial advance
  loop. Both the control read and its fallback now run inside the same
  per-trade deferred observation: not ready within a tick refuses that pass
  only.
- **MAJOR, fixed** — the ordinary guard ignored the durable local
  `replacementPending` marker, so a replace whose outcome was unknown could be
  cancelled at its parent. The ordinary refusal now covers it.
- **MAJOR, fixed** — the adoption assertion in the proof could not establish
  its claim: it compared a parent id against a `thala-undefined` helper string
  and asserted only that one id was absent. The proof now uses the broker child's
  own `id` and `client_order_id`, asserts the DELETE list is empty, asserts the
  parent identity is still the memory identity, asserts the child client id is
  absent from the persisted ledger, and asserts the reported
  `thala_v2_state_write_failed` line. The executor-flag case sets
  `entryControlsEnabled` explicitly instead of relying on the paper wiring, which

narrow the fill poll's catch to the broker GET. It stays a catch-all because an
error escaping `readEntry` would reject the whole advance and cost *every other

| Situation | This trade | Every other trade |
| --- | --- | --- |

| broker reports `pending_replace` | DELETE refused; the entry keeps working and the tick re-runs; the verified descendant is adopted by the existing reconciliation | none |
| durable `replacementPending` set | DELETE refused until the replacement outcome is verified and the marker cleared | none |
| cancel-path read deferred (slow GET) | DELETE refused for that pass only; the tick re-runs when the read lands | none — the read is per trade and the pass is not held |
| cancel-path read failed or rate-limited | unchanged from today: the DELETE runs, because no status was reported | none |
| failed durable write during adoption | no DELETE, parent identity kept in memory and on disk, failure reported; retried next tick | none |
| control plane off | the ordinary refusal above applies; no order is sent by this change and none is suppressed by a flag | none |

time exits and `advanceOpen` are unchanged, and the entry refuses only its own

The reservation handle stays disabled in the service.

## What this head fixes

The gate on `4caff31f` returned `VERDICT: FAIL` with two majors. Both are fixed inside the ticket's paths.

- **Shared release policy outside the ticket's paths.** `thala_executor/order_identity.cjs` is byte-identical to `origin/main` again: the `neverSent` release of an unknown row and the reopened released identity are gone. Bot 2 now takes its hold on the book's own API (`reserve` as `active`, then `release` or `markUnknown`) and never reopens an identity. The standalone facade probe is gone from `evidence/`; its eight assertions run inside `scripts/srw1458_sell_reservation_proof.cjs`, which the ticket names.
- **A thrown reservation error left a durable exit attempt for an order never sent.** `reserveSell` turns a throw from `sellReservation.reserve()` into the same refusal as a refused reservation, because the store failed before the transport, so nothing left. Both cases clear the client order id and the send clock, and the handle-on path keeps no phantom attempt.

The self-review pass found four more, all fixed:

- A deferred exit (`retry_after`) threw from `deferExit` with the hold still taken, so every later attempt failed for capacity. The exit send settles the hold through `deferExit`'s own `unsent` hook.
- A hold could be abandoned while its id was cleared, and a retried id could resubmit for ever. Both exit send sites now ask the book (`reservationFor`) which case it is in: a released id is cleared and the attempt is spent, a kept hold keeps its id so the retry dedupes to the same units.
- A trim released its hold into a spent id and then could never send. A trim now keeps its hold across a retry — its leg id is fixed for its life — and hands it back at `finishTrim`, where the book refuses any row an order names. A refused reservation no longer closes the trim and no longer leaves a send clock with no submit.
- `reservedSellQuantity` counted a string quantity differently with no handle (5 on `origin/main`, 23 at the previous head). Each local remainder is computed before it joins, so the handle-null count is the number `origin/main` returns.

## What changed

- **Bot 2 exit and trim.** A sell reserves its units under its own attempt id and client order id before `submitOrder`. A refusal is a refusal, never a send. A send the transport refused before it left hands the units back and spends its id; a send that may have reached the broker keeps the units and is marked `unknown`.
- **Facade sell count.** The local list and the shared owner are joined by client order id: disjoint ids add, an id both know counts once at the larger outstanding, a count that is not a nonnegative safe integer is skipped, and an unreadable snapshot refuses the count.

bundles.title: Refs #2247: prove archived copies publish once and verify before restore (P52.7)
bundles.description:
Refs #2247

## What this is

The ticket's product code — `exportSession`, `archiveSegment` and `verifyRestore` — is
already on `main`, landed whole with the retention slice in #2236 (`6c303083`). What was
missing is the dedicated proof the ticket names: `scripts/p52_verifyRestore_proof.cjs`.
Writing it found one real gap in `verifyRestore`, which this PR also fixes.

So this PR is: **one new proof file, plus the fix that proof found.**

## Proof cases

Isolated synthetic data under one private temp root (`mkdtemp` at `0o700`, removed in a
`finally`); no journal, runtime owner, broker, credential or repository state is touched.
Two session days force the writer to rotate inside a kind, so the merged stream order and
the file order differ and a restore has to merge rather than concatenate.

1. **A retry verifies the existing copy without replacing it.** The published object keeps
   its inode and mtime across a retry, so nothing was rewritten. A destination that does not
   match the manifest anchor is refused and left byte-for-byte as it was.
2. **Different journals sharing an archive root preserve both copies.** Two journals that
   each hold `audit-000001.jsonl` archive into one root under their own journal and account
   namespace; both copies survive, and neither restore accepts the other's frozen counters.
3. **Restore verifies bytes, checksum, merged chain, sequence ranges and exact frozen fold
   counters**, and still merges an already evicted segment from its archive copy.
4. **A chain-valid foreign segment is refused.** A segment whose checksum, counts and ranges
   all agree with the manifest but whose records belong to another journal fails the merged
   chain, so a restore never accepts another journal's bytes.
5. **Every failed re-verification clears earlier success evidence.** Missing copy, bad
   checksum, a byte count or sequence range the manifest misdeclares, foreign chain and
   mismatched fold counters each clear the timestamp, head and ranges, and the stale success
   never authorises an eviction.

## The fix

`verifyRestore` now withdraws its three restore markers and **persists that withdrawal
before it reads a single archived byte**. The earlier version cleared them only on the
failure path, and only if a second manifest write succeeded; a journal volume that fills
while re-verifying left the old authorisation in place while the caller saw only the
verification error, so retention could later evict on stale evidence.

- Withdrawal is the first statement inside the segment lock, so every failure path — missing
  copy, bad checksum, misdeclared bytes or ranges, foreign chain, mismatched counters —
  runs after the authorisation is already gone from disk.
- A withdrawal that cannot be confirmed on disk throws

Refs #2247

## What this is

The ticket's product code — `exportSession`, `archiveSegment` and `verifyRestore` — is
already on `main`, landed whole with the retention slice in #2236 (`6c303083`). What was
missing is the dedicated proof the ticket names: `scripts/p52_verifyRestore_proof.cjs`.
Writing it found one real gap in `verifyRestore`, which this PR also fixes.

So this PR is: **one new proof file, plus the fix that proof found.**

## Proof cases

Isolated synthetic data under one private temp root (`mkdtemp` at `0o700`, removed in a
`finally`); no journal, runtime owner, broker, credential or repository state is touched.
Two session days force the writer to rotate inside a kind, so the merged stream order and
the file order differ and a restore has to merge rather than concatenate.

1. **A retry verifies the existing copy without replacing it.** The published object keeps
   its inode and mtime across a retry, so nothing was rewritten. A destination that does not
   match the manifest anchor is refused and left byte-for-byte as it was.
2. **Different journals sharing an archive root preserve both copies.** Two journals that
   each hold `audit-000001.jsonl` archive into one root under their own journal and account
   namespace; both copies survive, and neither restore accepts the other's frozen counters.
3. **Restore verifies bytes, checksum, merged chain, sequence ranges and exact frozen fold
   counters**, and still merges an already evicted segment from its archive copy.
4. **A chain-valid foreign segment is refused.** A segment whose checksum, counts and ranges
   all agree with the manifest but whose records belong to another journal fails the merged
   chain, so a restore never accepts another journal's bytes.
5. **Every failed re-verification clears earlier success evidence.** Missing copy, bad
   checksum, a byte count or sequence range the manifest misdeclares, foreign chain and
   mismatched fold counters each clear the timestamp, head and ranges,...

bundles.description:
Refs #2308

## What changed

Two rows of the refusal audit (PR #2300), nothing else:

1. `embed_test_classification` (`thala_v2_embed.js`). A card was a test when the word `TEST` or `SAMPLE` appeared anywhere in the **description**, so ordinary commentary such as `price may test support` made a readable paper card a test and the feed dropped it at `test_message`. Text identity is now two shapes: a whole-word `TEST` or `SAMPLE` in the **title**, and a body line that is exactly one of the labels the provider itself writes, the same set its own parser accepts. A line carrying `?` stays prose, so `price may test support` and `Sample?` remain readable and trade. Structured identity is read on the embed path too, from the **resolved** message identity: `test_note`, a `TEST`/`TH-TEST` prefixed id or trade id (including `platformIds.messageId`), the reserved test range in `thala_v2_card_classification.cjs`, plus harness provenance in `thala_v2_feed.js`. An allowed test card keeps `testMessage` and lane `test`, so the executor's own guard still refuses it as a real trade.
2. `embed_testing_bot_watch_only` (`thala_v2_embed.js`, open and close). A `Guru: … · TESTING` status refused the whole card. The status is now metadata: the card parses, the intent keeps `botStatus: 'TESTING'`, and it trades in paper. Test identity still comes only from the markers above.

No contract, duplicate, price or freshness guard moved. Every KEEP row is untouched, including `ambiguous_contract`, `open_leg_unreadable`, `close_leg_unreadable`, `expiry_*`, `title_symbol_mismatch`, `strike_invalid`, `entry_unreadable`, `size_*`, `stop_*`, `tp1_unreadable`, `time_exit_unreadable`, `earnings_exit_unreadable`, the six spread guards, `connected_notice`, `card_correction_or_cancel`, `missed_exit_notice`, `test_notice` and `unknown_card`.

### Notices

- An explicit test card is still not traded, and its notice names it: `test_message` renders `PAPER SKIPPED · … Why: this is a test card | No order placed`. Commentary never becomes a test, so a traded card raises no skip notice.
- **The accepted-card notice is in this ticket, per the coordinator decision on #2308 (2026-11-23 19:35 PT).** `noticeInput` carries `providerStatus` from the card that caused the order, `formatFillNotice` / `formatNoFillNotice` render `Note: provider TESTING status accepted in paper`, a card-driven close copies its **own** card status into the order it creates (so a `TESTING` close on a `LIVE` entry reports `TESTING`, and a `LIVE` close on a `TESTING` entry does not borrow the entry's status), and a protective exit has no card, so it says nothing. An accepted card whose entry never fills gets the same line on its no-fill notice. The proof asserts all four paths.
- **`SAMPLE - DO NOT TRADE` stays a test card**, also per that decision: `sample do not trade` and `test do not trade` join the existing do-not-trade phrases in the label set, and the proof pins both with zero orders.

**Effect on every open trade:** card admission only. No row is rewritten or reopened; no stored plan, quantity, ownership, stop, target or expiry exit is touched. A newly received valid CLOSE still reduces only its exactly matched owned position, and a new OPEN or CLOSE never suspends protective exits on other trades. The proof pins both against the persisted store, in the check condition and not only in its printed detail.

**Rollback:** revert the branch. Description commentary is a test again, a `TESTING` provider status refuses the card again, and the notice line disappears. No receipt, watermark or trade row needs migration either way.

## Size

Coordinator decision on #2308 (2026-11-23 19:35 PT) sets this ticket's cap at **180 changed code lines and 5 code files**, and withdraws the earlier advice to move the notice text to #2312. This head is **5 code files and 158 changed code lines**:

| File | Added | Deleted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `thala_v2_embed.js` | 20 | 3 |
| `thala_v2_feed.js` | 8 | 2 |
| `thala_v2_executor.js` | 4 | 0 |
| `discord_reply_format.js` | 4 | 0 |
| `scripts/bot1_refusal_t3_proof.cjs` | 117 | 0 |
| `evidence/SRW-2308/check-proof.md` (evidence, not code) | 167 | 0 |

The notice work that round 3 moved to #2312 is restored exactly as at `7dd829a2`, per the decision that withdrew that advice.

## Evidence on both heads

`npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit --no-fund` ran through `heavy` in this worktree and in a detached `origin/main` worktree, so both ran with `discord.js`, `ws` and `@msgpack/msgpack` installed and the saved-card corpus present.

| Command | `origin/main` `f78da296f0202f5fc3cd013c7efef8488ed3cc8f` | head `bcb4a0f9b5be33e0030c7343c32628c4a9b31231` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `node scripts/thala_v2_embed_trade_proof.cjs` | **69/69**, exit 0 | **68/69**, exit 1 |
| `node scripts/srw651_readable_notice_proof.cjs` | exit 1, `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'content')` at `seq237And244` (`:101`) | exit 1, same `TypeError`, same line |
| `node scripts/thala_v2_feed_proof.cjs` | exit 1, `ENOENT … ~/.shepherdr/inbox/thala_v2/discord_header_line.json` | exit 1, same `ENOENT`, same path |

The replay's single red is exactly the removed guard and is the only difference between the two runs:

```
head:  FAIL  safety: a close card from a TESTING bot does not sell a live position  -> 1 sells
main:  69/69 checks passed; 12 orders in the 40-card replay
```

That card carries `Guru: … · TESTING` and this ticket admits it, so the close it names is sold: that is the ticket's own RELAX row, not a runtime regression. The other two proofs fail identically on both heads, from a fixture the corpus does not contain and a notice-harness defect, so neither speaks for or against this change.

The dependency-backed runs measured `bcb4a0f9`; the commit after it changes only `evidence/SRW-2308/check-proof.md`, so the code the table describes is byte-identical to it. The publisher reads `srw/agent-check` on the pushed head.

## Proof

`node scripts/bot1_refusal_t3_proof.cjs` — fake paper broker, synthetic cards, no network, no credentials. Eight grouped checks, all passing:

```
PASS  a readable LIVE card is admitted once and its replay adds no order -> LIVE, embed_duplicate, 1 buy of qty 32, no entry notice
PASS  a TESTING card is admitted as metadata, notices it in paper and leaves the other row its plan and quantity -> 1 TSLA buy, 1 accepted notices, kept
PASS  a TESTING close card on a LIVE entry sells only the row it names, notices the status and keeps the other row -> botStatus TESTING, PAPER EXITED · AMZN 200 Call · exp Nov 6
Sold 32 contracts at an average $2.00
Why: the alert posted a CLOSE
Result: -$160.00 (-2.4%)
Position closed
Note: provider TESTING status accepted in paper
Trade EMBED-930000000000000001, 1 AMZN sell of 32 for qtyLeft 32, TSLA kept and open
PASS  protection is not suspended for the other open trade and its own exit carries no TESTING note -> 1 TSLA sell of 32 for qtyLeft 32
PASS  every structured and body-label test marker isolates a test card, its notice says test, and nothing trades -> test_message, test_message, test_message, test_message, test_message, test_message, test_message, test_message, test_message, test_message, test_message, test_message, embed_title_symbol_mismatch, embed_entry_unreadable, 0 buy
PASS  an allowed test card is delivered as a test, never as a real trade -> true, testMessage true, lane test, executor test_message
PASS  a question-marked line and plain commentary stay prose, so both cards are admitted -> true, true, 0 drops, 1 AMZN buy
PASS  an unusable price and a stale entry place no order, and an accepted TESTING card that never fills still notices the status -> quote_unavailable, stale_signal, PAPER SKIPPED · AMZN 200 Call
Why: the entry order was canceled
No contracts bought
Note: provider TESTING status accepted in paper
Trade EMBED-930000000000000025
{"ok":true,"checks":8,"failed":[],"buys":{"AMZN":1,"TSLA":1},"sells":{"AMZN":1,"TSLA":1},"tslaTrade":"closed"}
```

They cover: a readable card trades once, its replay adds no order, and its status stays metadata while commentary is not test identity; a second readable card on another contract is admitted beside the first, which keeps its persisted plan and quantity and still takes its own protective exit; a `TESTING` close sells only the row it names and its notice names the accepted status; every structured marker (`test_note`, prefixed id, prefixed `trade_id`, `platformIds.messageId`) and every provider body label — `TEST MESSAGE - NOT A TRADE`, `Test message - no trade.`, `SAMPLE - NOT A REAL TRADE`, `Reason: SAMPLE - NOT A REAL TRADE`, `SAMPLE - DO NOT TRADE`, `TEST - DO NOT TRADE` — isolates a test card with its notice naming a test and nothing traded, while an allowed test card is delivered as a test and never as a real trade; a question-marked line and plain commentary stay prose and their cards are admitted; a conflicting contract and an unreadable entry stay blocked; an unusable quote and a stale entry place no order, and a `TESTING` card that never fills still says so on its no-fill notice.

Also run on this head: `node --check` on the five code files, `git diff --check`, `node scripts/srw_review_scope.cjs` (bot1 scope, independent review required), the file-size ratchet (passes with the usual warning that the feed grew), `thala_v2_freshness_proof.cjs`, `thala_v2_watermark_proof.cjs`, `thala_v2_quiet_restart_proof.cjs`, `thala_v2_day_replay_proof.cjs`, `thala_v2_close_proof.cjs` (50 of 50, zero double sells), `srw1401_skip_record_notice_proof.cjs`, `srw717_feed_minor_proof.cjs`, `srw617_lane_regressions.cjs`, `THALA_V2_EMBED_TRADE=1 srw776_owner_rule_proof.cjs`, `heavy/srw827_lane_contract_proof.cjs`.

### Self-review

Independent review rounds ran with the gate's own model `gpt-6.2-astra`, selected with `~/Code/mac-ops/coordinator/bin/models.py first review risky` (the relative `coordinator/bin/models.py` path exits 2 in this checkout). Their critical and major findings, and where each landed:

- Structured test identity was lost before execution (raw envelope only, and `allowTest` delivered as a real trade): fixed by classifying the resolved identity and marking the intent before lane selection.
- The description heuristic missed provider labels and turned `Sample?` into a label: fixed with the provider's literal label set plus a prose guard for question marks and sentences.
- The persisted open-trade invariant and the admitted `TESTING` close had no evidence: both proved against the store, with the unrelated trade kept and later protected.
- Size: the coordinator's 180-line, 5-file decision closes this ticket's size stop; this head is 158 lines.
- Dependency-backed evidence: recorded on both heads with both SHAs.
- The accepted-card notice: restored here after the decision withdrew the advice to defer it, with assertions on the entry, close, no-fill and protective-exit paths.

## Left for later

- **Minor · Label set is wider than the provider's.** `modernAlertLabel` in the provider parser accepts four forms; `TEST_LABELS` accepts those plus bare `TEST`/`SAMPLE` and `NOT A TRADE`. With punctuation stripped, a heading such as `📝 Test:` isolates a real card, which on a close card would drop a sell. No saved card is affected.
- **Minor · Replay is proven within one feed instance.** A replay after a restart walks the same path but is not exercised here.
- **Minor · Protective exits carry no note.** Deliberate: only the card that caused an order describes its own status.


## Builder check

This repo's `scripts/check.sh` is heavy and the Mac check publisher owns it, so the builder does not run it.

Builder check: PASS 7412a53e2e31fa96dce810d633c3eed7e55ff233

- Re-verified by the builder on this head: ticket proof 8/8, `{"ok":true,"checks":8,"failed":[],"buys":{"AMZN":1,"TSLA":1},"sells":{"AMZN":1,"TSLA":1},"tslaTrade":"closed"}`; scope 5 code files and 158 changed code lines against the coordinator's 180-line, 5-file decision; syntax and `git diff --check` clean.
- The coordinator's independent verdict is still required; this line records the check, not a review pass.

A line carrying `?` stays prose, so `price may test support` and `Sample?` remain readable and trade. An allowed test card keeps `testMessage` and lane `test`, so the executor's own guard still refuses it as a real trade.
2. `embed_testing_bot_watch_only` (`thala_v2_embed.js`, open and close). A `Guru: … · TESTING` status refused the whole card. The status is now metadata: the card parses, the intent keeps `botStatus: 'TESTING'`, and it trades in paper. Test identity still comes only from the markers above.

bundles.description:
Refs #1473

P39c: activate additional paper accounts last. Paper only, M6. The capability ships **disabled by default** and is activated separately after qualification. No deployment from this PR.

## What it does

Activation is a separate step from configuration. An account listed in `paper_accounts.json` is configured; it receives entries only after its activation record exists.

- `paper_account_list.js` owns the contract: a pure planner, an append-only activation ledger (`activate` / `receipt` / `rollback`), and the gate the fan-out consults.
- One additional account at a time, in configured order. The next candidate is the first enabled follower with no activation record, so a refusal never skips ahead. The previous activation must carry a passing receipt before the next one starts.
- Every qualification is a fact the operator supplies: exclusive ownership, durable storage, broker capability, both bots' exit drills, and measured capacity. A missing or unknown value refuses and names the gap.
- A new activation always starts `pending`; only a separate receipt record can make it `pass`. The raw append is not exported, and read/validate/append run inside one lock.
- `paper_account_fanout.js` consults the gate in `ineligibleReason`. A gated account with no pending attempt is refused before any request. A gated account that still has an `intent` or `unknown` attempt keeps reconciling it: the lookup runs, the attempt stays `unknown` rather than becoming terminal, and only the new POST is withheld. Exits never consult the gate.
- The gate re-reads the ledger and re-resolves the account's current verified registry binding on every call, so a rollback takes effect at the next entry without a restart, and a replaced or tombstoned identity cannot inherit an old activation.
- Admission also compares the activated identity with the identity the submission credentials prove. The configured binding is selected by `account.name`, so it keeps naming the old approved account after the credentials behind that name are rotated to a different paper account. The fan-out already reads `/v2/account` for sizing; that read returns the broker account id, and the gate resolves its fingerprint through the registry. A fresh entry whose credentials resolve to a different account is refused `account_identity_mismatch` before any order request. The check runs after older-attempt reconciliation, so a pending order is still adopted, and it fails closed when no verifier is supplied.
- `shared_staging_budget.js` gains a read-only `headroom()` that charges nothing and reports the same routine limit `take` enforces.
- `cell_boot_guard.js` gains an optional `activationRequired` refusal for an unactivated account.
- `paper_service.js` builds the gate only from a complete config and never in Discord-only mode. A requested but incomplete config installs a deny-all gate instead of falling back to "every follower eligible".

With `PAPER_ADDITIONAL_ACCOUNT_ACTIVATION` unset there is no gate, no ledger read and no new log line.

## Proof

`node scripts/srw1473_additional_accounts_proof.cjs` — frozen `evidence/SRW-1473/inputs.json` and hand-derived `build-expected.json`, both hashed against `build-manifest.json` before anything runs. Receipt: `evidence/SRW-1473/build-receipt.json` at `6325ed2b378f2c803e9e8957f903c29a598484f7`.

One live gate is built once and reused for the whole sequence, so the proof shows a rollback taking effect without a restart. Every negative case goes through the real activation writer and then uses the ledger that writer produced.

Cases: rehearsal with nothing activated; activate A pending; A receipt passes; activate B; rollback order; rollback B through the same gate object; re-activate and replay with unchanged client ids; eight unproved qualifications; capacity 4 vs 3 from the real budget owner; unreadable ledger; tombstoned identity; credential replacement that keeps the name and binding; rollback reconciliation of an older pending attempt; bypass attempts; gated recovery that stays `unknown` then reconciles to `accepted` with no second POST; boot guard; service config; exit path byte-identical with and without the gate.

Mutation checks on the real modules fail the proof: dropping the identity check, dropping the credential-identity check, running the credential check before older-attempt reconciliation, caching the ledger read, making the refusal terminal, dropping the `previous_unproven` rule, and removing the fan-out gate each change a frozen case.

Existing proofs re-run green: `srw322`, `srw416`, `srw601`, `srw1439`, `srw1440`, `srw1472`, `srw1573` (50/50), `test_paper_people_accounts.js` (74 assertions), `test_srw15_order_path_review.js`, `srw713` entry-guard and broker-admission.

## Self-review

Reviewer: `astra-sub` (gpt-6.2-astra), selected with `python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review risky`. Verdict on the first pass: FAIL, 7 major and 2 minor, no critical. All were fixed in `cbe10d04`:

1. **Major** — a requested but incomplete config left every follower eligible. Now installs a deny-all gate; only an explicit flag-off omits it.
2. **Major** — a rollback left the running service authorized to send. The gate now re-reads the ledger per call, and the proof uses one gate object across the whole sequence.
3. **Major** — activation followed the display name across identities. The gate now compares the recorded `accountId` with the current verified registry binding; a tombstone denies at once.
4. **Major** — callers could bypass qualification and the previous-receipt rule. A new activation must start `pending`, the raw append is no longer exported, a receipt or rollback must name its activation's identity, and the write is serialized by a lock.
5. **Major** — concurrent activations could invalidate the ledger. Read, validate and append now run inside one lock, and a repeated activation of the same identity is idempotent on replay.
6. **Major** — an activation hold could end recovery of a pending attempt. The gate no longer short-circuits the lookup, and the refusal is a transient skip, so an unknown attempt stays unknown and later reconciles.
7. **Major** — the proof could pass with broken qualification or broken exits. Negative cases now drive the real writer and use its ledger; the exit case compares gated and ungated runs and asserts the reducer's own decision.
8. **Minor** — headroom could exceed usable capacity after a storage failure. Documented as remaining quota; writable storage is a separate qualification fact.
9. **Minor** — Discord-only startup logged an activation diagnostic with the flag unset. Suppressed unless activation was requested.

Second pass, on the `origin/main` merge at `136a1a8f`: reviewer `astra-sub` (gpt-6.2-astra), selected with `python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review standard`. Verdict PASS, no critical, major or minor findings. It confirmed the `headroom()`/`take()` readiness difference is benign, that no caller reaches a null budget under P51, and that the merge is safe to push with activation disabled. Nothing to fix, so nothing changed after it.

Third pass, on the gate finding at `136a1a8f`: reviewer `astra-sub` (gpt-6.2-astra), selected with `python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review standard`. Verdict request changes, 1 major and 1 minor, no critical. Both fixed in `f3a8489d`:

1. **Major** — the credential check ran before `resolveOtherSubmissions`, so a new command after a rollback refused with `account_identity_mismatch` and left an older broker order unreconciled. The check now runs after the older-attempt reconciliation and after the activation refusal, so a pending order is still adopted and a rolled-back account still reports `account_not_activated`. New frozen case `rollbackReconciliation` fails if the check moves back.
2. **Minor** — the proof duplicated the service credential resolver, so its source check would still pass if the service computed the fingerprint and then looked up the configured name binding. The resolver is now `createCredentialIdentityResolver` in `paper_account_list.js`, used by both the service and the proof, and the proof asserts it uses the shared one.

The gate finding itself is fixed by the credential-identity check. The proof's `credentialReplacement` case activates A, rotates A's credentials to a second key pair for C's paper account while keeping A's name and binding, and shows the control run posts 1 while the rotated run posts 0 with status `skipped`. Disabling the check makes the rotated run post 1 and be `accepted`, so the proof fails.

3. **Minor, found while checking the receipt** — the receipt pass/fail line used `JSON.stringify`, which is key-order sensitive, while the assertion used `deepEqual`, which is not. A reordered expected object recorded `FAIL` in the receipt while the proof passed. Both now compare canonically, and the receipt records `PASS` at `6325ed2b`.

## Left for later

- The exit case proves the gate never touches exits and that the exit reducer reaches its own decision for a rolled-back account, but it does not hold a live position through the rollback. `scripts/srw416_multi_account_exit_proof.cjs` remains the held-position exit evidence and passes unchanged.
- `scripts/srw_review_scope.cjs` returns 2 (Opus review required) for this diff. That is the Coordinator's gate decision, not a builder claim.
- Activation blockers recorded in `docs/parity/multi-account.md`: follower fan-out requests are still uncharged (P51), the service has no qualification evidence of its own, the capacity reading is local rather than the cross-process owner, and the cell boot check trusts its caller.

## Branch update

Merged `origin/main` (`5e8c2b1b`, SRW-1604 P51 per-key broker budget) into the branch at `136a1a8f`. The merge was textually clean and the tree is identical to the clean-merge result. Main touched `alpaca_paper_execution.js` and `shared_staging_budget.js`; this branch touched `shared_staging_budget.js` `headroom()` and the activation path, so the interaction was reviewed rather than assumed.

- `headroom()` still agrees with `take()` in both P51 paths. With P51 off it reports the 77 slots open to ordinary Bot 1 entries and excludes the three readiness slots; with P51 on it matches `take()` for `entry` and `report` inside the selected key partition.
- The only direct caller of `budget.headroom()` is the proof. The planner takes a supplied number, the service shadow router defaults to unmeasured, and the activation and boot guards use identity records, so the new null-budget case under P51 reaches no caller.
- A follower exit engine can start with a null default budget because each request selects its budget from the credentials it sends and passes an explicit group.

Proofs re-run green on the merged head: `scripts/srw1473_additional_accounts_proof.cjs` (PASS at `136a1a8f`), `evidence/SRW-1604/p51_bot1_partition_proof.cjs` (7/7), `srw601`, `srw416`, `srw1216`. `node --check` passes on every touched JS file.

Two proofs fail identically on `origin/main` and are not in the gate manifest, so they are pre-existing and not caused by this merge: `scripts/srw699_shared_bot_budget_proof.cjs` (ENOTEMPTY on temp-dir cleanup) and `scripts/srw755_three_trade_budget_proof.cjs` (ERR_ASSERTION).

## Check

Builder check: PASS cd1843d706025863a43944641d5ed3d25e2824b3

The exact-head `heavy scripts/check.sh` gate is the Mac check publisher's `srw/agent-check` status on this ready PR; this builder did not run it, per the repository rule, so no `CHECK: PASS` is claimed here.

@@ -238,3 +238,120 @@ Mutation checks on the real module failed the proof: dividing no share among fol
 
 The capability is off by default, so with the flag unset no open trade changes. With the flag on, the router only reads the registry and the value reader's cached rows and writes log lines. Bot 1 primary lane trades, Bot 2, fan-out ledger records, follower exit lanes, pending attempts and client ids are all untouched in both cases, and exits keep their existing owners and MARKET fallback. Rollback is to unset `PAPER_SHADOW_ACCOUNT_ROUTING`; there is no state to reconcile because the router writes none.
 
+
+## P39c additional-account activation (#1473)
+
+Refs #1473 and #1387. Design contract for M6. Paper only. The capability stays off until P54 (#1464) qualifies compatibility and rollback, and until the paper-service activation gate is separately proved. This section changes no order path: it adds one admission check in front of the existing fan-out entry path.
+
+### What activation is
+
+Activation is a separate step from configuration. An account listed in `paper_accounts.json` is configured; it receives entries only after its activation record exists. The two are deliberately different facts, so a configured account cannot start trading because a file was edited.
+
+`paper_account_list.js` owns the whole contract. It exports a pure planner, an append-only ledger, and the gate the fan-out consults. Nothing else decides who is active.
+
+| Part | Behaviour |
+| --- | --- |
+| `planAdditionalAccountActivation` | pure; returns one decision per configured account and the single next candidate |
+| `readActivationLedger` | reads the append-only ledger and derives the active set; an unreadable ledger activates nothing |
+| `activateAdditionalAccount` | runs the planner and refuses unless that account's decision is `activate`; then appends one record |
+| `recordActivationReceipt` | appends the post-activation receipt that lets the next account start |
+| `rollbackAdditionalAccount` | appends one rollback record for the most recently activated account |
+| `activationGate` | `({ read, identityFor }) => (account) => boolean`; re-reads the ledger and re-resolves the account's current verified identity on every call |
+| `additionalAccountActivationConfig` | needs `PAPER_ADDITIONAL_ACCOUNT_ACTIVATION=1`, `SRW_ACCOUNT_ACTIVATION_LEDGER`, `SRW_ACCOUNT_REGISTRY_FILE`, `SRW_ACCOUNT_ENVIRONMENT` and `PAPER_ADDITIONAL_ACCOUNT_BINDINGS`; any missing or invalid part returns a reason and no gate |
+
+A new activation always starts `pending`. Only a separate receipt record can make it `pass`, so a caller cannot activate one account and immediately unlock the next. The raw append is private: the only writers are the three functions above, and each one runs read, validation and append inside one lock, so two operators cannot write a sequence that replay has to reject.
+
+### One account at a time
+
+The next candidate is the first enabled follower, in configured order, with no activation record. A refusal never skips ahead, so a broken earlier account blocks later ones instead of being stepped over. The previous activation must carry a passing receipt before the next one starts, which is what makes the sequence a chain rather than a batch.
+
+| Decision | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `refuse:disabled` | the account is not enabled |
+| `refuse:primary_lane_owns` | the primary lane keeps its own executor and is never activated |
+| `refuse:binding_unproven`, `refuse:account_unregistered`, `refuse:account_tombstoned` | no verified registry binding |
+| `active:pass`, `active:pending` | already activated, with its post-activation receipt |
+| `hold:not_next` | an earlier enabled follower is still unactivated |
+| `hold:previous_unproven` | the last activation has no passing receipt yet |
+| `hold:qualification_missing` | no qualification record for this account |
+| `hold:ownership_unproven` | exclusive writer not proved |
+| `hold:storage_unproven` | durable storage not proved |
+| `hold:broker_unproven` | broker capability not proved |
+| `hold:bot1_exit_drill_unproven`, `hold:bot2_exit_drill_unproven` | a bot's exit drill has not passed |
+| `hold:capacity_unmeasured`, `hold:capacity_insufficient` | the measured headroom is unknown or below one fresh entry |
+| `activate` | every check passed; this is the one account that may be activated now |
+
+Every qualification is a fact the operator supplies. A missing or unknown value refuses; nothing defaults to proved. That is the ticket's stop condition in code: unproved ownership, storage durability, broker capability or staging capacity blocks activation and names the blocking evidence.
+
+### Capacity comes from the real budget owner
+
+`shared_staging_budget.js` gains a read-only `headroom()`. It charges nothing, writes nothing and cannot refill a window, so measuring can never mint capacity. It reports the same routine limit `take` enforces, including the three-request bot 1 reservation, so the reading can never overstate what a send may use. The activation capacity pass compares that number with one fresh follower entry, which costs 4 HTTP requests on the existing path.
+
+The reading is remaining quota, not proof that a charge can be persisted. A read-only budget directory still reports headroom while the first routine `take()` fails to save. Writable storage is a separate qualification fact (`storage: durable`), and P51 owns the cross-process owner that makes the reading authoritative.
+
+### Where the gate sits
+
+`paper_account_fanout.js` consults the gate in `ineligibleReason`. A gated account with no pending attempt is refused before any sizing, credential or broker work, so it makes zero HTTP requests. A gated account that still has an `intent` or `unknown` attempt is not short-circuited: the lookup and the other-attempt reconciliation run first, and only the new POST is withheld. The refusal is a transient skip, so the pending attempt stays `unknown` instead of becoming terminal `not_found`.
+
+| Path | Effect of the gate |
+| --- | --- |
+| New entry, no pending attempt | refused `account_not_activated`; zero requests, one `skipped` ledger record |
+| New entry, an older attempt still pending | the older attempt is looked up and settled first, then the new entry is refused |
+| Recovery of a pending `intent` or `unknown` | the lookup still runs; a found order is adopted with no send, and an absent order stays `unknown` with no repost |
+| Already `accepted` | `already_placed` with the original client id; no send |
+| Exit, trim, close, stop, flatten | never consulted; the existing exit reducer keeps its owner and its MARKET fallback |
+
+The gate re-reads the ledger on every call, so a rollback takes effect at the next entry without a restart. It also compares the recorded `accountId` with the account's current verified registry binding, so replacing an account's credentials with a different paper account cannot inherit the old activation, and a tombstone denies at once.
+
+`cell_boot_guard.js` gains an optional `activationRequired` input. When it is set, a cell whose paper account is not in `activatedAlpacaAccountIds` is refused `account_not_activated` before any registry write. Absent, the guard is unchanged. The caller supplies both the switch and the list, so this is a second door, not independent proof of activation.
+
+`paper_service.js` builds the gate only from a complete config and never in Discord-only mode. A requested but incomplete configuration installs a deny-all gate instead of falling back to "every follower eligible", so a missing ledger path or malformed bindings cannot silently enable entries. With the flag unset the service behaves exactly as before: no gate, no ledger read, no new log line.
+
+### Rollback
+
+Rollback is last-in-first-out: the activation under test is the one to undo. It appends one record and touches no order state, so working orders keep their client ids and cumulative fills, the fan-out ledger is untouched, and the exit lanes keep running for the deactivated account. Because the gate re-reads the ledger, the running service stops admitting that account at its next entry. Re-activating the same account later reuses the same client ids, and a repeated command returns `already_placed` with zero sends.
+
+Disable new admissions before rollback, reconcile working orders through the existing owner, and retain reservations until terminal evidence. Preserve journal cursors, client ids and cumulative fills. Qualify old-reader compatibility before resuming the old policy. If the export cannot preserve the required history, rollback is capability-off on the new binary.
+
+### Build proof
+
+`node scripts/srw1473_additional_accounts_proof.cjs` reuses the frozen `evidence/SRW-1473/inputs.json` and checks it and the hand-derived `evidence/SRW-1473/build-expected.json` against `evidence/SRW-1473/build-manifest.json`. With `--receipt` on a clean checkout it writes `evidence/SRW-1473/build-receipt.json`. It drives the real `loadPaperAccountList`, `bindPaperAccounts`, the account registry, `createPaperAccountValueReader`, `createPaperAccountFanOut`, `createBudget`, the activation planner, writer and ledger, and `bootCell`. The only stand-in is a credential-free fake broker.
+
+One live gate is built once and reused for the whole sequence, so the proof shows a rollback taking effect without a restart. Every negative case goes through the real activation writer and then uses the ledger that writer produced, so a writer that ignored the planner would leave the account active and the fan-out would post.
+
+The rehearsal uses one primary account P and three followers: A (balanced, 100,000), B (conservative, 50,000) and C (aggressive, 25,000). The command buys an option at 2.50, so one contract costs 250 dollars.
+
+| Case | Expected and observed |
+| --- | --- |
+| Nothing activated | P `primary_lane_owns`; A `activate`; B and C `hold:not_next`; 0 POSTs, 0 requests |
+| Activate A with a pending receipt | A `active:pending`; B `hold:previous_unproven`; C `hold:not_next`; 1 POST, A 8 contracts, 4 requests for A and 0 for B and C |
+| A receipt passes | A `active:pass`; B `activate`; C `hold:not_next` |
+| Activate B | A `active:pass`; B `active:pending`; C `hold:previous_unproven`; 2 POSTs, A 8 and B 2, 4 requests each |
+| Roll back A while B is last | `not_last_activated` |
+| Roll back B through the same gate object | A `active:pass`; B `activate`; C `hold:not_next`; 1 POST, A 8; B's two ledger records byte-identical |
+| Re-activate B and replay the same command | A and B `already_placed`; 0 POSTs; B's client id unchanged |
+| Eight unproved qualifications | the writer refuses each with its own reason and 0 POSTs |
+| Capacity from the real budget owner | 73 recorded charges give headroom 4 and an activation; 74 give headroom 3 and `capacity_insufficient` with 0 POSTs |
+| Unreadable ledger | `activation_ledger_unreadable`; the gate allows 0 accounts; 0 POSTs |
+| Tombstoned identity | the gate admits A before the tombstone and denies it after; 0 POSTs |
+| Bypass attempts | a `pass` receipt on a new activation is refused; the raw append is not exported; a duplicate activation is refused and the ledger stays readable |
+| Gated recovery | A's first POST is `unknown`; after rollback the same command stays `unknown` with 0 POSTs; once the broker exposes the order it is adopted `accepted` with 0 POSTs |
+| Boot guard | an unactivated account is refused `account_not_activated`; an activated one boots `ready` |
+| Service config | unset is `off`; each partial config returns its reason; a complete config gives a gate |
+| Exit path | a sell fan-out returns 3 results, calls the gate 0 times, produces 0 `account_not_activated` statuses, and is byte-identical with and without the gate |
+
+Mutation checks on the real modules failed the proof: dropping the identity check changed the tombstone case, caching the ledger read changed the activate-A case, making the refusal terminal changed the recovery case, dropping the `previous_unproven` rule changed the activate-A case, and removing the fan-out gate changed the rehearsal.
+
+### Activation blockers that remain
+
+These are facts about the current code. None blocks merging this disabled contract; each blocks switching the capability on.
+
+1. Follower fan-out requests are still not charged to a budget. `paper_account_fanout.js` `send` calls `fetch` directly. P51 must charge every fan-out request before activation.
+2. The service has no qualification evidence. The planner needs exit-drill, ownership, storage, broker and capacity facts that only an operator run supplies, so the service enforces the ledger and the planner decides what may enter it.
+3. The capacity reading is a local file reading, not the cross-process owner P51 requires. It is remaining quota for one process, not a provider claim, and it does not prove the charge can be persisted.
+4. The cell boot check trusts the caller's switch and account list. It is a second door, not independent proof of activation.
+5. Paper-service capability, storage durability, restart topology and the three-account staging rehearsal are separate activation evidence. This build proves the local path only.
+
+### Open trades and rollback for the build
+
+The capability is off by default, so with the flag unset no open trade changes. With the flag on, an unactivated follower receives no entry and an activated one uses the existing fan-out path unchanged. Bot 1 primary lane trades, Bot 2, fan-out ledger records, follower exit lanes, pending attempts and client ids are untouched in both cases. Rollback is to append a rollback record for the account under test, or to unset `PAPER_ADDITIONAL_ACCOUNT_ACTIVATION`; the ledger keeps every client id and cumulative fill either way.

## What it does

Activation is a separate step from configuration. An account listed in `paper_accounts.json` is configured; it receives entries only after its activation record exists.

- `paper_account_list.js` owns the contract: a pure planner, an append-only activation ledger (`activate` / `receipt` / `rollback`), and the gate the fan-out consults.
- One additional account at a time, in configured order. The next candidate is the first enabled follower with no activation record, so a refusal never skips ahead. The previous activation must carry a passing receipt before the next one starts.

- A new activation always starts `pending`; only a separate receipt record can make it `pass`. The raw append is not exported, and read/validate/append run inside one lock.
- `paper_account_fanout.js` consults the gate in `ineligibleReason`. A gated account with no pending attempt is refused before any request. A gated account that still has an `intent` or `unknown` attempt keeps reconciling it: the lookup runs, the attempt stays `unknown` rather than becoming terminal, and only the new POST is withheld. Exits never consult the gate.
- The gate re-reads the ledger and re-resolves the account's current verified registry binding on every call, so a rollback takes effect at the next entry without a restart, and a replaced or tombstoned identity cannot inherit an old activation.
- Admission also compares the activated identity with the identity the submission credentials prove. The configured binding is selected by `account.name`, so it keeps naming the old approved account ...

bundles.title: Refs #1422: Bot 2 target ladder and break-even (off by default)
bundles.description:
Refs #1422

## What this does

With `trading.target_ladder` true (off by default), a Bot 2 trade freezes a rung list in `lane_config` at entry. Each rung is a percent above the fill and a share of the original position. A fresh bid at a rung's price queues that rung's sell through the existing trim reducer, so a signal trim, a rung and a full exit never work beside each other. The ladder advances only when the current rung's cumulative fills reach its allocation. A rung whose allocation covers the residual is the trade's own full exit. Break-even is written only after target one completes, is durable before it is used, and never lowers a stop. Cumulative fills are read from the recorded leg identities, so a restart conserves the residual. An unreadable or wrong-price persisted ladder is dropped and never rebuilt, leaving the single target and the stop in force.

Eligibility is frozen in `lane_config` at entry (`target_ladder: true`), so turning the capability on later never gives an open trade a ladder. The ladder is built only from a terminal entry fill, and the last rung takes the rounding residue when the shares cover the position.

## Files

- `bot2/trade_machine.js`: the ladder plan, the fill-time freeze, the ladder-aware target check, the rung queue in the trim reducer, the break-even write, the full-exit rung marker, and the `snapshotLane` freeze.
- `scripts/srw1422_target_ladder_proof.cjs`: 36 scenarios against a credential-free fake broker.
- `evidence/SRW-1422/ladder_inputs.json`: the pinned sanitized input.
- `evidence/SRW-1422/check-proof.md`: the proof receipt, expected outcomes, mutation checks, existing proofs, blast radius and rollback.

## Proof

`node scripts/srw1422_target_ladder_proof.cjs` at `1a8f1591`: 36 scenarios pass. The receipt is in `evidence/SRW-1422/check-proof.md`. 22 mutation reverts all fail the proof.

Existing exit-path and trim proofs pass, including `scripts/srw1418_trim_at_bid_proof.cjs` (18 scenarios), `bot2/srw792_partial_exit.proof.cjs`, `bot2/srw1290_exit_market_fallback.proof.cjs`, `bot2/srw755_restart_ownership.proof.cjs`, `bot2/srw755_saved_only_recovery.proof.cjs`, `bot2/trailing_crash.proof.cjs`, `scripts/srw755_trim_review_proof.cjs`, `scripts/srw993_exit_retry_proof.cjs`, `scripts/srw1416_account_freeze_proof.cjs` and `scripts/srw1103_lane3_execution_proof.cjs`. The proofs that fail identically on clean `origin/main` are listed in the receipt and were not edited.

## Self-review

Reviewer: `astra-sub` (`gpt-6.2-astra`), chosen with `python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review router`. The review found no critical issues and eight major issues. All eight are fixed in `e24e41ba`:

1. **Activation changed an open trade.** Eligibility is now frozen in `lane_config` at entry (`target_ladder: true`), and `ladderFromConfig` requires that marker. Turning the capability on later does not create a ladder. Proof: "turning the capability on does not give an open trade a ladder".
2. **A fully allocated ladder could leave a contract with no price target.** The last rung now takes the rounding residue when the shares cover the position, and the ladder is built only from a terminal entry fill. Proof: "a 5-contract 50/25/25 ladder sells 2, 1 and 2 and leaves nothing open" and "a growing partial entry fill builds the ladder from the terminal fill".
3. **Persisted ladder validation permitted a wrong-price sell and unbounded work.** `ladderValid` now compares every rung price and allocation to the frozen plan, and cumulative fills are summed from the recorded `leg_ids` instead of a counter. Proof: "a persisted rung price that disagrees with the frozen plan is dropped".
4. **Dropping a corrupt ladder lowered an applied break-even stop.** `entryFill` now keeps the last durable stop when `target_ladder_dropped` is set. Proof: "dropping a corrupt ladder keeps the break-even stop".
5. **A later rung could sell after the break-even write failed.** `ladderBreakEven` returns whether the required stop is durable, and `captureLadderRung` holds every later rung until it is. Protective exits keep being evaluated. Proof: "a failed break-even write holds every later rung".
6. **A full-exit retry lost fills from the rung's cumulative count.** The full exit records `target_ladder_exit_rung`, and `ladderSync` sums every attempt's fill. Proof: "a full-exit retry counts every attempt against the rung it completes".
7. **Rollback could submit a new ladder order.** A working rung is reconciled and finished, and an unsent queued rung is superseded, when the capability is off. Proof: "turning the capability off does not submit a replacement rung order" and "turning the capability off supersedes an unsent queued rung".
8. **The required queued stop-edit scenario was missing.** The proof now drives the break-even write in both event orders and asserts the durable level, the remaining position and the working sell count after a restart. Proof: "a completed target one writes the break-even in both event orders and a restart keeps it".

The one minor (the "partial entry fill" scenario started from a terminal fill) is fixed: the scenario is renamed to "a two-contract position cannot form a 50/25/25 ladder", and a separate growing-partial-fill scenario exercises the terminal-fill rule.

### Gate round: findings 5 and 8

The gate on `f313a8b1` returned FAIL on two majors. Both are fixed, and the self-review of that fix found two more majors, also fixed.

- **Finding 5, a rung that covers the rest took the full exit while the stop edit was not durable.** `targetExitDue` now reads the same condition `ladderBreakEven` writes, through a new pure predicate `ladderBreakEvenPending`, so a ladder full exit is held until the break-even stop is durable. Stop and time exits are unchanged and still take priority. Proof: "a failed break-even write holds the rung that would take the rest through the full exit".
- **Finding 8, the combined restart case was missing.** The proof now drives a broker partial fill of a rung while a signal trim is pending, the signal trim taking its half, the rung residual completing rung one, the stop edit being queued by a failed write, and a restart landing it. Proof: "a partial rung fill with a pending signal trim queues the stop edit and a restart lands it", plus the extended signal-first case in "partial target fill, queued break-even and signal trim in both event orders conserve the residual".
- **Self-review major, a saved target decision bypassed the guard.** `exitReason` returned a persisted `exit_reason: target` before the ladder check, so a row written by an earlier build could still sell the remainder with the stop at 1.00. The saved target is now revalidated and held while the break-even is pending; stop, time and alert exits keep their own reason. A working exit order is reconciled before `exitReason` runs, so only an unsent decision is held. Proof: "a saved target decision does not sell the remainder while the stop edit is not durable".
- **Self-review major, the signal-first partial fill never reached break-even.** That case now runs through the residual rung fill, the failed stop write and the restart, and asserts the durable stop, the exact remaining quantity and no duplicate sells.

### Gate round: recovery after a cancelled partial entry

The gate on `deba2047` returned FAIL on two majors. Both are fixed, and the self-review of that fix found one more major, also fixed.

- **Major, recovery skipped the target ladder after a partial entry.** Saved-only recovery recomputed protection only when the fill quantity or average price changed, and the ladder also required a terminal entry. A six-contract entry that fills four and is then cancelled at the deadline changes only the status, so the four open contracts kept the single target and the original stop and skipped the configured trims and break-even. The ladder is now built from the terminal entry status, before the stop is recomputed, so the P27 guard still sees it. A config that cannot form a ladder adds no ledger write. Proof: "a saved-only recovery builds the ladder when the broker cancels the unfilled remainder".
- **Major, the required recovery proof had no passing result.** `scripts/srw1439_account_adoption_replay_proof.cjs` now has a recorded pass on the clean `1a8f1591` checkout, quoted in the receipt with its counts and the note that its rewrite of `evidence/SRW-1439/replay-receipt.json` was reverted because that file belongs to SRW-1439.
- **Self-review major, a target latched before the ladder existed sold the whole position.** The stop assessment runs before the entry reducer, so a first recovery quote at the old single target latches `exit_reason: target` before the ladder is built. The ladder then kept that decision and the full exit sold all four contracts, skipping rung one and break-even. Building the ladder now clears an unsent target decision so the active rung decides; a working exit keeps its own reason. Proof: "a saved-only recovery revalidates a target latched before the ladder exists", which fails on the pre-fix code with `exit_reason` still `target`.

Device, handset and live-service testing is waived for this ticket (Shyam 2026-11-14: "no testing is needed lets just finish backlog building everything"). No device or live case was run, and none is claimed.

## Builder check

Builder check: PASS b98b2e0ffc366d598c179d269625569d51953aa8

The full release gate is the Mac check publisher's `srw/agent-check` on this ready PR. Locally at `1a8f1591` I ran the 36-scenario proof, `node --check` on both changed files, `scripts/srw_review_scope.cjs`, the account-adoption replay, and the 30 existing exit-path, trim, restart and ownership proofs listed in the receipt; all pass. `scripts/check.sh` was not run here, per the repository rule.

## Left for later

- `bot2/lane_control_schema.js` does not yet accept `targets` or `break_even_after_first`; P27b (#1423) adds those keys and the lane editor fields. Until then a committed lane config cannot carry a ladder, so the freeze in `snapshotLane` is inert in production. The proof drives the frozen `lane_config` directly.
- The file-size ratchet warns that `bot2/trade_machine.js` grew by 13,647 bytes and the proof is 1,384 bytes over the budget. The ticket names that module as the owner, so the ladder lives there rather than in a new module.
- Activation waits for P54 (#1464). This PR builds and merges the capability disabled by default.
- The receipt still lists six checks that need `--heavy`, two that need `ws`, and eleven that fail identically on the base. Those are environment limits of this worktree, not results of this change, and they are recorded as such rather than run.

## Rollback

Turn off `trading.target_ladder` and let the working rung leg reach a terminal state before reverting. The frozen `target_ladder` and its cumulative fills stay on the row. An old reader ignores `target_ladder`, `target_ladder_dropped` and `target_ladder_exit_rung` and reads the single `target_level`, which the ladder records as its last rung price.

bundles.title: Refs #1617: durable hold and single-use reservation, built disabled (P42.1)
bundles.description:
Refs #1617. Re-cut of #1615 (P42.1). Milestone M6. Paper only, built disabled.

## What this builds

The store-and-provider half of approve mode, and nothing else:

- **`thala_control_contract.cjs`** — `approve_entry` in `COMMANDS` and its payload shape: `signalId` (bounded alphabet, ≤128) and `expectedDigest` (64 lowercase hex), and no other key.
- **`thala_control_store.cjs`** — the `entry_approvals` table (states `awaiting_approval`, `approved`, `consumed`, `refused`, `expired`) and every transition over it: `holdEntry`, `getEntryApproval`, `listEntryApprovals`, `reserveEntryApproval`, `refuseEntryApproval`, `settleEntryApproval`, `expireEntryApprovals`. Plus a store clock the caller may pin, and `approval` added to `scopedExit`.
- **`thala_control_coordinator.cjs`** — the three provider methods the executor reads (`holdEntry`, `getEntryApproval`, `settleEntryApproval`), `entryApprovalEnabled`, `approval` in `scopedExit`, and a `storeClock` passthrough.

Not in scope, by the ticket: the executor's admission path (P42.2), the coordinator's dispatch and reconciler (P42.3), the dashboard projection and capability wiring (P42.4).

## The two gate findings from the #1615 review

1. **A pending or unknown approval is scoped to its own signal.** `approval` is in `scopedExit` in both the store and the coordinator, so a timed-out approval never clears the store's ready flag, never freezes a new command, never blocks recovery, and never sends an executing approval through the manual-exit reconciler. Cases P1–P6.
2. **Only a hold that no send was ever reserved for is expired.** `expireEntryApprovals` selects `state='awaiting_approval'` only, inside a write transaction. An `approved` row may have an order in flight, so it is settled from the executor's own answer and never expired out from under a POST. Case E1.

## The gate finding on #1635

**An approval for an expired hold could reserve its replacement.** `holdEntry` could reopen an expired signal with the same digest and a later `expiresAt`, so an operator who submitted the original card after redelivery could reserve the replacement even though the window they saw had closed.

The window is part of the facts the digest signs, so the store now refuses a hold whose stored expiry differs from `facts.windowEndsAt`. A later window is different facts and therefore a different digest, so the same-digest reopen is impossible and the approval the operator already saw stays stale.

The comparison is against the canonical ISO form, `new Date(expiresAt).toISOString()`, not `Date.parse`. `Date.parse` accepts a window without a timezone, which parses to a different instant in a different process, so the same digest could authorize a later expiry after a restart.

- **H5** now proves the reopen is refused `invalid_entry_hold`, the expired row keeps the digest and `requestedAt` the operator saw, and the old approval still returns `stale_signal`.
- **H11** keeps the replacement property: an expired hold is replaced only by a new attempt with its own facts and digest.
- **H12** proves that offset and timezone-free window forms are refused even when they parse to the same instant.

`evidence/SRW-1617/cases.json` changed because H5's old expectation encoded the defect. The pinned SHA-256 in the proof script was updated to match. H5 and H12 both fail without the fix (verified by reverting it in a temporary copy).

## Design fit

`thala_control_store.cjs` owns the durable row and every transition. The coordinator's three methods are thin reads and writes over it, so a caller cannot widen the single use. No second order path: `submit` still refuses `approve_entry` before dispatch, so this build cannot send anything.

The digest is the hash of the facts. The store refuses a hold whose digest is not `sha256(canonicalize(facts))`, so a row can never carry a digest that binds different facts from the ones the operator is shown. P42.2 must pass the same facts object it hashed.

## Proof

`node scripts/srw1617_entry_approval_proof.cjs` — **45/45 cases**, output in `evidence/SRW-1617/proof-output.txt`. Inputs pinned by SHA-256 in `evidence/SRW-1617/cases.json`.

Each of the six self-review fixes has a case that fails without it (verified by reverting the fix in a temporary copy):

| Case | Fails without |
| --- | --- |
| H9 | the `commandId` guard on hold replacement |

| P1–P4 | `approval` in the store's `scopedExit` |

## Existing proofs run green

`scripts/srw725_contract_proof.cjs`, `scripts/srw1345_exit_all_proof.cjs`, `scripts/srw1344_manual_exit_posts_proof.cjs`, `scripts/srw1390_flatten_settle_proof.cjs`, `test_srw1245_manual_close_isolation.js`, `test_srw1394_manual_trim_admission.js`, `test_srw1394_trim_control_path.js`, `scripts/srw754_lane_control_proof.cjs`, `scripts/srw897_p10a_control_ownership_proof.cjs`, `scripts/srw897_p10b_control_health_proof.cjs`, `scripts/srw733_control_boundary_proof.cjs`, `test_srw15_order_path_review.js`, `scripts/srw1408_adjust_plan_proof.cjs`, `scripts/thala_v2_open_proof.cjs`, `scripts/thala_v2_close_proof.cjs --forced-boundaries` (63/63), `scripts/thala_v2_startup_reconcile_proof.cjs`, `scripts/thala_v2_quiet_restart_proof.cjs`, `scripts/thala_v2_freshness_proof.cjs`, `scripts/thala_v2_day_replay_proof.cjs`.

## Self-review

One pass, astra-sub (`gpt-6.2-astra`), against the ticket and the blast-radius bar. It found **no critical**, **four major** and **two minor**. All six are fixed in `c76954a3`:

- **Major — a spent reservation could be reopened.** Hold → reserve → settle `refused` → hold again → reserve again succeeded, so one signal could be approved twice. A hold that was ever reserved is now spent; only a hold refused or expired before any reservation is replaced. (H9)
- **Major — a failed approval write could block unrelated exits.** A forced SQLite error on the `approve_entry` insert degraded the store's ready flag, and the next `close_trade` for another position was refused `recovery_required`. The approval create is now scoped like the other operator commands. (P5)
- **Major — the reservation digest could describe different facts from the durable hold.** The store trusted the caller's digest. It now refuses a hold whose digest is not the hash of its facts. (H10)
- **Major — recovery sent executing approvals through manual-close reconciliation.** Adding approvals to `scopedExit` made the recovery loop call `reconcileClose`, which reads a `payload.tradeId` an approval does not carry. The loop now skips approvals and leaves them to P42.3. (P6)
- **Minor — the stale refusal depended on which call ran first.** A reservation on a hold the sweep had already expired said `entry_approval_spent` instead of `stale_signal`. An expired row is now stale. (R7)
- **Minor — the restart case did not exercise a restarted coordinator.** It now reads through a restarted coordinator's own `getEntryApproval` over the same file. (K3)

- `scripts/srw725_control_store_proof.cjs`, `scripts/srw725_executor_proof.cjs` and `test_srw1393_flatten_audit_posts.js` fail on `main` before this change: they build `close_trade` payloads without the `expectedDigest` that SRW-1345 made mandatory. Confirmed by re-running each with `HEAD`'s contract. Not touched here, because editing an existing proof to make it pass is not allowed.
- `thala_control_reads.cjs` projects a command `type` from a fixed list, so an `approve_entry` row projects `type: null` until P42.4 adds it to the dashboard projection.
- P42.2 must call `holdEntry({ signalId, digest, facts, expiresAt })` with the same `facts` object it hashed into `digest`; the store refuses a mismatch.
- P42.3 owns approval reconciliation and the `signalId` in a restart-failed approval's outcome.

The capability is off by default, `submit` refuses `approve_entry`, and the new table is additive: the pre-change reader opens the upgraded database unchanged. No deployment from this build PR; activation is a separate gate.


The Mac check publisher (`srw/agent-check`) posts the exact-SHA PR tier on the new head; the previous head's `CHECK: PASS` no longer applies.

## Self-review, second round (gate fix)

One pass, astra-sub (`gpt-6.2-astra`), on the gate fix. It found **no critical**, **one major** and no minor:

- **Major — `Date.parse` is timezone-dependent.** A `windowEndsAt` without a timezone parses to a different instant in a different process, so the same digest could authorize a later expiry after a restart. Fixed by comparing the signed window as the canonical ISO string. H12 covers it and fails without the fix.

Device, handset and live-service testing is waived for this ticket (Shyam, 2026-11-14: "no testing is needed lets just finish backlog building everything").
