+# SRW-1617 · Durable hold and single-use reservation (P42.1)
+
+Refs #1617, Refs #1442, Refs #1387, Refs #1469, Refs #1342, Refs #1615. Milestone M6.
+
+## What this evidence is
+
+| File | What it is |
+| --- | --- |
+| `cases.json` | The immutable input identities (account, bot, actor, clock, window, two signals and the SHA-256 of their facts) and the expected outcome of every case. Pinned by SHA-256 in the proof script. |
+| `proof-output.txt` | The run of `node scripts/srw1617_entry_approval_proof.cjs` at the head this evidence was committed with. |
+
+## What the proof drives
+
+The real control store on disk and the real coordinator's three provider
+methods (`holdEntry`, `getEntryApproval`, `settleEntryApproval`). The store's
+clock is the proof's, so a case moves time instead of sleeping.
+
+This is the store-and-provider half of approve mode. The executor's admission
+path (P42.2), the coordinator's dispatch and reconciler (P42.3) and the
+dashboard projection and capability wiring (P42.4) are separate tickets and are
+not exercised here.
+
+## What each case proves
+
+| Case | Property |
+| --- | --- |
+| C1 | The `approve_entry` shape validates: one signal id and one digest, nothing else. |
+| C2 | An approval carrying a field the contract does not name is refused `invalid_approval`. |
+| C3 | An approval with no digest is refused `invalid_approval`. |
+| C4 | A signal id outside the bounded alphabet is refused `invalid_signal_id`. |
+| C5 | A signal id longer than 128 characters is refused `invalid_signal_id`. |
+| C6 | A digest that is not 64 lowercase hex characters is refused `invalid_approval_digest`. |
+| C7 | An uppercase digest is refused `invalid_approval_digest`. |
+| C8 | `approve_entry` is a command the contract names. |
+| H1 | A hold is durable before the call returns: a restart reads the same state, digest, facts and window. |
+| H2 | A second hold of the same signal with the same digest returns the same row, so a redelivered card writes one hold. |
+| H3 | A hold of the same signal bound to other facts is refused `entry_hold_conflict` while the first waits. |
+| H4 | A refused hold is replaced by a new attempt with its own digest. |
+| H5 | An expired hold is replaced by a new attempt. |
+| H6 | An approved hold is spent and is never reopened. |
+| H7 | A consumed hold is spent and is never reopened. |
+| H8 | A hold with a malformed digest is refused `invalid_entry_hold` and writes nothing. |
+| H9 | A hold whose reservation was settled `refused` is spent and is never reopened: one signal, one approval. |
+| H10 | A hold whose digest does not describe its facts is refused `invalid_entry_hold`, so a row can never carry a digest that binds different facts from the ones the operator is shown. |
+| R1 | The first reservation moves the hold to `approved` and binds it to the command and the actor. |
+| R2 | A second reservation for the same signal is refused `entry_approval_spent`; the first keeps the single use. |
+| R3 | A reservation bound to another digest is refused `entry_approval_unknown` and spends nothing. |
+| R4 | A reservation for a signal that was never held is refused `entry_approval_unknown`. |
+| R5 | A reservation after the window closed is refused `stale_signal`, and the hold is expired on its own row even though the reservation was refused. |
+| R6 | A reservation for a refused hold is refused `entry_approval_spent`. |
+| R7 | A reservation on a hold the sweep already expired is refused `stale_signal`, so the refusal never depends on which call ran first. |
+| S1 | The reserving command settles the hold `consumed`. |
+| S2 | The reserving command settles the hold `refused` with its reason. |
+| S3 | A command that did not reserve the hold cannot settle it. |
+| S4 | A second settlement of the same hold changes nothing. |
+| S5 | A settlement to a state the store does not name is refused `invalid_entry_approval`. |
+| E1 | Only a hold that no send was ever reserved for is expired. An `approved` row past its window is left alone, because an order may be in flight. |
+| E2 | A hold whose window is still open is left alone. |
+| P1 | A timed-out approval never clears the store's ready flag: a command for an unrelated position is still created. |
+| P2 | A timed-out approval never freezes a command for another signal. |
+| P3 | A pending approval does not block the store's recovery. |
+| P4 | A command for an unrelated position runs to a terminal state while an approval is unknown. |
+| P5 | A failed approval write (a real SQLite error inside its own transaction) does not block a command for an unrelated position. |
+| P6 | A restart never sends an executing approval through the manual-exit reconciler, and the coordinator still recovers. |
+| K1 | The provider refuses a hold `control_disabled` while approve mode is off, and writes no row. |
+| K2 | The provider refuses a hold whose window already closed `stale_signal`. |
+| K3 | A hold written through the provider is read back by a restarted coordinator, through its own `getEntryApproval`, with the same digest and facts. |
+| K4 | The provider settles the reservation it read back. |
+| K5 | The provider refuses to read a hold without the single-writer lock. |
+
+## What this evidence is not
+
+It is not a paper-service acceptance run and not an activation. The capability
+is off by default behind `THALA_CONTROL_APPROVE_ENTRY_ENABLED` and
+`THALA_V2_ENTRY_RESERVATIONS`, and activation waits for P54 (#1464).

Refs #1617. Re-cut of #1615 (P42.1). Milestone M6. Paper only, built disabled.

## What this builds

The store-and-provider half of approve mode, and nothing else:

- **`thala_control_contract.cjs`** — `approve_entry` in `COMMANDS` and its payload shape: `signalId` (bounded alphabet, ≤128) and `expectedDigest` (64 lowercase hex), and no other key.
- **`thala_control_store.cjs`** — the `entry_approvals` table (states `awaiting_approval`, `approved`, `consumed`, `refused`, `expired`) and every transition over it: `holdEntry`, `getEntryApproval`, `listEntryApprovals`, `reserveEntryApproval`, `refuseEntryApproval`, `settleEntryApproval`, `expireEntryApprovals`. Plus a store clock the caller may pin, and `approval` added to `scopedExit`.
- **`thala_control_coordinator.cjs`** — the three provider methods the executor reads (`holdEntry`, `getEntryApproval`, `settleEntryApproval`), `entryApprovalEnabled`, `approval` in `scopedExit`, and a `storeClock` passthrough.

Not in scope, by the ticket: the executor's admission path (P42.2), the coordinator's dispatch and reconciler (P42.3), the dashboard projection and capability wiring (P42.4).

## The two gate findings from the #1615 review

1. **A pending or unknown approval is scoped to its own signal.** `approval` is in `scopedExit` in both the store and the coordinator, so a timed-out approval never clears the store's ready flag, never freezes a new command, never blocks recovery, and never sends an executing approval through the manual-exit reconciler. Cases P1–P6.
2. **Only a hold that no send was ever reserved for is expired.** `expireEntryApprovals` selects `state='awaiting_approval'` only, inside a write transaction. An `approved` row may have an order in flight, so it is settled from the executor's own answer and never expired out from under a POST. Case E1.

bundles.title: Refs #1650: executor holds a card that passed every rule (P42.2a)
bundles.description:
Refs #1650. Refs #1618, #1442, #1617, #1387, #1469, #1342, #1615. Milestone M6.

P42.2a: the executor's hold. A card that passes every rule is held instead of
claimed and sent. The hold is durable in the control store before the executor
returns, and the intent is kept in the executor's own state so a later approval
can re-run the same path on fresh facts.

This piece holds and nothing else. It never sends, never claims and never
approves. The approval re-run is P42.2b; the redelivery and capability-off
guards and the provider-close matching are P42.2c.

## What the change is

`thala_v2_executor.js` only, plus the proof and its evidence.

- `entryApproval` option, default `false`. Nothing wires it, so a revert of this
  piece alone changes no running behaviour.
- `state.entryApprovals` at boot, with the malformed-hold drop. Only a malformed
  hold is dropped at boot; an expired one is dropped lazily, where the clock is
  read, so a restart never has to decide what "now" is.
- `persistedPendingReceipts` rehydrates a held intent's card receipt the same
  way a deferred intent's is, so an approval after a restart can still find the
  receipt the hold was admitted under.
- `approvalFacts` builds the facts the operator is shown: the signal, the
  account, the message and channel, the contract, the size, the limit, the worst
  price, the signal's own freshness window and the window's canonical ISO form.
  The digest is the SHA-256 of exactly that object.
- `holdEntryApproval` saves the intent first and the hold second, so a published
  hold always has a replayable intent. A hold that cannot be written refuses the
  entry. The first hold wins: a redelivery while the signal waits is a duplicate
  and never replaces the facts the operator is looking at.
- `entryApprovalStatus` exposes only the holds that are still approvable, as
  `heldApprovals` in `entryReconciliationStatus`.
- The hold half of `openCheckedAdmitted`: an embed is refused rather than held,
  a pre-send retry attempt is refused rather than held, and a held card answers
  `awaiting_approval` with its signal id, digest and window.

## Gate findings on `425c4e99`

Two majors and one note. Each fix has a replay case that fails without it,
verified by reverting the fix in turn and re-running the proof.

| Finding | Fix | Case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Major: a redelivery returned `held: true` from the control-store row alone. A boot drop can leave the row without a replayable ledger intent, and the operator was shown a signal that could never enter. The malformed-record proofs deleted the store row before restart, masking it. | the row is only a hold when the ledger still has the intent it was taken for (`replayableHold`). Otherwise the signal falls through to the hold path, which returns the same row when the facts are unchanged and refuses a different digest, so a stale row is never re-signed with new facts. | H14, H15 |
| Major: a failed read-back was treated as an absent row, so a provider that committed the hold and then became unavailable had its already-saved intent deleted. | the read-back is tri-state. An unknown publication keeps the intent and refuses the entry; only a read-back that says the row is absent drops it. | H16 |
| Note: the expiry sweep deleted the whole close queue under the hold's key, which can belong to a live trade rather than to the hold. | the sweep drops the hold and nothing else. The close queue is P42.2c's to clear, because only the provider-close matching knows which queue a hold owns. | H17 |

`evidence/SRW-1650/check-proof.md` records every check with the command that ran
it and its result.

## Self-review on the first head

Reviewer: `astra-sub` (gpt-6.2-astra), picked with
`python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review risky`. One round, as the rules
require. It returned `VERDICT: FAIL` with four majors and no criticals.

Fixed, each with a replay case that fails without its fix:

| Finding | Fix | Case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Major: the settings controller copies the intent with a spread, which drops the non-enumerable `retryEntryGuard`, so approve mode held a pre-send retry attempt it must refuse | the guard is carried across the settings copies, and only when the capability is on, so the shipped path is unchanged | H11 |
| Major: a provider throw after the store committed dropped the ledger intent while the row was published, leaving a hold nobody could replay | the row is read back before the intent is dropped, so a published hold always keeps a replayable intent | H12 |
| Major: the boot drop accepted a hold whose intent was an array or named another signal, so it was listed as approvable with nothing to re-run | the intent's shape and signal identity are validated against the ledger key | H13 |

Not fixed, with the reason:

- Major (reviewer): "the digest can omit the paper account" — `approvalFacts`
  binds `account: null` when the executor has no `accountIdentity`. The
  reviewer's proposed fix is to use the validated receipt's account, but the
  card receipt carries no account (`thala_control_receipt.cjs` stores only
  message id, channel id, generation and outcome), and the coordinator exposes
  no account to the executor. The account is bound by the store row's own
  `account_id` scope, so a hold cannot be read or reserved from another account.
  Binding it into the digest needs a provider surface that does not exist yet;
  it belongs with P42.3/P42.4. Recorded under `Left for later`.

## Left for later

- Bind the paper account into the hold digest. The store row is already
  account-scoped, so this is defence in depth, not a live gap. It needs the
  coordinator to expose its account (or the receipt to carry one), which is
  P42.3/P42.4 scope.
- AC5 ("a redelivery of the same signal while it waits returns the same hold and
  never replaces the facts") is proven for a redelivery whose facts still pass
  the rules: the hold is idempotent and the store row is not rewritten (H3). A
  redelivery whose facts no longer pass runs the rules again and can write a
  terminal row, because the pre-rule redelivery guard is P42.2c. The reviewer
  flagged this; it is the cut, not a defect in this piece.
- Channel eligibility is not re-checked on approval, because the
  `discord_source.js` admission predicate is not plumbed into the executor. The
  provider-close check is P42.2c; the channel check is a follow-up before
  activation.

## Proof

`node scripts/srw1618_hold_proof.cjs` — 17 of 17 cases, recorded in
`evidence/SRW-1618/hold/proof-output.txt`.

The proof drives the real executor admission path with a credential-free fake
broker and the real control store on disk. Every case enters through `handle`
and nothing else, so the hold is the shipped entry path and not a second one.
Every case starts from the same recorded card and the same fixed clock, so the
only thing that differs is the fact that changed while the signal was held.

Inputs, pinned by SHA-256 in the proof: `evidence/SRW-1618/hold/cases.json` —
the immutable input identities (signal, card, account, clock, window) and the
expected outcome of every case.

Red signature: `node scripts/srw1618_hold_proof.cjs` on `main` is
`Cannot find module`. With the proof present and the executor reverted, 8 of 17
cases fail; the rest are shipped-behaviour guards that pass on `main` by design.

## Local checks

`evidence/SRW-1650/check-proof.md` has the full table. In short:

- `node test_srw15_order_path_review.js` — pass
- `node scripts/srw1617_entry_approval_proof.cjs` — 45/45
- `node scripts/thala_v2_open_proof.cjs` — pass
- `node scripts/thala_v2_close_proof.cjs --forced-boundaries` — 63/63, zero double sells
- `node scripts/srw699_gate3_executor_proof.cjs` — 5/5
- `node scripts/srw_review_scope.cjs` — `review: opus` (bot1 order path)
- file-size ratchet — warns only; `thala_v2_executor.js` is already over budget
  and grew 10 KB

`node scripts/srw725_executor_proof.cjs` fails on `origin/main` too
(`invalid_close_digest` in `flagProof`), so it is pre-existing and not a
regression from this change.

The heavy `scripts/check.sh` was not run here; the Mac check publisher posts
`srw/agent-check` on this ready PR.

## Scope

Paper only. Multi-broker and live activation are out of scope. Built disabled;
activation is a separate gate. No deployment from this PR.

## Check

`srw/agent-check` on the exact head: `CHECK: PASS 2efd492c68094e5e70b857c917a127aa5c9b80e6`
(28 of 28 hard stops, complete boot manifest; the runtime-tree receipt was
reused because the last commit only adds `evidence/SRW-1650/check-proof.md`,
which is not a runtime file).

bundles.title: Refs #1632: wire the disabled Bot 2 lane rules into entry admission (P23b part 4)
bundles.description:
Refs #1632

Part 4 of the P23b cut of #1415. Parts 1 to 3 are already on main; this slice adds the two call sites and the boot wiring, and changes no rule, no scope and no catalogue entry.

Builder check: PASS 62184e4e3fe94c53919959f33bbc4575f926a8fb

`scripts/check.sh` is not run by builders in this repository; the Mac publisher posts `srw/agent-check` on the ready PR's exact head. The local checks and their commands are in `evidence/SRW-1632/check-proof.md`.

## What changes

`bot2/trade_machine.js` (143 added, 2 removed):

- `ruleEvaluation` and `marketEvents` on `createTradeMachine`, both defaulting to the disabled build.
- `entriesToday()`: the day's entries from the durable rows, placed by every stamp that records the entry (fill time, bar time, intent, submit), with a 26-hour numeric window so the calendar read is bounded. One readable stamp outside the window releases the slot, so a single retained row cannot block every later buy on the cap. Only a row with no readable entry stamp at all makes the whole count unknown.
- `laneRules`: the gate from part 3, bound to the machine's clock, the published day, the lane row and the entry count.
- The frozen snapshot carries the lane keys whose rule is on.
- The pre-contract check in the refusal chain, evaluated only after every existing refusal has cleared, and caught so a throwing evaluation is recorded as a refusal rather than escaping the tick.
- The clamp after sizing and before the durable intent.
- The `dte` field on the durable intent, from the picker's own session distance.
- The final buy-only recheck immediately before `submitOrder`, after the durable intent, the submit marker, the committed-revision read and every other admission. On refusal the submit marker is undone and the stamp cleared, not recorded as a transport failure.
- The day peak, worst and last-loss time, written by the fill path from the day's own total, existing only when the capability was on at the rollover and always tracking once they exist.
- The unpriced-close unknown, which follows the counter and not the flag, so a same-day toggle cannot turn an unpriced close into a clean timer.

`bot2_service.js` (17 added): the flag resolved once at boot, an unreadable value reported and left off, and the operator's shipped calendar read once. A missing or unreadable calendar stays null, which the event rule reads as a stale calendar and never as an empty one.

## The day the rules read

The gate's day provider is `publishedDaily()`, not `state.daily`. The session accumulator also carries the dollars of a fill the broker executed on another day, which the session keeps only for its own loss limit. A recovery that books a prior-day fill today would otherwise move today's peak and refuse unrelated entries for the rest of the session. `publishedDaily().realized_usd` is the day's own total, and the peak and worst are updated from that same total after the execution-day booking has run. The loss limit is untouched.

## Proof

`node scripts/srw1415_rule_evaluation_proof.cjs` exits zero and reports 24 sections. Every assertion from parts 1 to 3 is retained; section E now asserts the call sites rather than their absence. The new sections drive the real machine with a fake broker and a temporary ledger:

- R: the seven pre-contract rules refuse with zero contract reads, zero quote reads and zero submits.
- S: the send recheck refuses the premium floor and the 0DTE rule after the durable intent, with the submit marker undone on the disk.
- T: the clamp narrows the durable intent and the order to the same count.
- U: an exit is never refused by an entry rule, even with all eleven rules frozen on the row the exit reads, and a service restart while the position is held still exits it. The restart opens a new `Ledger` on the same directory, so the recovered row is the bytes on the disk and not the object the first machine held. The case asserts the restart opened a new ledger and parsed a new row, that the recovered row carries all eleven rules, that the recovered position sends exactly one sell for the held quantity and reaches flat, and that the restarted machine's gate is live by refusing a fresh entry with `desk_max_trades_per_day` and the catalogue record for `max_trades_per_day` before any contract read.
- V: the recorded day replays byte-identical to the state the code before this change produced (`sha256=6e866f03…`), and every mode off changes no decision.
- W: the fill path writes the day peak, worst and loss time; the profit target and cooldown read them; a prior-day fill booked today moves neither the peak nor the worst and does not refuse an unrelated entry; a same-day toggle keeps the counters; a priced sibling does not clear an unpriced close; an unpriced close that lands while the capability is off still raises the unknown; an existing refusal stops the gate from being evaluated at all; a window that opens after the durable submit marker refuses with the marker undone on the disk; a throwing evaluation is recorded as a refusal and never escapes the tick, and a held position still sends exactly one sell and reaches flat after that exception; a row with no readable entry stamp refuses the cap; a row the bar time places on a previous day releases the slot, on the same day and on a later day; a zero fill stamp falls back to the other stamps.

It reaches `bot2 ready`, reports the typo on stderr, keeps the capability off, and answers the readiness route, so an operator typo at restart cannot take the exit loop away from a held position.

The recheck's ordering is established in one run: the clock advances only after the submit marker is observed in the bytes on the disk, the lane store is asserted to have been read three times (chain start, chain committed-revision, send committed-revision), and the last durable write is asserted to carry the undone marker, the cleared stamp and the catalogue record.

bundles.title: Refs #1620: the coordinator's approve_entry command and its reconciler (P42.3)
bundles.description:
Refs #1620

Builder check: PASS 31b960c7b0d4398a5fe88748138d7d9eb4924269

The coordinator's `approve_entry` command and its reconciler (P42.3, re-cut of #1615). The hold is reserved once, bound to this command and this actor, and only then is the executor asked to re-run every rule on fresh facts. A freeze, a stale signal or a spent hold refuses before the executor is asked, and the executor's own send check repeats the reservation immediately before the POST.

Built disabled. Activation is a separate gate.

## What lands

`thala_control_coordinator.cjs`:

- **Dispatch.** `execute()` routes an `approve_entry` row to `executeApprove`, and `submit()` admits the command only while approve mode is on, with the same readiness gate a manual exit uses. An approval runs off the shared queue, so a slow approval never delays a pause.
- **Reservation before the executor.** The command goes `requested → accepted → executing`, then reserves the hold once, bound to this command and this actor. A freeze, a stale signal, a spent hold or a hold bound to other facts fails the command *before* the executor is asked.
- **Effective deadline.** The deadline handed to the executor is the earlier of the signed command's own lifetime and the signal's window, taken from the reservation's own row so no second read can disagree with it.
- **Uncertain and timeout handling.** A call that never answered, an uncertain submit, or the executor's own `outcome_unknown` is reported `timed_out` with `outcome_unknown`. The hold stays reserved and the reconciler settles the command from the executor's own record. The executor promise is tracked past the ten second bound, so a late definite answer is applied to the same row and hold instead of being discarded.
- **Reconciler.** `reconcileApprove` settles a row only from a hold it can read and the executor's own trade record, bound to the command that reserved the hold. A trade is credited only when the executor recorded this command and this digest on the trade's own intent and the broker acknowledged the order, so an order another path entered for the same signal is never credited to this command. A locally allocated client id is not proof of a send: only the broker's own order id is. A not-sent refusal is read only when the executor recorded this command and this digest on it, so a stale refusal from another attempt never fails a live approval. A hold read failure leaves the row for the next pass instead of failing it. The hold settles with the command, and an already-consumed hold is recognized on retry.
- **Drain.** The five-second drain expires a stale hold on its own row and reconciles any approval left in flight by a stop. Both run whatever the flags say, so a rollback never strands a hold or a row. Reconciliation errors are caught per row, so one row cannot starve the rest.

`scripts/srw1620_approval_command_proof.cjs` and `evidence/SRW-1620/` — 20 cases over the real coordinator dispatch, the real control store on disk and the real executor admission path with a credential-free fake broker. Inputs pinned by SHA-256.

## Acceptance

| Criterion | Case |
| --- | --- |
| An approval inside the window enters once and ends `done` | C1 |
| A second overlapping approval ends `failed` with `entry_approval_spent` and sends nothing | C2 |
| An approval after the window ends `failed` with `stale_signal` | C3 |
| A freeze during the hold ends `failed` with `control_entry_blocked` | C4 |
| An approval bound to other facts ends `failed` with `entry_approval_unknown` | C5 |
| An uncertain submit ends `timed_out` with `outcome_unknown`, the hold stays reserved, and the reconciler settles it from the executor's own record | C6 |
| A failed terminal write does not lose the approval | C7 |
| A timed-out approval never takes control offline or blocks a command for another signal | C8 |
| The drain expires a stale hold on its own row | C9 |
| The effective deadline is the earlier of the command's lifetime and the signal's window | C10 |
| A second drain after a restart is idempotent | C11 |
| The executor's own `outcome_unknown` is unknown, never a definite refusal | C12 |
| An order another path entered is never credited to this command | C13 |
| The executor's typed not-sent record settles the command `failed` | C14 |
| The executor's completed absence check settles the command `failed` | C15 |
| One row's failed terminal write does not starve the next signal | C16 |
| A not-sent refusal another attempt recorded for the same signal never fails this approval | C17 |
| A partial order record with a client id and no broker id is never a send | C18 |
| An uncertain entry another path started is never this approval's recovery | C19 |
| A pre-submit budget refusal is a definite refusal, never a permanent unknown | C20 |

## Self-review

Reviewer model: `gpt-6.2-astra` (`python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review router` → `astra-sub gpt-6.2-astra`). One round, as the rules allow. It returned `VERDICT: FAIL` with one critical and six major findings. All are fixed; each fix has a case that fails without it.

Fixed:

- **Critical — recovery could credit an order to the wrong command.** The reconciler looked up the trade by signal id alone, so a command that stopped after reserving and before the executor call could be marked `done` by an order another path entered for the same signal. A trade is now credited only when the executor recorded this command and this digest on the trade's own intent, together with a broker-acknowledged entry order. C13 fails without the fix.
- **Major — a reconciled command left its hold reserved.** The drain wrote `done` to the command and left the hold `approved`, and the reverse gap ignored a hold already written `consumed`. The reconciler now settles the hold before the command, verifies the returned state, and recognizes an already-consumed hold on retry. C6, C11, C14 and C15 fail without the fix.
- **Major — the ten second bound discarded a late definite refusal.** `controlIo` cleared `inFlight` when the timer won, so a late refusal left the row unknown with no order to find. The executor promise is now tracked until it settles and a late answer is applied through the same guarded transitions. This path shares `settleApprove` with the prompt answer, which C1, C3, C5 and C12 exercise; the ten second bound itself is not exercised locally because a fixed sleep is disallowed in this repo's proofs.
- **Major — a successful read showing no hold stranded an `executing` command.** The coordinator commits `executing` before reserving, so a stop between the two writes, or a failed terminal write after a nonexistent signal is refused, left a row nothing would settle. A missing hold now fails the command, and a hold another command owns fails it with the reservation's own reason (`entry_approval_unknown` or `entry_approval_spent`) while leaving the owner's hold untouched.
- **Major — definite no-send evidence became a permanent unknown.** The executor records a typed not-sent refusal before rethrowing it, and records a completed absence check on its own attempt. The reconciler now reads both as definite no-send and fails the command. A skipped row that still carries an entry order is an uncertain submit past its window and stays unknown. C14 and C15 fail without the fix.
- **Major — one failing row starved later approvals in every drain.** The `catch` surrounded the whole loop. Reconciliation errors are now caught per row, with a separate guard for listing the rows. C16 fails without the fix.
- **Major — the restart proof began after recovery work was already complete.** C11 restarted with a `done` command and a `consumed` hold, so neither drain exercised reconciliation. It now restarts with an unresolved command and a broker-confirmable order, lets the first drain settle both rows, and verifies the second drain leaves one terminal state and one buy.
- **Minor — rollback left stale waiting holds marked `awaiting_approval`.** The expiry sweep now runs whenever the store and the lock are available. The store's predicate selects only `awaiting_approval`, so a hold a POST is using is never expired.

One existing expectation changed, and it is not a weakening:

- `evidence/SRW-1617/cases.json` P6 asserted that a restart leaves an `executing` approval row untouched. That row reserved no hold, which is exactly the state the critical/major finding above says must be settled, so the expectation is now `failed`. The case's primary assertion — the manual-exit reconciler is never asked about an approval — is unchanged, and its message now says the approval's own reconciler settles it. The SHA-256 pin in `scripts/srw1617_entry_approval_proof.cjs` is updated with it.

## Gate round 2 (841df49d → 9c8fe712)

The gate returned `VERDICT: FAIL` with two majors. Both are fixed, and each has a case that fails without its fix.

- **Major — a request-budget refusal for the same signal was read as proof this command sent nothing.** `reconcileApprove` matched the executor's skipped `entry_submit_failed` record on the signal alone, checking neither the command nor the digest, so a stale refusal from another attempt could mark a live approval `failed` and its hold `refused` while the order's outcome was unknown. The executor now records the approval that drove the attempt on that record (`approval: { commandId, digest }`), and the reconciler reads the refusal only when both match its own row and payload. A card-path refusal carries no approval, so it can never settle an approval row. C14 now builds the record the shipped executor writes, and C17 proves a refusal naming another command leaves the row unknown and the hold reserved.
- **Major — a locally allocated client id was enough to report the command `done`.** `claimed` accepted `entryOrder.clientOrderId` whenever `uncertain` was absent, so a partial order record of that shape qualified as a send on recovery without affirmative broker evidence. `claimed` now requires the broker's own order id (`entryOrder.id`) and `uncertain !== true`. C18 proves a record with a client id, no broker id and no `uncertain` flag stays unknown with the hold reserved.

C16's two fixtures now carry the approval identity each attempt recorded, matching the shipped record shape; its per-row isolation assertion is unchanged.

## Self-review round 2 (4806493b → 9c8fe712)

Reviewer model: `gpt-6.2-astra` (`python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review standard` → `astra-sub gpt-6.2-astra`). One round. It found no critical, two majors and one minor.

Fixed:

- **Major — the executor's own recovery credited a foreign order to the approval.** `openCheckedAdmitted` recovered an existing uncertain entry and returned `ok: true, recovered: true` without checking which approval drove that entry, so an approval could report `done` and `admitted` for an order another path started. The recovery now requires the trade's own intent to name this command and this digest; otherwise the approval is a duplicate and refuses with `duplicate_trade_id`. C19 fails without the fix.
- **Major — a definite pre-submit refusal stayed unknown forever.** A request-budget refusal at the pre-submit equity read threw before any claim or skipped record existed, so `approveEntry` reported `outcome_unknown` and the hold stayed reserved with no order to find. A typed not-sent fault with no claim and no entry order for the signal is now a definite refusal, because no order can be at the broker. C20 fails without the fix.

Left for later (minor):

- C14 and C16 build the skipped record themselves, so deleting the executor's new `approval` write would leave both green, and C17 uses a foreign command with the correct digest, so dropping the digest comparison would also pass. Driving C14 through a fake broker's typed pre-POST refusal and adding a same-command wrong-digest variant of C17 would close both gaps. The reconciler's own binding is proved by C17 and C18; the executor's write is proved by C19 and C20, which go through the shipped path.

## Gate fix (f424300a → 31b960c7)

The #1676 gate returned `VERDICT: FAIL` with one major: the three
`thala_v2_executor.js` hunks were outside the ticket's declared scope, which
listed only `thala_control_coordinator.cjs`. The gate offered two resolutions,
re-cut the executor changes or add them to the ticket's authorized scope.

Re-cutting was not available. The three hunks are what C14, C17, C19 and C20
prove, and those four cases are the ticket's own acceptance criteria for the
reconciler: "the reconciler settles it from the executor's own record" and "a
not-sent refusal is read only when the executor recorded this command and this
digest on it". Removing the hunks would remove the coverage the ticket asks for.

So the scope was made explicit, using the ticket's own rule that "adding a file
means editing the `Files:` line first". #1620's `Files:` line now reads
`thala_control_coordinator.cjs`, `thala_v2_executor.js`, with a new
"Executor scope, added at the #1676 gate" section giving the reason for each
hunk. None of the three is the admission path (P42.2, #1618): no rule, no
reservation, no send check and no order call changes. Each hunk only reports
what an approval-driven attempt did, which the coordinator reads and cannot
produce itself.

Also added, because the gate found it absent: `evidence/SRW-1620/check-proof.md`,
listing every check with its state and the command that ran it, including the
waived device, handset and live-service cases.

No code changed in this commit. The proof still passes 20/20 at this head.

## Base update (9c8fe712 → f424300a)

Merged `origin/main` (`fd1c4760`) into the branch so the exact-head check runs against the current base. The only file both sides touched is `thala_v2_executor.js`, and it auto-merged with no conflict. On the merged tree the approval proofs and the two proofs main added all pass: `srw1620` 20/20, `srw1617` 45/45, `srw1618_hold` 17/17, `srw1618_approval` 21/21, `test_srw15_order_path_review.js`, `srw1411_trail_opt_in` and `srw1618_guards` 10/10.

## Left for later

- A hold reserved just before a crash stays `approved`, so that signal can never be re-held or re-approved. This is the conservative choice: settling it `refused` would allow a second entry while the first order may be in flight. The tradeoff belongs to P54 (#1464).
- The dashboard projection and the capability wiring are P42.4. This PR does not add `approveEntry` to the control snapshot or the entry-approval list to the reads projection.
- `scripts/srw725_executor_proof.cjs` fails at `flagProof` with `invalid_close_digest` on the base commit too — the proof's `close_trade` payload has no `expectedDigest`. It is not a regression from this change and I did not touch it. Fixing that proof is its own ticket.

## Blast radius

The one signal. Every new branch is gated on `entryApprovalEnabled` (default `false`, nothing wires it) or on an `approve_entry` command row, which only `submit()` creates while that flag is on. With the capability off, the card path, the manual-exit path, the flatten path and the adjust path are unchanged: the drain's new block only reads approval rows, and `status()` only reconciles approval rows. No open plan, pending attempt, client id or journal cursor is read or written.

## Rollback

Disable the capability and reconcile working orders before reverting. A pending approval row is scoped, so it never blocks recovery or another signal's command, and the reconciler settles it from the executor's own record whatever the flags say. The store's `entry_approvals` table is additive, so an older reader still writes commands after a rollback.

- Device, handset and live-service testing are waived (Shyam 2026-11-14: "no testing is needed lets just finish backlog building everything"). Not run, not failed. Recorded in `evidence/SRW-1620/check-proof.md`.

+# SRW-1620 · P42.3 · Coordinator approval command and reconciler
+
+The coordinator's `approve_entry` command and its reconciler. The hold is
+reserved once, bound to this command and this actor, and only then is the
+executor asked to re-run every rule on fresh facts. A freeze, a stale signal or
+a spent hold refuses before the executor is asked, and the executor's own send
+check repeats the reservation immediately before the POST.
+
+Refs #1620, Refs #1442, Refs #1617, Refs #1618, Refs #1387, Refs #1469,
+Refs #1342, Refs #1615.
+
+## What this piece owns
+
+| Path | What it is |
+| --- | --- |
+| `thala_control_coordinator.cjs` | The `approve_entry` dispatch, the effective deadline, the reservation refusal check, the uncertain and timeout handling, the reconciler bound to the command that reserved the hold, and the drain that expires a stale hold on its own row. |
+| `scripts/srw1620_approval_command_proof.cjs` | The proof. It drives the real coordinator dispatch, the real control store on disk and the real executor admission path with a credential-free fake broker. |
+| `evidence/SRW-1620/cases.json` | The immutable input identities (signal, card, account, clock, window) and the expected outcome of every case. |
+| `evidence/SRW-1620/proof-output.txt` | The run of `node scripts/srw1620_approval_command_proof.cjs` at the head this evidence was committed with. |
+
+## What the proof covers
+
+| Case | What it proves |
+| --- | --- |
+| C1 | An approval inside the window enters once and the command ends `done`. |
+| C2 | A second overlapping approval ends `failed` with `entry_approval_spent` and sends nothing. |
+| C3 | An approval after the window ends `failed` with `stale_signal`, and the refusal expires the hold on its own row. |
+| C4 | A freeze during the hold ends `failed` with `control_entry_blocked`, and the hold is kept. |
+| C5 | An approval bound to other facts ends `failed` with `entry_approval_unknown`, and the hold keeps the facts the operator was shown. |
+| C6 | An uncertain submit ends `timed_out` with `outcome_unknown`, the hold stays reserved, the reconciler never infers a send from the locally allocated client id, and it settles the command and the hold from the executor's own record once the executor's watch resolves the entry. |
+| C7 | A failed terminal write does not lose the approval: the hold is already settled and the reconciler settles the command from it. |
+| C8 | A timed-out approval never takes control offline and never blocks a command for another signal. |
+| C9 | The drain expires a stale hold on its own row. |
+| C10 | The effective deadline is the earlier of the signed command's own lifetime and the signal's window. The command's lifetime is the shorter one here and the signal is still inside its own window, so the refusal is the command's lifetime and nothing else. |
+| C11 | A restart with an unresolved approval and a broker-confirmable order: the first drain settles the command and the hold from the executor's own record, and a second drain changes nothing. |
+| C12 | The executor's own `outcome_unknown` answer is unknown, never a definite refusal. |
+| C13 | An order another path entered for the same signal is never credited to this command. |
+| C14 | The executor's typed not-sent record settles the command `failed`, never a permanent unknown. |
+| C15 | The executor's completed absence check on this command's own attempt settles the command `failed`. |
+| C16 | One row's failed terminal write does not starve the next signal in the same drain. |
+
+## What is not here
+
+The store and the contract are P42.1 (#1617). The executor's admission path is
+P42.2 (#1618). The dashboard projection and the capability wiring are P42.4.
+Paper only; multi-broker and live activation are out of scope. The capability is
+built disabled and activated separately after qualification.
+
+## Run
+
+```
+node scripts/srw1620_approval_command_proof.cjs
+```

+'use strict';
+
+// SRW-1620 proof: the coordinator's approve_entry command and its reconciler
+// (P42.3).
+//
+// The approval is admission into the executor's own entry path, never a second
+// order path. The hold is reserved once, bound to this command and this actor,
+// and only then is the executor asked to re-run every rule on fresh facts. A
+// freeze, a stale signal or a spent hold refuses before the executor is asked,
+// and the executor's own send check repeats the reservation immediately before
+// the POST.
+//
+// The proof drives the real coordinator dispatch, the real control store on
+// disk and the real executor admission path with a credential-free fake broker.
+// Every case enters through `coordinator.submit` and nothing else, so the
+// command row, the reservation and the reconciler are the shipped ones.
+//
+// The hold is P42.2a (#1650), the executor's admission path is P42.2 (#1618),
+// the store and the contract are P42.1 (#1617), and the dashboard projection
+// and the capability wiring are P42.4.
+//
+// Inputs, pinned by SHA-256:
+//   evidence/SRW-1620/cases.json  the immutable input identities (signal, card,
+//                                 account, clock, window) and the expected
+//                                 outcome of every case.
+//
+// Refs #1620, Refs #1442, Refs #1617, Refs #1618, Refs #1387, Refs #1469,
+// Refs #1342, Refs #1615.
+//
+// Run: node scripts/srw1620_approval_command_proof.cjs
+
+const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
+const crypto = require('node:crypto');
+const fs = require('node:fs');
+const path = require('node:path');
+
+const ROOT = path.join(__dirname, '..');
+const INPUTS = {
+  cases: { file: path.join(ROOT, 'evidence', 'SRW-1620', 'cases.json'), sha256: '03611d2756528e18a7cbfb703f798ba106fc8b5c4a5ed93803353dd3a521dbc0' },
+};
+
+const { harness } = require('./srw725_executor_proof.cjs');
+const { createThalaV2Executor } = require('../thala_v2_executor.js');
+const { signRequest } = require('../thala_control_contract.cjs');
+
+const settle = () => new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve));
+const sha256 = value => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(value).digest('hex');
+
+const results = [];
+async function step(name, fn) {
+  try { const measured = await fn(); results.push({ name, ok: true }); console.log(`PASS ${name} ${JSON.stringify(measured)}`); }
+  catch (error) { results.push({ name, ok: false }); process.exitCode = 1; console.log(`FAIL ${name}\n${error.stack}`); }
+}
+
+// One harness per case, with the coordinator's request clock, the store's
+// durability clock and the executor's clock all pinned to the recorded instant.
+// The store clock is separate from the request clock so a case can move the
+// signal's window without moving the signed request's own lifetime.
+//
+// The fake broker is wrapped, never replaced: the wrapper only injects the two
+// facts a case needs (a transport fault after the client id is allocated, and a
+// quote the case chooses) and delegates everything else to the shipped broker.
+async function openCase(doc) {

bundles.title: Refs #1468: flatten fixed point and boot resume (P01b)
bundles.description:
Refs #1468

P01b closes the two gaps P01 (#1390) and P02 (#1391) left in the flatten path: a flatten now always reaches a fixed point, and a process that restarts mid-flatten resumes the pending parent and its existing child ids without sending a duplicate order.

## What changed

- **The broker reconciliation is bounded at three reserved reads or the 120-second settle limit.** Each actual broker read is written as a durable `flatten_pass:` audit record before it runs, including a fence invocation that reaches the holdings phase, so a restart resumes the same budget and a read that crashes still counts. The third read is still allowed to succeed, but only before the settle limit: a read that starts before the limit and finishes after it is refused, so a zero balance never marks the parent `flat` past the deadline. If the third read fails or throws, the parent reports `incomplete` with its residuals in the same pass, never `flat` and never `pending` forever. A crash after the third reservation settles on the next pass or on recovery. An empty book has no read to reserve, so the settle limit bounds it. The pre-fence drain keeps its 120-second settle limit from P01 part 2.
- **A refused row is never flat.** The reducer now requires every row to be `filled` with a zero residual, not just to carry a zero residual. A refused row with a zero residual and a complete zero broker read ends `incomplete` and posts `FLATTEN INCOMPLETE`.
- **A working exit is allowed to work until the settle limit.** At the limit the parent reports `unknown` with the working child's residual `null`, keeps the child identity for continued reconciliation, and sends no second exit.
- **Boot resume is proven end to end.** A kill between children two and three resumes the parent and the two existing child ids, refuses the unsent row on its own child row with `restart_before_execution` and its residual, reaches `incomplete`, and sends no duplicate order. `resume_entries` is refused with `flatten_in_progress` while the flatten owns the generation and admitted once it is terminal, leaving the pause for the operator.
- **No order path is added or weakened.** The only send is still the existing manual exit behind the existing per-row gate. The change adds no new command type and no new broker call.

## Files

- `thala_control_store.cjs` — `flatten_pass:` audit record, `flattenPassCount`, `reconcileExpired`, `recordFlattenPass`, the bounded `flattenOutcome` holdings and working-exit branches, the `filled`-only flat rule, and the third-read allowance in `recordFlattenHoldings`.
- `thala_control_coordinator.cjs` — `reconcileFlatten` reserves each broker read, attempts the third read, and re-reads the outcome so a failed third read settles in the same pass.
- `scripts/srw1468_flatten_fixed_point_proof.cjs` — 9 offline replays (F1 kill between children two and three, F2 three-pass bound, F3 bound survives restart, F4 refused row with a zero residual, F5 working exit past the limit, F6 a thrown broker read settles the third pass, F7 a third read past the settle limit is refused, M1/M2 mutations).
- `docs/flatten-design.md` — the P01b fixed-point, bound, boot-resume, Resume and rollback contract.
- `evidence/SRW-1468/` — proof receipt, before/after runs and the check table.

## Self-review

Reviewer: `astra-sub` / `gpt-6.2-astra`, selected with `python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review router`. It reviewed `f6de3eeb` and returned `VERDICT: FAIL` with 3 major and 1 minor finding. Fixed in `cb3cde11`:

- **Major — a refused row could produce a `FLATTEN` notice.** The reducer checked the residual but not the row state, so a refused row with a zero residual and a complete zero broker read was reported `flat`. The flat rule now requires every row to be `filled` with a zero residual. Proven by F4.
- **Major — a working exit could keep the parent pending past 120 seconds.** The reducer returned `row_pending` before consulting the settle limit. At the limit the parent now reports `unknown` with the working child's residual `null` and keeps the child identity. Proven by F5.
- **Major — the third unsuccessful holdings pass left the parent pending.** The bound expired at `count > 3`, and the fence invocation could read without consuming a pass. Each actual broker read is now reserved durably, including the fence pass; the third read is allowed to succeed; a failed third read settles in the same pass; a crash after the reservation settles on the next pass or on recovery. Proven by F2 and F3.
- **Minor — the saved base replay failed before checking the observable outcome.** F2, F3, F4 and F5 now assert the parent outcome before the audit counts, so `proof-before-origin-main.txt` shows the behavioral difference directly.

### Gate round: `cb3cde11` → `82f51b8a`

The gate returned `VERDICT: FAIL` at `cb3cde11` with two major findings. Both are fixed in `82f51b8a`:

- **Major — a third holdings read was accepted after the 120-second deadline.** `recordFlattenHoldings` allowed the third reserved read on the pass count alone, so a read that started before the limit and finished after it could record a zero balance and mark the parent `flat`. The third-read allowance now also requires `!drainExpired(commandId)`, so the read is refused and the parent stays `incomplete` with its residuals. Proven by F7.
- **Major — a thrown broker read or timeout skipped settlement.** The read escaped the pass to the outer catch, leaving the durable parent `executing` and blocking Resume until another reconciliation ran. The read is now caught inside the pass as a failed read, and the `recordFlattenHoldings` call is caught too, so the pass re-reads the outcome and the third failure settles in the same pass. Proven by F6.

The other prior findings were already resolved at `cb3cde11` and are unchanged.

### Merge from `origin/main`

The branch merged `origin/main` at `94d55718` (P42 #1442, `91377d46`). The merge touched `thala_control_store.cjs`, `thala_control_coordinator.cjs` and `thala_control_reads.cjs`, so the committed proof receipt no longer matched the checkout. `evidence/SRW-1468/proof-after.txt` was regenerated at `f923b4cf`; `--receipt` prints `RECEIPT OK` and the proof is 9/9 on the merged head. Both fixes are unchanged by the merge.

### Reviewer for this round

`python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review router` is not present in this repository, so the reviewer was chosen from the router catalog instead: `task/review` first (the provider could not start the turn), then `claudeAgent` / `claude-sonnet-5-5` at `effort: high`. It reviewed `82f51b8a` and returned no Critical or Major findings. It confirmed both fixes and re-ran the proof with each fix reverted: F7 fails without the deadline check, F6 fails without the read catch, and F7 fails without the record catch. Its three Minor findings are under `Left for later`.

## Checks

Builder check: PASS f923b4cf2abf22370780f7554d6749a6f1553cfc

- `NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 node scripts/srw1468_flatten_fixed_point_proof.cjs` — 9/9.
- `NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 node scripts/srw1390_flatten_settle_proof.cjs` — 9/9.
- `NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 node scripts/srw1390_flatten_fence_proof.cjs` — 34/35. R13 is the pre-existing failure documented in `evidence/SRW-1390-settle/README.md`; it fails identically at the base.
- `test_srw15_order_path_review.js`, `scripts/srw1344_manual_exit_posts_proof.cjs` (15/15), `scripts/srw1345_exit_all_proof.cjs` (20/20), `test_srw1341_manual_exit_admission.js`, `test_srw1245_manual_close_isolation.js` (9/9) — pass.
- `node scripts/srw_review_scope.cjs` — `review: opus` for the coordinator and store, as expected for an order-path change.

## Left for later

- Minor, `thala_control_coordinator.cjs:610`: the record catch swallows every error, not only `flatten_holdings_premature`, so a dropped successful read leaves no trace. The retry keeps it safe.
- Minor, `thala_control_coordinator.cjs:594-597` and `:608-609`, `thala_control_store.cjs:1060-1063`: the new comments are multi-line and partly restate the code; the read-catch comment and the second sentence of the store comment are candidates to trim under the `no-comments` rule.
- Minor, `evidence/SRW-1468/README.md`: one short wrapped line ("to reserve, so the") left over from the paragraph edit. Cosmetic.
- The three-pass bound is on the broker reconciliation, not the pre-fence drain. The drain keeps its 120-second settle limit from P01 part 2. This is the reading in `docs/parity/index.html` ("drains every earlier submission ... and repeats broker reconciliation. After three passes or 120 seconds it reports incomplete or unknown with residuals"). A hard three-pass bound on the drain itself would change the outcomes of the existing fence and settle proofs, which assert a parent stays `pending` while a pre-fence buy works.
- Activation waits for P54 (#1464) and for the 120-second limit to be measured against staging entry lifetimes.
- `scripts/srw1390_flatten_fence_proof.cjs` R13 is the pre-existing failure documented in `evidence/SRW-1390-settle/README.md`; not caused by this ticket.

### Branch update

Merged `origin/main` (`91377d46`, `93c71f41`) into the branch with no conflicts at `94d55718`. The merge changed `thala_control_store.cjs`, `thala_control_coordinator.cjs` and `thala_control_reads.cjs`, so the committed proof receipt no longer matched; `evidence/SRW-1468/proof-after.txt` was regenerated at `f923b4cf` and `--receipt` prints `RECEIPT OK`. The ticket proofs were re-run on the merge result: `srw1468_flatten_fixed_point_proof.cjs` 9/9, `srw1390_flatten_settle_proof.cjs` 9/9, `srw1390_flatten_fence_proof.cjs` 34/35 (R13, the pre-existing failure documented in `evidence/SRW-1390-settle/README.md`). The release gate is `srw/agent-check` on this head.

`srw/agent-check` on the exact PR head: `success` — "Clean exact-SHA PR tier passed".

 3. **Should Exit all remain on the dashboard once Flatten exists?** The design
    says yes, for the reason in the comparison table. If review disagrees, the
    change is to hide one button, not to change the fan-out.
+
+---
+
+# P01b: fixed point and boot resume
+
+Status: built disabled. Paper only. No deploy, no live activation.
+
+Refs #1468 (P01b), #1390 (P01), #1391 (P02), #1387. Milestone M1. The parity
+design is `docs/parity/index.html`; the ticket plan is `docs/parity/tickets.md`.
+
+## What this contract adds
+
+P01 (#1390) built the durable admission fence: a flatten commits its pause
+generation and the set of entries admitted before it, then sends one exit per
+confirmed row, and never sends an exit into a contract a pre-fence buy can still
+fill. P02 (#1391) holds a manual exit on a working entry until the fill state is
+known. This contract closes the two gaps those parts left open:
+
+1. **A fixed point.** A flatten always ends `flat`, `incomplete` or `unknown`
+   with residuals. It never waits forever on a broker read that cannot be taken.
+2. **Boot resume.** A process that restarts mid-flatten resumes the pending
+   parent and its existing child ids, refuses the rows it did not fence, and
+   reaches the same fixed point without sending a duplicate order.
+
+## The fixed point
+
+The parent outcome is a reducer over durable records only: the snapshot rows,
+the child command rows, the fence, the drain evidence and the last broker
+holdings read. No caller asserts an outcome.
+
+- A row is `filled` only when its child ended `done` with `executorState:
+  filled`; its residual is then zero.
+- A row is `refused` when its child ended `failed` with a known residual or an
+  admission stamp of `false`; its residual is the ledger's, bounded by the
+  confirmed quantity. A late fill above the confirmed quantity is `null`
+  (unknown), never the larger number.
+- A row is `unknown` when its child ended without a readable outcome, or timed
+  out. It is never zero.
+- The parent is `flat` only when every row is `filled` with a zero residual, no
+  row was excluded, and the broker's own holdings read shows zero for every
+  contract in scope. A refused row with a zero residual is still not flat. The
+  snapshot rows alone never make a parent flat.
+- The parent is `incomplete` when a row was refused or excluded, or when the
+  broker reconciliation reached its bound without a complete read.
+- The parent is `unknown` when a row or the fence cannot be read, or when a
+  working exit is still in progress at the settle limit. The working child keeps
+  its durable identity and its residual stays `null`.
+
+## The three-pass bound
+
+The drain of pre-fence buys is bounded by the 120-second settle limit measured
+from the fence's durable audit time (P01 part 2). The broker reconciliation that
+follows the drain repeats up to **three reserved reads or the settle limit**,
+whichever comes first. Each actual broker read is written as a durable
+`flatten_pass:` audit record before it runs, including a fence invocation that
+reaches the holdings phase, so:
+
+- a restart resumes the same budget instead of starting over;
+- a read that crashes still counts;
+- the bound is the same for every caller.
+
+The third read is still allowed to succeed. If it fails, the parent reports
+`incomplete` with its residuals and the holdings it did read in the same pass,
+never `flat` and never `pending` forever. A crash after the third reservation
+settles on the next pass or on recovery. An empty book has no read to reserve,
+so the 120-second settle limit bounds it. A working exit is a legitimate exit in
+progress: it is allowed to work until the settle limit, where the parent reports
+`unknown` with the working child's residual `null` and keeps the child identity
+for continued reconciliation.
+
+The bound is implemented in `thala_control_store.cjs` (`reconcileExpired`,
+`recordFlattenPass`) and driven by `thala_control_coordinator.cjs`
+(`reconcileFlatten`). It adds no order path: the only send is still the existing
+manual exit behind the existing per-row gate.
+
+## Boot resume
+
+On boot the coordinator reads every unresolved command row from the store.
+
+- A flatten parent in `requested` or `accepted` never reached its fence, so it
+  fails with `restart_before_execution` and attempts no exit.
+- A flatten parent in `executing` or `timed_out` with a committed pause effect
+  stays open and is reconciled. Without the pause effect it fails.
+- A child in `requested` or `accepted` is failed with `restart_before_execution`
+  and sends nothing.
+- A child in `executing` or `timed_out` is reconciled from the executor's own
+  record, exactly as a manual exit is.
+- A snapshot row with no child is refused on its own child row with
+  `restart_before_execution` and its residual. Only the process that fenced a
+  parent sends its exits, so boot never sends one.
+
+Existing child ids and pending attempts are preserved: the resume never creates
+a second child for a trade that already has one, and the idempotency key
+`flatten:<parent>:<trade>` makes a replay return the existing row.
+
+## Resume entries
+
+`resume_entries` is refused with `flatten_in_progress` while a live flatten owns
+the generation: a parent is in progress until it ends or every snapshot row has
+a child past `requested`. A terminal flatten leaves the pause in place, so the
+operator resumes explicitly. The pause is never lifted by the flatten itself.
+
+## Rollback
+
+Disable `THALA_CONTROL_FLATTEN_ENABLED` (and the exit-all and manual-exit flags
+it depends on). A parent already fenced keeps reconciling whatever the flags
+say, so a rollback never strands one. Reconciliation sends and cancels nothing.
+The journal cursors, client ids and cumulative fills are untouched. Qualify the
+old reader before resuming the old policy: the new records are audit events
+(`flatten_pass:`), not new columns, so an older reader can still write a command
+after a rollback.
+
+## Activation
+
+Build and merge disabled. Activation waits for P54 (#1464, compatibility and
+rollback qualification) and for the 120-second limit to be measured against
+staging entry lifetimes. The paper-service evidence is a separate activation
+gate.
+
+## Evidence
+
+`evidence/SRW-1468/` holds the proof receipt and the before/after runs.
+`scripts/srw1468_flatten_fixed_point_proof.cjs` drives the real executor, the
+real coordinator and the real SQLite store through the real card intake, entry
+send and manual exit paths, with a credential-free fake broker.

+'use strict';
+
+// SRW-1393 (P01b) replays, offline and paper only: the flatten fixed point and
+// boot resume. Each replay drives the real Thala executor, the real control
+// coordinator and the real SQLite control store through the real card intake,
+// entry send and manual exit paths. Only the broker is fake: it holds orders and
+// positions in memory, needs no credential and opens no network socket. Every
+// expected outcome is read back from the store and the broker; no replay writes
+// the outcome it checks.
+//
+// The store stamps the fence with its own clock (Date.now) and measures the
+// settle limit from that durable time. The replays move one shared wall clock
+// that the coordinator and the store both read, as in service.
+//
+// Each replay is independent, and the script runs every replay even when one
+// fails, so a run against origin/main reports each replay's own before result.
+
+const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
+const crypto = require('node:crypto');
+const fs = require('node:fs');
+const os = require('node:os');
+const path = require('node:path');
+const Module = require('node:module');
+const storeModule = require('../thala_control_store.cjs');
+const { createControlCoordinator, controlFlags } = require('../thala_control_coordinator.cjs');
+const { setControlReceipt } = require('../thala_control_receipt.cjs');
+const { createThalaFeed } = require('../thala_v2_feed.js');
+const { createThalaV2Executor } = require('../thala_v2_executor.js');
+const { hashBody } = require('../thala_control_contract.cjs');
+
+const FIXTURE = path.join(__dirname, '../fixtures/thala_v2/thala_test_1.json');
+const NOW = Date.parse('2026-11-03T14:40:00Z');
+const ACCOUNT = 'a'.repeat(64);
+const SYMBOL = 'TSLA261106C00400000';
+const OTHER = 'TSLA261106C00410000';
+const THIRD = 'TSLA261106C00420000';
+const PAPER = { origin: 'https://paper-api.alpaca.markets', accountId: 'paper-1', expectedAccountId: 'paper-1', keyContext: 'paper', redirect: 'error' };
+const ON = { THALA_CONTROL_ENABLED: '1', THALA_CONTROL_PAUSE_ENABLED: '1', THALA_CONTROL_MANUAL_EXIT_ENABLED: '1', THALA_CONTROL_EXIT_ALL_ENABLED: '1', THALA_CONTROL_FLATTEN_ENABLED: '1' };
+const LIMIT_MS = 120_000;
+const PASS_LIMIT = 3;
+const realOpen = storeModule.openControlStore;
+const wall = { now: Date.now() };
+Date.now = () => wall.now;
+const settle = async (n = 60) => { for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) await new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve)); };
+const deferred = () => { let resolve; const promise = new Promise(r => { resolve = r; }); return { promise, resolve }; };
+
+function cardDoc(tradeId, symbol = SYMBOL) {
+  const doc = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(FIXTURE, 'utf8'));
+  delete doc.test_note;
+  doc.trade_id = tradeId; doc.id = `SURATAI_MUDI_TSLA-${symbol}`; doc.sent = new Date(NOW).toISOString();
+  doc.option = { ...doc.option, symbol, occ21: `TSLA  ${symbol.slice(4)}`, strike: Number(symbol.slice(-8)) / 1000 };
+  // An option-priced stop, so the exit pass reads the bid the operator confirms.
+  doc.stop = { ...doc.stop, basis: 'option_pct', option_pct: -50, underlying_price: null, underlying_cross: null };
+  return doc;
+}
+
+// The fake broker: orders, fills and positions in memory. The position is the
+// net of filled buys and sells, so a holdings read is derived from the orders the
+// executor actually sent, never set by a replay.
+function fakeBroker() {
+  const orders = new Map(), submitted = [], canceled = [];
+  let serial = 0;
+  const gates = {}, state = { lookupDown: false, controlLookupDown: false }, hooks = {};
+  const position = symbol => [...orders.values()].filter(row => row.symbol === symbol)
+    .reduce((sum, row) => sum + (row.side === 'buy' ? 1 : -1) * Number(row.filled_qty || 0), 0);
+  const broker = {
+    paperIdentity: () => ({ ...PAPER }),
+    getPaperAccountFingerprint: async () => ACCOUNT,
+    getUnderlyingPrice: async () => 400.41,
+    getEquity: async () => 1000000,
+    getBuyingPower: async () => 1000000,
+    getOptionQuote: async () => ({ bid: 6.05, ask: 6.15, at: NOW }),
+    getCloseEvidence: async symbol => ({ position: { symbol, qty: String(position(symbol)) }, orders: [...orders.values()].filter(row => row.symbol === symbol).map(row => ({ ...row })) }),
+    submitOrder: async order => {
+      if (gates.send && order.side === 'buy') { const gate = gates.send; delete gates.send; gate.entered.resolve(); await gate.release.promise; }
+      const reason = order.beforeSend?.();
+      if (reason) throw Object.assign(new Error(reason), { code: reason, notSent: true });
+      const { beforeSend, ...fields } = order;
+      const row = { ...fields, id: `o${++serial}`, status: 'new', filled_qty: '0', submitted_at: new Date(NOW).toISOString() };
+      orders.set(row.id, row); submitted.push({ ...row }); hooks.onSubmit?.(row);
+      if (gates.ack && order.side === 'buy') {
+        const gate = gates.ack; delete gates.ack; gate.entered.resolve();
+        const outcome = await gate.release.promise;
+        if (outcome === 'lost') throw Object.assign(new Error('socket hang up'), { code: 'ECONNRESET' });
+        if (outcome === 'rejected') { orders.delete(row.id); submitted.pop(); throw Object.assign(new Error('insufficient buying power'), { status: 403 }); }
+      }
+      return { ...row };
+    },
+    replaceOrder: async (id, patch) => {
+      const parent = orders.get(id);
+      const child = { ...parent, ...patch, id: `o${++serial}`, client_order_id: `${parent.client_order_id}-r1`, replaces: parent.id, status: 'new' };
+      parent.status = 'replaced'; parent.replaced_by = child.id; orders.set(child.id, child);
+      return { ...child, _srwOwnership: { parentClientOrderId: parent.client_order_id, rootClientOrderId: parent.client_order_id, ancestors: [parent] } };
+    },
+    getOrder: async id => ({ ...orders.get(id) }),
+    findOrderByClientId: async id => { if (state.lookupDown) throw Object.assign(new Error('lookup unavailable'), { status: 503 }); const row = [...orders.values()].find(value => value.client_order_id === id); return row ? { ...row } : null; },
+    listOrders: async () => [...orders.values()].map(row => ({ ...row })),
+    cancelOrder: async id => { canceled.push(id); orders.get(id).status = 'canceled'; },
+    // The entry control read the executor uses for a bound entry its ledger has
+    // no record of. A missing client id answers 404, as the paper adapter does.
+    getControlOrder: async ({ clientOrderId }) => {
+      if (state.controlLookupDown) throw Object.assign(new Error('http_error'), { status: 503 });
+      const row = [...orders.values()].find(value => value.client_order_id === clientOrderId);
+      if (!row) throw Object.assign(new Error('http_error'), { status: 404 });
+      return { ...row, _controlAncestors: [] };
+    },
+  };
+  const gate = where => { const value = { entered: deferred(), release: deferred() }; gates[where] = value; return value; };
+  const fill = (id, qty = null) => { const row = orders.get(id); row.filled_qty = String(qty ?? row.qty); row.status = Number(row.filled_qty) >= Number(row.qty) ? 'filled' : 'partially_filled'; row.filled_avg_price = row.side === 'buy' ? '6.1' : '6.05'; };
+  const expire = id => { orders.get(id).status = 'expired'; };
+  return { broker, orders, submitted, canceled, position, gate, fill, expire, state, hooks };
+}
+
+// One bot: a real store on disk, the real coordinator and the real executor,
+// wired the way paper_service.js wires them (the coordinator is the executor's
+// control provider). `start` reopens everything from the same files, which is a
+// restart: the new coordinator holds no memory of the parents it fenced.
+async function bot({ dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'srw1468-')), fake = fakeBroker(), modules = {} } = {}) {
+  const ledger = path.join(dir, 'ledger.json');
+  const ledgerStore = { load: () => (fs.existsSync(ledger) ? JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(ledger, 'utf8')) : { trades: {} }),
+    save: image => { fs.writeFileSync(`${ledger}.next`, JSON.stringify(image)); fs.renameSync(`${ledger}.next`, ledger); } };
+  const h = { dir, fake, cards: 0, execNow: NOW };
+  h.start = async () => {
+    h.executor?.stop?.();
+    h.store?.close();
+    storeModule.openControlStore = (_file, identity) => (h.store = (modules.open ?? realOpen)(path.join(dir, 'control.sqlite'), identity));
+    try {
+      h.coordinator = (modules.coordinator?.createControlCoordinator ?? createControlCoordinator)({ accountId: ACCOUNT, secret: Buffer.alloc(32, 7), broker: fake.broker, flags: controlFlags(ON), lockHeld: () => true, clock: () => Date.now() });
+    } finally { storeModule.openControlStore = realOpen; }
+    h.executor = createThalaV2Executor({ broker: fake.broker, entryControlBroker: fake.broker, store: ledgerStore, clock: () => h.execNow, controlProvider: h.coordinator.admissionEnabled ? h.coordinator : null,
+      manualExitEnabled: true, holdMissingPrices: true, keepHighScoreOnPaper: true, caps: { maxContractsPerTrade: 50, bookPremiumUsd: 25000 } });
+    h.coordinator.setExecutor(h.executor);
+    h.coordinator.setLedgerReady((await h.executor.reconcileStartup()).ready);
+    h.coordinator.refreshCache(Date.now());
+    await h.coordinator.refreshIdentity();
+    h.coordinator.reconcileCardHistory({ verified: true });
+    await settle();
+  };
+  h.command = (type, payload = {}) => {
+    const key = `srw1468-${type}-${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
+    return h.coordinator.submit({ body: { type, idempotencyKey: key, expectedPaperAccountId: ACCOUNT, payload }, idempotencyKey: key, actor: 'shyam', expiresAt: Date.now() + 30_000 });
+  };
+  h.wait = async commandId => {
+    for (let n = 0; n < 200; n++) { const row = h.coordinator.lookup({ commandId }); if (['done', 'failed', 'timed_out'].includes(row.state)) return row; await settle(5); }
+    return h.coordinator.lookup({ commandId });
+  };
+  // A card arrives through the real feed, and its receipt is recorded by the
+  // real coordinator at the live pause generation, exactly as discord_source does.
+  h.card = async (tradeId, symbol = SYMBOL) => {
+    const doc = cardDoc(tradeId, symbol);
+    const sourceMessageId = String(1500000000000000000n + BigInt(++h.cards));
+    const message = { id: sourceMessageId, channel: { id: '456' }, text: JSON.stringify({ v: 2, seq: doc.seq, type: doc.type, trade_id: tradeId, full_json: 'x.json' }), attachments: [{ name: 'x.json' }] };
+    setControlReceipt(message, h.coordinator.receiveCard({ messageId: sourceMessageId, channelId: '456' }));
+    let intent;
+    const feed = createThalaFeed({ channelIds: ['456'], fetchAttachmentText: async () => JSON.stringify(doc), onIntent: value => { intent = value; } });
+    assert.equal((await feed.handle(message)).ok, true, 'the card is accepted by the feed');
+    return intent;
+  };
+  h.entryOrder = tradeId => fake.orders.get(h.executor.trades[tradeId].entryOrder.id);
+  // An open, confirmable row: a real entry, filled at the broker, picked up by
+  // the executor's own advance, with the bid the exit pass recorded.
+  h.openRow = async (tradeId, symbol = SYMBOL) => {
+    const intent = await h.card(tradeId, symbol);
+    assert.equal((await h.executor.handle(intent)).ok, true, `${tradeId} is entered`);
+    fake.fill(h.entryOrder(tradeId).id);
+    for (let pass = 0; pass < 4 && !(h.executor.trades[tradeId].lastBid > 0); pass++) { await h.executor.advance(); await settle(); }
+    assert.equal(h.executor.trades[tradeId].state, 'open', `${tradeId} is open`);
+    assert.ok(h.executor.trades[tradeId].lastBid > 0, `${tradeId} has the bid its exit pass saw`);
+    return h.executor.trades[tradeId];
+  };

+    h.coordinator.refreshCache(Date.now());
+    const confirmed = h.coordinator.reads().controlSnapshot.flatten;

+  };

+  await h.start();
+  assert.equal((await h.wait(h.command('resume_entries').command.commandId)).state, 'done', 'entries are running');
+  return h;
+}
+
+const REPLAYS = [];
+const replay = (name, fn) => REPLAYS.push({ name, fn });
+
+// A pre-fence entry held at its acknowledgement: admitted at send, no trade
+// row yet. The flatten is confirmed while it is held.
+async function heldEntry(h, tradeId, symbol = SYMBOL) {
+  const late = await h.card(tradeId, symbol);
+  const ack = h.fake.gate('ack');
+  const entering = h.executor.handle(late);
+  await ack.entered.promise;
+  return { ack, entering };
+}
+const byTrade = outcome => Object.fromEntries(outcome.rows.map(item => [item.tradeId, item]));

+// A store on its own, for the reducer contracts that do not need the executor.
+const STORE_ID = { accountId: 'paper-1', botId: 'thala' };
+function storeOnly() {
+  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'srw1468-store-'));
+  const store = realOpen(path.join(dir, 'control.sqlite'), STORE_ID);

+  store.setPause({ mode: 'running', expectedGeneration: 0, actor: 'operator' });

+}
+
+// F1: three open rows on three contracts, and a pre-fence buy on the third
+// contract. The flatten sends the first two exits and cannot send the third
+// while the buy works. The process is killed between the second and third
+// child. The restart resumes the parent and the two existing child ids, refuses
+// the unsent row on its own child row, and reaches incomplete with no duplicate
+// order. Resume is refused while the flatten owns the generation and admitted
+// once it is terminal, leaving the pause for the operator.
+async function killBetweenChildren(modules) {
+  const h = await bot({ modules });
+  try {
+    await h.openRow('TH-261120-10001');
+    await h.openRow('TH-261120-10002', OTHER);
+    await h.openRow('TH-261120-10003', THIRD);

+    const commandId = created.command.commandId;
+    await settle();
+    ack.release.resolve('ok'); await entering;
+    await h.executor.advance(); await h.drain(); await h.executor.advance();

+    assert.deepEqual(h.sells().map(sell => sell.symbol).sort(), [OTHER, SYMBOL].sort(), 'the two clear rows exit');

+    const refused = await h.wait(h.command('resume_entries').command.commandId);
+    assert.equal(refused.state, 'failed'); assert.equal(refused.outcome.reason, 'flatten_in_progress');
+    assert.equal(h.coordinator.getPause().mode, 'paused', 'entries stay fenced');
+    // Kill and restart: the new process did not fence the parent. The pre-fence
+    // buy ends before the restart, so the drain is settled and the unsent row is
+    // the only thing left to account for.
+    h.fake.expire(h.entryOrder('TH-261120-10004').id);
+    await h.start();
+    assert.equal(h.coordinator.health().ready, true, 'control recovers with the parent scoped');
+    const resumed = h.parent(commandId);
+    assert.ok(childIds.every(id => resumed.children.some(child => child.command_id === id)), 'the existing child ids are resumed unchanged');
+    for (let pass = 0; pass < 4; pass++) await h.pass();
+    assert.equal(h.sells().length, 2, 'the restart sent no duplicate exit');
+    const row = await h.wait(commandId);
+    assert.equal(row.state, 'done', 'the parent reaches a fixed point');
+    assert.equal(row.outcome.state, 'incomplete', 'the refused row keeps it from flat');
+    const rows = byTrade(row.outcome);
+    assert.equal(rows['TH-261120-10001'].state, 'filled', 'the first child is flat');
+    assert.equal(rows['TH-261120-10002'].state, 'filled', 'the second child is flat');
+    assert.equal(rows['TH-261120-10003'].state, 'refused'); assert.equal(rows['TH-261120-10003'].reason, 'restart_before_execution', 'the unsent row is refused on its own child row');

Refs #1468

P01b closes the two gaps P01 (#1390) and P02 (#1391) left in the flatten path: a flatten now always reaches a fixed point, and a process that restarts mid-flatten resumes the pending parent and its existing child ids without sending a duplicate order.

## What changed

- **The broker reconciliation is bounded at three reserved reads or the 120-second settle limit.** Each actual broker read is written as a durable `flatten_pass:` audit record before it runs, including a fence invocation that reaches the holdings phase, so a restart resumes the same budget and a read that crashes still counts. The third read is still allowed to succeed, but only before the settle limit: a read that starts before the limit and finishes after it is refused, so a zero balance never marks the parent `flat` past the deadline. If the third read fails or throws, the parent reports `incomplete` with its residuals in the same pass, never `flat` and never `pending` forever. A crash after the third reservation settles on the next pass or on recovery. An empty book has no read to reserve, so the settle limit bounds it. The pre-fence drain keeps its 120-second settle limit from P01 part 2.
- **A refused row is never flat.** The reducer now requires every row to be `filled` with a zero residual, not just to carry a zero residual. A refused row with a zero residual and a complete zero broker read ends `incomplete` and posts `FLATTEN INCOMPLETE`.
