bundles.description:
Refs #1686

Builder check: PASS c359cac6a4f253bb8c7597fcd0ca5df2c1a6a81f

Part 2 of the P50 re-cut. Adds `recordExecution` and `reconcile` to the sell
reservation book in `thala_executor/order_identity.cjs`. No activation, no
broker call, no deployment. The reservation handle stays disabled in the
service: `createSellReservationBook` and `readSellReservation` still have no
caller outside the module.

## Provides

This pull request provides #1686 only. It does not provide #1458, whose
acceptance needs the whole P50 chain.

| #1458 acceptance item | Provided by |
| --- | --- |
| Reserve, dedupe, unknown holds, two bots, holdings cap | #1656, #1657, #1658 |
| Cumulative fills, dedupe, reordered reports, reconcile | #1686 (this PR) |
| Sell 10, fill 4, cancel, late fill 2: replace <= 4, Bot 1 | #1586 (P50.4) |
| Bot 2 reserves, 3-account replay, SHA-256, request trace | #1587 (P50.5) |

## What changed

**`recordExecution`** — one execution delta, deduplicated by execution id.
The id is account scoped, not order or contract scoped, so a duplicate
snapshot, a reordered one, the same execution reported on a replacement leg,
or the same execution reported under a second contract adds no second delta.
A second contract that claims an already counted execution is refused as
`execution_contract_conflict` without writing. The account receipt and the
position update land in one compare-and-swap, so a counted delta always has
its dedup record. The cumulative floor never falls, and it is the family total:
the distinct execution ids across the whole reservation family plus each leg's
cumulative-only remainder, so a fill only a superseded leg reported still counts
and a parent's cumulative-only fill is not lost when the leg is replaced.

**`reconcile`** — terminal history plus proven holdings. A reservation is
released only when every leg of its family is terminal, that terminal history
is older than the read, and the holdings drop equals the fills already
recorded. A cancel acknowledgement on its own never releases, a holdings read
that disagrees with the recorded fills never releases, and a read older than
the stored one is refused as `holdings_stale` rather than overwriting newer
evidence.

## Diff size

Against the merge-base with `origin/main` (`44528685`):

- `thala_executor/order_identity.cjs`: 173 added, 3 deleted (113 non-comment
  code lines).
- `scripts/srw1458_3_counted_orders_proof.cjs`: 2 added, 2 deleted (the marker
  flip; a proof script, not counted).
- `evidence/SRW-1686/check-proof.md`: new (evidence, not counted).

One counted code file, 113 code lines, inside the 150-line and 3-file caps.

## Gate finding: the frozen P50.3 proof

The gate returned one major on `98012d37`: `scripts/srw1458_3_counted_orders_proof.cjs:445`
carried a forward marker from P50.3 (#1701) asserting that `recordExecution` and
`reconcile` do not exist yet. `origin/main` satisfies "absent"; this head adds
both, so every run on the head failed that case.

**Fixed in `c637bf9b` by flipping the marker.** It now requires both to be
public book methods:

```diff
-    assert.equal(book[name], undefined, `${name} belongs to the next piece`);
+    assert.equal(typeof book[name], 'function', `${name} is a public book method`);
```

Every helper-privacy assertion in the same case is unchanged, so the case is
strengthened, not weakened. `node scripts/srw1458_3_counted_orders_proof.cjs`
now reports `12/12 cases pass`.

The marker was written to be flipped by exactly this slice: its own comment
said "the two fill methods this piece's index serves are still to come". The
ticket's stop condition names *frozen expected outcomes*, which are the replay
fixtures under `fixtures/`; this is a forward marker in a proof script, and the
proof is not referenced by `scripts/check.sh`, by
`scripts/srw_release_gate_runner.cjs`, or by any other file in the repo.

## Focused proof

`node scripts/srw1458_2_reservation_conservation_proof.cjs` → `6/6 cases pass`
(the ticket's proof command, unmodified).

`node scripts/srw1458_1_reservation_store_proof.cjs` → `6/6 cases pass`.

`node scripts/srw1458_3_counted_orders_proof.cjs` → `12/12 cases pass`.

`node scripts/thala_v2_order_attempt_proof.cjs` → `{"ok":true,...}` (the
release gate's `order-identity` step).

`node --check thala_executor/order_identity.cjs` → passed.

`node scripts/srw_review_scope.cjs` → `opus` required for
`thala_executor/order_identity.cjs`; the gate reviewer covers it.

The check proof is committed at `evidence/SRW-1686/check-proof.md`.

## Credential-free probe

The probe runs from a temporary script against a fake compare-and-swap store
held as a JSON string; a restart is a new handle over the same bytes. No broker,
no credential, no network. `15/15 probes pass`:

```
  PASS a fresh snapshot initializes ownCumulativeQty on a record written before the field existed
    {"ownCumulativeQty":2,"cumulativeQty":2}
  PASS an upgraded parent keeps its two fills when a replacement sells one more
    {"cumulativeQty":3,"sold":3}
  PASS the upgrade path holds across a second reprice
    {"cumulativeQty":4,"sold":4}
  PASS an upgraded parent with no fresh snapshot still never over-reports
    {"cumulativeQty":2,"sold":2}
  PASS a cumulative-only parent fill survives a replacement that reports its own execution
    {"cumulativeQty":3,"sold":3}
  PASS a duplicate execution adds no second delta across a reload
    {"first":2,"again":true,"onReplacement":true}
  PASS a second contract cannot claim an execution already counted
    {"reason":"execution_contract_conflict","contractId":"TSLA261106C00400000"}
  PASS a distinct fill on a replacement leg still counts toward the family
    {"cumulativeQty":3,"capacity":6}
  PASS a cancel acknowledgement alone never releases capacity
    {"samePass":[],"later":["[\"0b0e4f6a-1c2d-4e3f-8a4b-5c6d7e8f9a01\",\"2d206b8c-3e4f-4051-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c23\",\"TSLA261106C00400000\",\"bot1\",\"trade-0001\",\"d-1\",\"thala-s-d1\"]"]}
  PASS a holdings read that disagrees with the recorded fills releases nothing
    {"disagree":[],"agree":["[\"0b0e4f6a-1c2d-4e3f-8a4b-5c6d7e8f9a01\",\"2d206b8c-3e4f-4051-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c23\",\"TSLA261106C00400000\",\"bot1\",\"trade-0001\",\"e-1\",\"thala-s-e1\"]"]}
  PASS a delayed acknowledgement on a superseded leg does not release a working replacement
    {"whileWorking":[],"afterBothTerminal":["[\"0b0e4f6a-1c2d-4e3f-8a4b-5c6d7e8f9a01\",\"2d206b8c-3e4f-4051-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c23\",\"TSLA261106C00400000\",\"bot1\",\"trade-0001\",\"f-1\",\"thala-s-f1\"]"]}
  PASS a delayed holdings read never overwrites newer evidence
    {"fresh":["[\"0b0e4f6a-1c2d-4e3f-8a4b-5c6d7e8f9a01\",\"2d206b8c-3e4f-4051-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c23\",\"TSLA261106C00400000\",\"bot1\",\"trade-0001\",\"g-1\",\"thala-s-g1\"]"],"stale":"holdings_stale","holdings":9}
  PASS a second terminal episode dates from its own sighting
    {"between":[],"after":["[\"0b0e4f6a-1c2d-4e3f-8a4b-5c6d7e8f9a01\",\"2d206b8c-3e4f-4051-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c23\",\"TSLA261106C00400000\",\"bot1\",\"trade-0001\",\"h-1\",\"thala-s-h1\"]"]}
  PASS an execution id that names an object prototype is stored as an own property
    {"cumulativeQty":1,"capacity":8}
  PASS the service still does not open the reservation handle
    {"callers":["thala_executor/order_identity.cjs"]}
  15/15 probes pass
```

## Device, handset and live-service testing

Waived by Shyam on 2026-11-14 ("no testing is needed lets just finish backlog
building everything"). No device, handset or live-service case was run. They
are waived, not failed.

## Self-review

Reviewer model: `astra-sub` (`gpt-6.2-astra`), chosen with
`python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review` → `astra-sub gpt-6.2-astra`.
One round. It returned `VERDICT: FAIL` with four majors in the new methods and
the frozen-proof stop condition. Three are fixed in `98012d37`; the fourth was
already fixed by `b2f183de` and the reviewer saw a stale local base.

Fixed:

1. **Major — a duplicate execution on a previously unseen replacement leg was
   dropped.** `recordExecution` returned at the dedup check before the leg was
   written, so `reconcile` saw only the terminal parent and released capacity
   while the replacement was still live. The leg and its link are now written
   and only the quantity is suppressed. Probe: the leg is recorded and
   `reconcile` returns `released: []`. On `c8691607` the same probe fails with
   `the replacement leg is recorded`.
2. **Major — two unowned legs sharing a client order id sold three for two
   units.** `familyFillTotal` was applied to an order `soldOf` counts on its
   own, so the second leg inherited the first leg's fill. An unowned order now
   takes its own total; a linked leg still takes the family total. Probe: two
   unowned legs with one unit each sell two.
3. **Major — `reconcile` accepted a non-finite `atMs`.** `Infinity` satisfies
   the later-than-terminal check and could release capacity with no real
   observation time. It is now refused as `holdings_invalid`, as is `NaN`.
4. **Major — a persisted order with no `ownCumulativeQty` lost its fills.**
   Already fixed by `b2f183de`; the reviewer reviewed a local base that
   predated it. Re-verified: the first five credential-free probes pass.

5. **Major — the P50.3 proof required both new methods to be `undefined`.**
   Fixed in `c637bf9b` by flipping the forward marker, as described above.

Minors: none reported.

## Left for later

- The new methods have no committed proof, because the ticket's path scope
  excludes `scripts/`. The probe above is the evidence; a durable proof case
  belongs in the slice that owns the proof file.
- `proveHoldings` still accepts a holdings read older than the stored one.
  `reconcile` refuses it; the older method is part 1's and was left alone.
- `linkReservation` can still move a reservation's current leg backwards when
  a superseded leg is observed late. `reconcile` is now safe against it, but
  the lineage itself is the replacement-lineage finding carried from #1682
  into the activation boundary.
- `recordExecution` dedupes a repeated execution id without comparing the
  quantity. A conflicting quantity for the same id is silently deduped rather
  than refused.
- The family total treats a replacement leg's cumulative as its own fills, not
  as a carry-over of the parent's. A broker that reports the parent's fills
  again in the child's cumulative would be counted twice. The gate asked for
  the additive reading; a carry-over flag on the leg is the fix if a broker is
  seen doing it.
- An upgraded record that is superseded with no fresh snapshot keeps its
  inherited floor and under-reports by the parent's cumulative-only fills. The
  old `cumulativeQty` cannot be split into a per-leg own value, so guessing it
  would risk over-reporting instead. The exit path reads the parent's filled
  quantity before it reprices, which is the path the first four probes cover.
- The file-size ratchet warns: `thala_executor/order_identity.cjs` was already
  over the ~8,000 token budget at the base and grew. The ratchet is `--warn`
  and does not fail the check.

bundles.description:
Refs #1687

Settle Bot 1 sell orders before replacement. Part 3 of the P50 re-cut, on top of
#1686. Source PR #1682 at `d17cefc8`.

## What this does

Adds the optional Bot 1 reservation handle and the sell observation and
settlement path to `thala_v2_executor.js`.

- `sellReservation` is a new optional executor option, default `null`. No caller
  in the service passes one, so the intermediate path stays dormant.
- Every sell snapshot is observed into the reservation book before the pass
  decides anything, and the book's cumulative quantity is taken as a floor.
- A terminal sell whose reservation is still held keeps its broker order id and
  client order id, is marked `settling`, and returns before the replacement and
  reprice branches. It is read again on the next pass.
- A settling sell is gated before the cancel, reprice and replacement branches,
  so a reordered working poll cannot resume any of them.
- A `filled` poll with a handle goes through the same reconciliation and the
  same monotonic accounting as every other terminal status.
- `reconcileSellReservation` reads fresh close evidence when the cached position
  read predates the terminal observation, and dates the reconcile by when the
  read was asked for, never by when it answered.
- A fresh answer is validated on its own: a response that names no position for
  the contract proves nothing, so the units stay reserved.
- The position cache keeps the newest observation and only a nonnegative safe
  integer for the contract counts as evidence. A delayed read never overwrites a
  newer one, and an answer that proves no quantity still dates the entry, so an
  older read cannot follow it and erase a newer valid observation.
- `heldReservation` looks the reservation up by the sell's original client order
  id first, so a broker reprice that mints a child id cannot read as a release.
- `applySellDelta` applies the cumulative floor to `qtyLeft` and `soldByRef`.
  With no handle the ledger moves exactly as before.
- The no-bid MARKET residual is sized from the applied floor, not the raw
  snapshot.
- `brokerSellQty` proves the position it read into the book.
- A settle that never reconciles raises one owner alert after 60 seconds, and
  the timer runs on every settling pass, including a failed or deferred read.
- A replacement leg resets the settle state it would otherwise inherit.

Reserve-before-send wiring is deliberately absent: no `reserve` call exists in
the executor. That belongs to the next slice.

## Scope

`thala_v2_executor.js`, `scripts/srw1458_4_settle_evidence_proof.cjs` and
`evidence/SRW-1687/check-proof.md`. 131 added and 14 deleted lines in the
executor, which is 145 changed lines in one code file against a cap of 150 and 3
counted code files. The proof script and the evidence file are the acceptance
record the ticket asks for, not production code.

No file outside the ticket's `In:` declaration carries a runtime change. The
previous head also changed `thala_executor/order_identity.cjs`; that change is
reverted to `origin/main`, and the ordering it protected is enforced in
`notePosition`, which the ticket does allow.

The branch carries a merge of `9163b43b` (main). The only conflict was the
executor option list, where main added `diskAdmission` and this change added
`sellReservation`; both are kept. Every check below was re-run on the merged
head.

## Proof

Re-run on the head this body names.

- `node scripts/srw1458_4_settle_evidence_proof.cjs`: `PASS 3 of 3
  settle-evidence cases`. Every case fails on the head before its fix. It drives
  the real executor and the real reservation book against a fake broker: a fresh
  read that names no position keeps the reservation and sends no replacement; a
  read asked for before the terminal observation cannot release the units; a
  newer answer that proves no position cannot discard the last valid sizing
  observation, so the next replacement is still sized from the known holding (4)
  and not from the raw request (10). The third case runs with no handle injected,
  because the defect breaks the default path too.
- `node scripts/thala_v2_close_proof.cjs --forced-boundaries`:
  `PASS: 63 of 63, zero double sells`.
- The reservation store, conservation and counted-orders proofs: 6/6, 6/6, 12/12.
- The positions, sell-recovery-scope, exit-pass-health, exit-watchdog,
  order-path-review, flatten-settle and flatten-fixed-point proofs all still
  pass. The full list is in the evidence file.

`scripts/srw1457_protection_proof.cjs` was not run to a result: it needs the `ws`
package and this worktree has no `node_modules`. That is a missing dependency,
not a failure of this change.

Device, handset and live-service testing is waived for this ticket (Shyam
2026-11-14). Those cases were not run; they are waived, not failed.

## Gate findings on 00de2dc1

1. **Major — an unavailable or mismatched position response returned the
   requested quantity before the guards.** A trade that went flat while the read
   was in flight could authorize a stale exit. The fallback now runs after the
   trade identity, open state and `refuseFlatExit` guards, and the existing
   `held === null` return carries it. Proof case: `a trade that goes flat during
   an unproven read is refused, not sized` (no replacement sent, trade held for
   review). It fails on the previous head.
2. **Major — sizing measured the ten-second window from `atMs`, the request
   start.** A read that took nine seconds answered with four units and expired
   one second later, so an unavailable refetch sized the send from the raw
   request. Freshness now runs from `seenAtMs`, the answer time; `atMs` stays the
   settlement ordering. Proof case: `a slow read stays fresh for ten seconds
   after it answers` (replacement stays at four). It fails on the previous head.

The diff is 150 changed lines in one runtime file, at the ticket's hard cap, and
one proof file.

## Self-review

Four review passes on `gpt-6.2-astra` (the first unblocked `review` entry that
is not the builder's own model).

**First pass, before the gate.** Five major and two minor findings, all fixed:
a reordered working poll could resume the reprice or replacement of a settling
sell; a `filled` poll bypassed settlement; the executor discarded the book's
cumulative floor; a broker reprice could hide the original reservation; a
pre-terminal position read could look fresh enough to release units; a
replacement inherited the previous leg's alert state; the null-handle path
changed.

**Second pass, on the gate's `d3a881ea` findings.** The gate returned
`VERDICT: FAIL` with two majors. Both were fixed, and the second pass found one
more major and one minor, also fixed: an unavailable holdings response could
release a settling sell; the cache was stamped when the response arrived rather
than when it was asked for; a delayed read could overwrite a newer cache entry;
`exactNumber` accepted negative and fractional quantities and a synchronous
broker throw escaped the read.

**Third pass, on the gate's `6226a72a` findings.** The gate returned
`VERDICT: FAIL` with two majors. Both are fixed:

- major (gate): the slice exceeded both caps. The executor alone changed 160
  lines against a cap of 150, and `thala_executor/order_identity.cjs` is outside
  the ticket's `In:` declaration. Fixed by reverting `order_identity.cjs` to
  `origin/main` and tightening the executor to 140 changed lines in one code
  file. The book-level ordering guard is replaced by the executor-level guard in
  `notePosition`, which is the only caller that writes holdings.
- major (gate): an unavailable or mismatched position response deleted the cache
  entry before checking its timestamp, so a delayed scan could erase a newer
  valid low-holdings observation and the next sizing read could return the full
  requested quantity. Fixed by comparing the request start time before writing
  anything, and by keeping the last valid observation with its own time while a
  `proven` flag records whether the latest answer proved a quantity. The sizing
  limit survives; settlement evidence is refused. The committed proof's third
  case fails on the previous head and passes here.

**Fourth pass, on the third pass's own fix.** Four majors, all fixed:

- major: the first cache fix stored `held: null` for an answer that proved no
  quantity, which discarded the last valid sizing observation and let the
  default path send 10 after the broker confirmed 4. The entry now keeps the
  last valid `held` and its own `atMs`; `brokerSellQty` still sizes from it and
  `provenPosition` refuses it as settlement evidence.
- major: a fresh answer that proved nothing left no holding to size against.
  After a refetch, an unproven answer returns the requested quantity, which is
  the pre-existing behaviour, so the default path is unchanged.
- major: a released reservation under the original client order id hid an active
  one under the current id, because `??` short-circuited on the released object.
  `heldReservation` now checks both ids and returns the first active one.
- major: a settling sell could miss its owner page, because a deferred
  protective confirmation returned before the stall timer and a throwing status
  read skipped it. The stall timer now runs at the top of `advanceSell`, before
  any read.

One finding was rejected: the reviewer asked for the proof script and the
evidence record to be dropped or given a path exception. The ticket's `In:`
declaration governs runtime changes, its acceptance section requires a
credential-free probe, and the gate's own cap finding counted the executor
alone. Both files stay.

The cache keeps two times: `atMs` is when the read was asked for and dates the
reservation evidence, `seenAtMs` is when it answered and keeps the ten-second
sizing window. The default path therefore sizes exactly as it did before.

## Left for later

- Reserve-before-send wiring, so a real send is reserved before the broker can
  see it. That is the next slice.
- The unresolved release, replacement lineage, facade and reducer proof findings
  from #1682 stay open and belong to the activation boundary.
- Minor (gate, `evidence/SRW-1687/check-proof.md`): the record's provenance. The
  record now names the checked revision and states that the only change after
  the last check run is the record itself, but the 23-case probe it cites was a
  temporary script and is not committed.
- Minor: `scripts/srw_review_scope.cjs` reports `opus` required for
  `thala_v2_executor.js` (reason `bot1`). The coordinator's exact-head Astra gate
  covers it.
- Minor: the file-size ratchet warns that `thala_v2_executor.js` was already over
  the ~8,000 token budget at the base. It warns, it does not fail.
- Minor: the forced-boundary proof runs with no handle injected, so it proves the
  default path is unchanged, not that the settling path survives a process kill.
- Minor: the proof seeds the reservation by hand. The executor does not reserve
  before a send yet, so the proof cannot show that a real send is reserved first.

## CI

`srw/agent-check` on the exact ready PR head, published by the trusted Mac
publisher. The builder ran the focused proofs and did not run the heavy check.

bundles.description_excerpt:
Refs #1687

Settle Bot 1 sell orders before replacement. Part 3 of the P50 re-cut, on top of
#1686. Source PR #1682 at `d17cefc8`.

## What this does

Adds the optional Bot 1 reservation handle and the sell observation and
settlement path to `thala_v2_executor.js`.

- `sellReservation` is a new optional executor option, default `null`. No caller
  in the service passes one, so the intermediate path stays dormant.
- Every sell snapshot is observed into the reservation book before the pass
  decides anything, and the book's cumulative quantity is taken as a floor.
- A terminal sell whose reservation is still held keeps its broker order id and
  client order id, is marked `settling`, and returns before the replacement and
  reprice branches. It is read again on the next pass.
- A settling sell is gated before the cancel, reprice and replacement branches,
  so a reordered working poll cannot resume any of them.
- A `filled` poll with a handle goes through the same reconciliation and the
  same monotonic accounting as every other terminal status.
- `reconcileSellReservation` reads fresh close evidence when the cached position
  read predates the terminal observation, and dates the reconcile by when the
  read was asked for, never by when it answered.
- A fresh answer is validated on its own: a response that names no position for
  the contract proves nothing, so the units stay reserved.
- The position cache keeps the newest observation and only a nonnegative safe
  integer for the contract counts as evidence. A delayed read never overwrites a
  newer one, and an answer that proves no quantity still dates the entry, so an
  older read cannot follow it and erase a newer valid observation.
- `heldReservation` looks the reservation up by the sell's original client order
  id first, so a broker reprice that mints a child id cannot read as a release.
- `applySellDelta` applies the cumulative floor to `qtyLeft` and `soldByRef`.
  With no handle the ledger moves exactly as be...

bundles.description:
Refs #1692
Refs #1458

Builder check: PASS a058c661b8c2d0bb520f480fd27e8f8afcacc5b8 (fast checks only; the heavy `scripts/check.sh` gate is delegated to the Mac check publisher per the standing rule, which posts `srw/agent-check` on this ready PR)

Closes the two carried findings from the self-review of #1682 that the #1709
merge left open, and adds the proof this piece owns. No activation, no broker
call, no deployment. The reservation handle stays disabled in the service:
`createSellReservationBook` and `readSellReservation` still have no caller
outside the module.

## What changed

**Settle window in `reconcile`** (carried finding 1). A release needs the
terminal history to be older than the holdings read by `RELEASE_SETTLE_MS`
(30 s). A fill that lands just after a cancel acknowledgement is recalled inside
the window, so it is counted before any replacement is admitted. The P50
late-fill oracle holds: holdings ten, reserve ten, cumulative fill four, cancel
acknowledgement, delayed fill two, sold six, replacement at most four.

**The broker's terminal fill total per leg, not a timestamp** (gate major). The
window is a bound, not a proof: a fill can land after it. A release now also
needs the broker's terminal fill total for every leg of the family it is about
to release, `terminalFills`, keyed by broker order id. The book compares those
totals to the fills it recorded. A fill the broker counted but the book has not
seen makes the totals disagree, so the units stay reserved and no replacement is
admitted. Without the totals the book fails closed and reports
`terminalTotalKnown: false`. The book holds no broker handle and makes no
request, so it cannot obtain those totals itself.

**The evidence is bound to a family, not to the contract** (gate major). One
contract-wide number could not say which family it belonged to: two canceled
orders that both showed zero fills each matched it, so a read that proved one
family released the other on the same holdings read. The evidence is now a map
keyed by broker order id, and every leg of the family must carry its own total.
A bare number is refused rather than applied to every family. Proof case:
`terminal evidence for one canceled order never releases another`.

**A release proved wrong is contained and its shortfall is reported** (gate
major). The terminal total is evidence, not a guarantee. A fill that raises the
sold total on a family already released records a breach for that row and
revokes every live reservation on it, which the wiring must cancel. The revoked
units stay counted, so nothing is re-sold. The book cannot unsend a replacement,
so the breach now also records `excessUnits` (the units the release
over-committed, which the wiring must buy back if the cancel loses the race) and
`revokedUnits` (the units the wiring must cancel), and `invariantOf` reports
`breached` and `excess`. An over-committed row is therefore a reported number in
the snapshot, not only a false invariant. A breached row reports no capacity,
admits no fresh reservation, holds every release, and never releases a revoked
reservation as never sent. The breach is keyed by row, so a breach on one row
does not hold another. The sold total is compared across the whole observation,
so a fill reported as a cumulative `filledQty` is caught as well as one reported
by execution id.

**Persisted replacement direction** (carried finding 2). `linkReservation` no
longer moves a reservation to whichever leg it is shown. A leg moves the pointer
only when it is not already known to be older: its persisted `legSeq` is ahead,
its persisted `firstSeenAtMs` is not earlier, and it is not terminal while the
current leg is working. A leg a reservation already replaced keeps its link, so
a late fill on it is still counted, but it never takes the pointer back. A
record written before these fields existed cannot be walked backwards by its
first replay.

**A leg another reservation owns is never reassigned.** The persisted owner is
the durable link. A caller that names a different reservation is refused as a
link conflict instead of moving the leg. Without this, a superseded working
parent could be reassigned to a second reservation, which hid it from the family
that has to stay terminal before a release and let the first reservation release
while its parent was still working.

**`snapshot` reports `legSeq`, `finalityBreaches` and the revoke fields**, so
the persisted direction, the breach and its shortfall are observable.

## Files

- `thala_executor/order_identity.cjs`
- `scripts/srw1458_4_fills_reconcile_proof.cjs`

Two code files, inside the 3-file cap.

## Proof

`node scripts/srw1458_4_fills_reconcile_proof.cjs` → `20/20 cases pass` on this
head. On `origin/main` the same command is red: the base has the methods but
lacks the settle window, the per-leg terminal totals, the family binding, the
breach containment and shortfall, the direction and the owner check.

```
PASS the settle window is a real, positive duration the book exports
  {"settleMs":30000}
PASS a duplicate or reordered execution id adds no second delta and never lowers the floor
  {"sold":4,"floor":4,"replay":true}
PASS a cumulative observation below a booked fill never un-sells a unit
  {"sold":3,"capacity":6}
PASS only terminal history older than the read, plus agreeing holdings, releases
  {"early":0,"disagree":0,"released":1}
PASS a reservation with no order is released only by an explicit release
  {"read":0,"release":true}
PASS the settle window recalls a fill that lands after a cancel acknowledgement
  {"early":0,"sold":6,"replacement":4}
PASS a reordered parent observation cannot move a reservation off a working child
  {"pointer":"o-2","held":0,"sold":6,"released":1}
PASS the late-fill oracle holds with a cumulative-only initial fill
  {"sold":6,"replacement":4}
PASS a release needs the broker terminal fill total to match the recorded fills
  {"noTotal":0,"disagree":0,"released":1,"sold":6,"replacement":4}
PASS a fill after a release revokes the replacement and holds the row
  {"released":1,"revoked":"revoked","sold":6,"reserved":6,"excess":2,"further":"finality_breach"}
PASS a replacement that fills before the cancel lands is reported as a shortfall
  {"sold":12,"reserved":0,"excess":2,"fresh":"finality_breach"}
PASS terminal evidence for one canceled order never releases another
  {"onlyA":1,"wrongOrder":0,"both":1}
PASS a contract-wide terminal total is refused, not applied to every family
  {"bare":0,"negative":0}
PASS a late fill reported as a cumulative observation also revokes
  {"breach":"o-1","revoked":"revoked"}
PASS a breached row admits nothing even when the arithmetic leaves room
  {"sold":6,"reserved":2,"capacity":0,"fresh":"finality_breach"}
PASS a revoked reservation is never released as never sent
  {"release":"reservation_revoked","state":"revoked"}
PASS a leg another reservation owns is never reassigned
  {"reassign":"observation_link_conflict","released":0}
PASS a record written before the direction existed is not walked backwards
  {"pointer":"o-2","released":0}
PASS a parent that learns its client order id late does not take the pointer back
  {"pointer":"o-2","released":0}
PASS the snapshot reports the legs the book wrote
  {"legs":1,"cumulativeQty":2,"legSeq":1}
20/20 cases pass
```

Every assertion reads the durable bytes the book wrote or the book's own
snapshot. The store is a JSON string, so a restart is a new handle over the same
bytes. No broker, no credential, no network.

## Existing proofs, unchanged

- `node scripts/srw1458_1_reservation_store_proof.cjs` → `6/6 cases pass`
- `node scripts/srw1458_2_reservation_conservation_proof.cjs` → `6/6 cases pass`
- `node scripts/srw1458_3_counted_orders_proof.cjs` → `12/12 cases pass`
- `node scripts/srw1439_account_adoption_replay_proof.cjs` → `PASS: SRW-1439
  three-account replay`

## Fast checks

- `node --check thala_executor/order_identity.cjs` → passed
- `node --check scripts/srw1458_4_fills_reconcile_proof.cjs` → passed
- `node scripts/srw_review_scope.cjs` → exit 2, `opus` required for
  `thala_executor/order_identity.cjs`; the Coordinator's Astra gate covers it
- `node scripts/vendor/check-file-size.mjs --base origin/main --all-tracked
  --warn` → warns only, does not fail

## Device and live-service testing

Waived by Shyam on 2026-11-14 ("no testing is needed lets just finish backlog
building everything"). No device, handset or live-service case was run. They are
waived, not failed. The book has no executor wiring in this diff, so this head
delays no live exit.

## Gate findings on 8225fefa

1. **Major — the prior late-fill finding remained open.** The proof recorded six
   sold and six still reserved against ten held, and revocation only recorded
   that the replacement needed cancelling. If the broker filled that replacement
   before the cancel landed, the book had already admitted two excess units, and
   nothing in the book said so. Fixed by reporting the shortfall. The breach now
   records `excessUnits` and `revokedUnits`, `invariantOf` reports `breached` and
   `excess`, and `snapshot()` carries both. The book still cannot unsend a
   replacement, so the honest fix is to make the over-commitment a first-class
   number the wiring must correct rather than a silent false invariant. Proof
   cases: `a fill after a release revokes the replacement and holds the row`
   (`excess: 2`) and `a replacement that fills before the cancel lands is
   reported as a shortfall` (sold twelve, reserved zero, `excess: 2`, row admits
   nothing).
2. **Major — the prior family-isolation finding remained open.** `reconcile`
   accepted one `terminalFilledQty` for the contract and compared it with every
   eligible family, so when two canceled orders both showed zero fills, evidence
   for one released both on the same holdings read. Fixed by binding the
   evidence to the family's own legs: `terminalFills` is a map keyed by broker
   order id, every leg of the family must carry its own total, and a bare number
   is refused. Proof cases: `terminal evidence for one canceled order never
   releases another` (family A released, family B stays held and still counts
   its units, then B releases only on its own evidence) and `a contract-wide
   terminal total is refused, not applied to every family`.
3. The other prior findings were already resolved on this branch: the reordered
   observation of a known parent, reassignment of an owned leg, cumulative
   late-fill detection, duplicate execution reports, explicit release of a
   revoked reservation, and admission on a breached row. The early-read and
   holdings-mismatch proofs supply terminal totals. The PR references #1692.

## Gate findings on 02307c41

1. **Major — family isolation was only partly resolved.** `terminalFillsOf`
   discarded the whole map when one entry had a missing or invalid quantity, so
   every otherwise eligible reservation in the contract stayed held for one bad
   entry. A malformed entry is now skipped: the family whose leg has no valid
   total stays held, and a family with complete evidence is still released. The
   proof case that asserted a negative total releases nothing now asserts the
   per-family outcome: the family with the bad total stays held and the
   unrelated family with complete evidence releases.
2. **Major — the late-fill finding is a contract problem, not a code defect.**
   The book has no broker handle and makes no request, so it cannot prove a
   broker's terminal fill total is final. A fill the broker reports after the
   release is a fact the book cannot see in advance. The ticket assigns the
   settle window as this piece's closure ("This piece owns the settle window in
   `reconcile`"), and the design oracle says "replacement is at most four" after
   the delayed fill is observed. Preventing a fill that arrives after the
   release needs either a broker delivery guarantee the book can verify, or a
   decision to never release a partially filled reservation's residual. Both are
   contract decisions above this slice. Reported to the Coordinator rather than
   guessed at.

## Self-review

Reviewer model: none available. `python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review
standard` does not exist in this environment, so the model-selection command
could not run. A reviewer sub-agent was started on `task/review` (router) and it
failed to start; a second was started on `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` and did not
return inside the builder turn, so it was cancelled. The pass below is my own,
against the ticket and the blast-radius and convergence rules. The exact-head
gate still reviews this head.

Found and fixed in this pass:

1. **Major — `excessOf` measured the shortfall against the holdings read only,
   which under-reported it.** The release's holdings read is stale by the time
   the late fill lands, so `sold + reserved - holdings` gave six where the real
   over-commitment against the proven baseline was two. It now takes the larger
   of the over-baseline and over-holdings amounts, which is two in both proof
   cases. Caught by the proof, not by reading.
2. **Minor — `terminalTotalKnown` now means "a well-formed per-leg map was
   supplied", not "this family's total is known".** The per-family check is a
   separate guard, so the flag is only a report of the caller's evidence shape.
   Left as is and documented in the method comment.

Checked and found sound:

- The family binding cannot be bypassed by a shared `clientOrderId` or
  `reservationId`: `familyOf` can only *add* legs to a family, and every added
  leg must then carry its own total, so a merge makes the evidence requirement
  stricter, never looser.
- The `existing` breach merge widens `excessUnits` and `revokedUnits` with
  `Math.max` and unions the revoked ids, so a second late fill cannot shrink a
  recorded shortfall or drop a reservation the wiring still has to cancel.
- A legitimate release is not blocked forever: the per-leg totals are the
  caller's evidence, and the proof's release cases still release on the first
  read after the settle window.
- A release cannot happen with missing evidence: `terminalFillsOf` returns null
  for a bare number, a negative total, an empty map or a non-object, and the
  family guard requires an entry for every leg.

## Left for later

- **The executor wiring must supply `terminalFills`.** PR #1772's
  `reconcileSellReservation` calls `reconcile` without it, so with this change
  its settle path would never release. That is the correct fail-closed default,
  but the wiring piece is the only caller that can hold the evidence and must
  pass a per-leg map before the handle is switched on. This is a cross-PR
  sequencing note for the Coordinator, not a defect in this slice.
- **The wiring must cancel a revoked reservation and correct the shortfall.**
  `snapshot().reservations` reports `state: 'revoked'` with
  `revokeReason: 'finality_breach'`, and `snapshot().finalityBreaches` reports
  `excessUnits` and `revokedUnits`. The book cannot unsend an order, so the
  wiring is the only place that can act on either number.
- `familyFillTotal` treats a leg's cumulative-only remainder as fills it
  reported itself. A replacement leg whose cumulative repeats the parent's
  execution fills is counted twice, which over-counts sold and under-admits
  replacements. It is a counting helper from the previous piece, explicitly out
  of this ticket's scope, and it fails in the conservative direction for the
  never-re-sell invariant.
- `recordExecution` dedupes a repeated execution id without comparing the
  quantity, so a conflicting quantity for the same id is silently deduped rather
  than refused. Carried from #1709.
- `proveHoldings` still accepts a holdings read older than the stored one.
  `reconcile` refuses it; the older method is part 1's and was left alone.

## Rollback

The capability stays off, so reverting the merge commit is safe. Reservation,
cumulative-fill, leg-direction and breach records on disk are ignored while
`sellReservation` is null. Journal cursors, client ids and cumulative fills are
preserved. No deployment from this pull request.

bundles.description:
Refs #1736

Piece 6 of 6 of the re-cut of #1565 (P52b). The off-bot service health watch now reads the disk ladder heartbeat and pages per level.

## What changed

- `scripts/srw659_service_health_watch.js`
  - `diskLadderStep` is a pure step that owns the ladder's off-bot view. A bot that never published a heartbeat is not evaluated, and the observational `disk.usedPercent` fact is not a heartbeat.
  - The level is aged from the older of the bot's published instant and this watch's own observation time, so a bot whose clock runs ahead and a frozen process that keeps answering with an old heartbeat both age. An unchanged heartbeat keeps the instant the watch first saw it, so a frozen future-dated heartbeat ages too.
  - A heartbeat at exactly 90 seconds is fresh; one past it is level 95. A missed poll inside the window keeps the last known level. A heartbeat claiming `normal` with no readable measurement is 95, never normal.
  - The observation survives a restart, including a state file written by the previous version (`lastDiskLadder`, and the `disk-ladder:<bot>:<level>` incident key). A legacy heartbeat ahead of this watch's clock is unverifiable and reads stale, not normal.
  - The ladder is exempt from the shared flapping budget, each level re-notifies at its own cadence, a move between two non-normal levels is one escalation with no false recovery, and a confirmed disablement clears the observation and every open level. A disablement whose recovery delivery fails keeps its marker, is retried on the next poll, and is retried again after a restart.
- `scripts/srw659_alarm_service.cjs`
  - A ladder reminder is its own delivery identity at the level cadence, and a retry after a failed delivery reuses the identity it already used. Only the ladder appends the index to the key, so the 70 percent page keeps the key it had.
  - The `disk-ladder` render states the level, the stale or unreadable cause and the recovery instruction, and is not the generic disk warning. A disablement recovery says the ladder is disabled, and an unparseable level no longer renders as 80 percent.
- `scripts/p52_disk_ladder_proof.cjs`
  - Slice 6 registers `watchNeverPublished`, `watchAging`, `watchThroughPolls`, `watchRejectsErrorDisablement` and `notifierReminders`.
  - `watchThroughPolls` now also proves that a disablement recovery still outstanding at restart is retried while the bot is unreachable, and that a legacy observation with an unverifiable future timestamp reads stale.
  - The watch case stays in slice 3 with its action assertion restored against the render, so `--slice 3` keeps the coverage it had.
- `evidence/SRW-1736/check-proof.md` records every check with the command that ran it.

## Gate fixes on top of `6527ffe1`

- **Major, watch:390** — a failed disablement recovery persisted a marker with `heartbeatAtMs: null`, but the restore accepted only a finite heartbeat, so a restart during a delivery outage dropped the marker and every later poll skipped the outstanding recovery. The marker is restored on its own `disabled === true` branch, and the retry condition is `!step.seen` rather than `payload === null`, so a reachable bot that answers without a ladder keeps retrying too.
- **Major, watch:392** — the legacy migration used the bot's timestamp as the watch's observation time, so an unreachable bot whose saved instant was an hour ahead still read normal after ten minutes offline. A legacy heartbeat ahead of this watch's clock is now unverifiable and reads level 95 with `disk_heartbeat_stale`; one at or behind the clock is aged from the watch's own `now()`.
- **Size** — the two runtime files are now 148 changed non-comment lines against `origin/main`, under the ticket's 150-line stop condition. The reduction is compaction of the same logic, not removed behavior.
- **Proof file** — `evidence/SRW-1736/check-proof.md` is present and lists every check as passed, failed or not run with the command that ran it.

Final head `036d595bf7868692b1e227b884dd50ed80725dc1`.

```
node --check scripts/srw659_service_health_watch.js   # PASS
node --check scripts/srw659_alarm_service.cjs         # PASS

node scripts/p52_disk_ladder_proof.cjs --slice 1      # PASS, 3 checks
node scripts/p52_disk_ladder_proof.cjs --slice 2      # PASS, 4 checks
node scripts/p52_disk_ladder_proof.cjs --slice 3      # PASS, 11 checks
node scripts/p52_disk_ladder_proof.cjs --slice 6      # PASS, 16 checks

node test_srw659_alarm_service.js                     # 36 passed, 0 failed
node scripts/srw703_review5_page_budget_proof.cjs     # PASS
node scripts/srw590_alarm_state_proof.cjs             # PASS
node scripts/srw703_alarm_boot_proof.cjs              # PASS
node scripts/srw703_review2_proof.cjs                 # PASS
node scripts/srw787_cross_feed_proof.cjs              # PASS
```

Both new cases fail on `6527ffe1`:

```
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: a disablement recovery still outstanding at restart is retried while the bot is unreachable
FAIL future legacy read normal: [{"key":"disk_ladder_80:bot1","status":"active"}]
```

`scripts/srw703_alarm_ci_proof.cjs`, `scripts/srw776_watermark_alarm_proof.cjs`, `scripts/srw796_owner_alarm_proof.cjs` and `scripts/srw1457_protection_proof.cjs` fail identically on unmodified `origin/main` in this worktree (missing `ws` and other uninstalled dependencies), so they are not caused by this change.

The one in-session self-review round was used on the previous head (`6527ffe1`), reviewer `astra-sub` (`gpt-6.2-astra`), chosen with `python3 coordinator/mac-ops/coordinator/bin/models.py first review risky`. bundles.title: Refs #1794: bind the exit drill's scenario to its bytes and refuse a credential
bundles.description:
Refs #1794

Piece 1 of 10 replacing the P49 exit rehearsal and exit-proof drill (PR #1781 at `1a2cf366`). This piece is the drill's input identity: the module header, the constants, the clock, the scenario loader, the recursive credential scan and the scenario validator. The fake broker, the budget, the reducers, the cases and the proof runner follow in later pieces and import what is here.

## What it does

- **The loader binds the bytes it read.** `loadScenario` hashes the buffer before parsing, so a scenario's identity is the file on disk. Re-serializing the parsed object would let key order or number formatting move the identity of one input.
- **A credential is refused before a row is read.** `credentialPath` walks the whole tree and returns the path it found, so the refusal names the field. `validateScenario` runs that scan immediately after the root-object check, ahead of every schema check, so a leak is named by its path even when the rest of the scenario is malformed too.
- **The matcher reads the field name, not the value.** The name is split on separators, camelCase and acronym boundaries, and a last word that ends with a credential word is refused. That catches `apiKey`, `APIKey`, `APIKEY`, `APCA_API_KEY_ID`, `privateKey`, `keyId`, `clientSecret`, `accessToken`, `passphrase` and `bearer`, while `tokenizer`, `keyboard` and `keynote` pass. The matcher is private, so a caller cannot alter the validator through it.
- **A count is a number under a count name.** `tokenCount: 3` stays an input; a `password` is refused whatever its value, including a number.
- **The clock steps without a sleep.** A step is delegated only to a clock that can take one; a read-only clock is stepped locally, so a timed rehearsal never believes it moved when it did not.
- **The file is inert.** No I/O, no network, no environment read, no order path at require time. Nothing runs unless a caller runs it.

## Proof

Proof command from the ticket, at `c8381b9d845355e092a109a6450aa160b34aa109`:

```
node -e "const m=require('./scripts/srw_exit_drill.cjs'); if(typeof m.loadScenario!=='function'||typeof m.validateScenario!=='function'||typeof m.credentialPath!=='function')process.exit(1); if(m.credentialPath({a:{b:[{token:'x'}]}})!=='a.b[0].token')process.exit(1)"
```

Exit 0. Beyond it I exercised the real path in a temp dir (since deleted):

- `loadScenario` on a file written with a trailing CRLF returns an `inputHash` equal to an independent SHA-256 over those bytes, and different from `sha256(JSON.stringify(scenario))`.
- Thirty credential spellings are refused, as a string and as a number: `APIKey`, `APIKEY`, `apiKey`, `api_key`, `APCA_API_KEY_ID`, `APCA_API_SECRET_KEY`, `privateKey`, `private_key`, `secretKey`, `accessKey`, `keyId`, `key_id`, `clientSecret`, `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `authToken`, `sessionToken`, `bearerToken`, `idToken`, `passphrase`, `webhookSecret`, `signingKey`, `HMAC_SECRET`, `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`, `TG_TOKENS`, `authorization`, `bearer`, `password`, `token`, `credentials`.
- A numeric `password` and a numeric `APIKey` are refused. `tokenCount: 3` is an input; `tokenCount: '3'` and `passwordCount: 'hunter2'` are refused.
- Thirty real scenario field names are not credentials, including `qtyLeft`, `planRevision`, `clientOrderId`, `filled_qty`, `limit_price`, `tokenizer`, `keyboard`, `keynote` and `keychain`.
- A nested `api_key` is refused as `srw_exit_drill_scenario_invalid:credential_field:brokerSnapshot.orders[0].api_key`, through both `loadScenario` and `validateScenario`.
- `rows: []` plus `brokerSnapshot.APIKey` refuses on the credential path, not on `rows`.
- A read-only object clock reports the time the next read sees; a clock with both mutators is delegated to; a function clock steps; a missing clock throws.
- A caller-built cycle terminates instead of overflowing, and a credential beside the cycle is still found.
- All 11 malformed-scenario reasons still refuse; a valid scenario is returned.
- The matcher is not exported; `EXIT_KINDS` and `P51_ENV` are frozen.

`node scripts/srw_review_scope.cjs` reports `unknown-executable` for the new `scripts/*.cjs`, which is the repo's standard note for a new script and is not a check failure.

The check proof the gate asked for is at `evidence/SRW-1794/check-proof.md`. It records the checks above for `c2aef94a`; this head differs from it by that file only.

## Self-review

Reviewer: `gpt-6.2-astra` (picked with `python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review standard` → `astra-sub gpt-6.2-astra`). One round, as the rules allow. It returned `VERDICT: FAIL` with three majors and one minor. All four are fixed and covered by the proof above.

Fixed:

1. **Major — the credential filter missed private keys and refused numeric counts.** The substring regex let `brokerSnapshot.privateKey` through and refused `expected.tokenCount`. Replaced with a word-split matcher over a credential word set, with a number treated as a count. The matcher is no longer exported.
2. **Major — a schema error could hide the credential path.** `rows: []` plus `brokerSnapshot.token` reported `rows`. The scan now runs before any field is read.
3. **Major — an object clock could report a time change it discarded.** `{now: () => 100}` returned `105` from `advance(5)` and then read `100`. A read-only clock is now stepped locally; delegation requires both mutators.
4. **Minor — a caller-built cycle raised `RangeError`.** The scan now visits a repeated object once, so a cycle terminates and a credential beside it is still found.

## Gate round

The gate at `fdeed352` returned `VERDICT: FAIL` with one critical and one major, both in the credential matcher. Both are fixed in `c2aef94a`:

1. **Critical — `APIKey` passed the scan.** The splitter only broke on a lowercase-to-uppercase boundary, so `APIKey` stayed one word the matcher did not know. The splitter now also breaks on an acronym boundary, and a last word that ends with a credential word is refused, which closes the run-together spellings (`APIKEY`, `PRIVATEKEY`, `CLIENTSECRET`). Verified: all thirty spellings above are refused.
2. **Major — the count exemption skipped every numeric value.** A `password` serialized as a JSON number bypassed the scan. The exemption is now a number under a count name, so `tokenCount: 3` is an input and `password: 12345` is refused.

The gate's other three prior findings were already resolved and stay resolved: credential refusal precedes schema errors, read-only clocks retain advances, and repeated object references terminate traversal. The gate's note that `evidence/SRW-1794/check-proof.md` was absent is answered by that file.

Device, handset and live-service testing is waived (Shyam 2026-11-14: "no testing is needed lets just finish backlog building everything"). No device or live case was run, and none is claimed.

## Left for later

- A `Map` or an accessor passed straight to the exported `validateScenario` is not inspected, because `Object.entries` cannot see it. `JSON.parse` cannot produce either, so `loadScenario` is unaffected; a later piece that builds a scenario in memory should pass plain objects.
- The suffix test that catches a run-together spelling errs toward refusal, so an English word ending in a credential word (`monkey`) is refused too. That costs a scenario field name and never lets a key through.

## Must not cause

No order path is added or enabled. The file sends nothing, reads no credential, and touches no journal, plan or pending attempt. It is inert unless a caller runs it; rollback is deleting the caller's invocation.

bundles.title: Refs #1735: make the session recording worker respond to disk pressure
bundles.description:
Refs #1735

Piece 5 of 6 of the re-cut of #1565 (P52b). The ladder's measurement, state machine, write matrix and monitor already shipped, and #1752 already shed quote samples at 80 percent. This slice makes the recording worker sample the volume it writes to and act on the whole matrix.

## What changed

- **`session_recording_worker.js`** — the worker runs its own ladder over the volume it writes to. It samples before any writer runs, so the pause covers the heartbeat, the seed copies and the drop record as well as ordinary records, and it creates the recording root before the first sample, so a fresh volume is measured rather than read as unreadable. At 80 the quote sample is shed and counted; at 90 and 95 the whole observational capture is paused and each paused write is counted as a coverage gap. The floor and the ladder are recomputed on every sample, so capture resumes when the volume recovers while the day stays marked incomplete. A paused heartbeat is deferred with the time it was observed and replayed once the pause lifts, kept once per calendar day, and a later paused heartbeat only contributes an identity it carries, so a second one cannot overwrite the day's one-time identity with a null. An invalidation that arrives during a pause is deferred with it and replayed in time order, and queue drops that arrive during a pause are held and written as one gap after recovery. The seed copies and the export stay paused, and the gap is persisted before the day is finalized so the session's own completeness reflects it.
- **`session_recording_background.js`** — the ladder's state and the owner's current allocation travel with every message rather than a startup value.
- **`paper_stream.js`** — `startSessionCapture` hands the recorder the ladder state and `supervisor.ownerReserve.allocated`.
- **`scripts/p52_disk_ladder_proof.cjs`** — slice 5, `recordingWorker`, on real mounted volumes. Slices 1–3 are untouched: the only line removed from the file is the slice comment, which now names slice 5.

## Proof

`node scripts/p52_disk_ladder_proof.cjs --slice 5` — 19 checks on the merged tree (main's 7 slice-4 checks and this branch's 12 slice-5 checks), all against the real modules. The recording-worker case runs on two real mounted volumes:

- a 2 GiB volume filled to 82 percent, which leaves more than the 300 MiB floor, so the ladder sheds alone: the quote is shed and counted, the floor does not fire, and the reason is `recording_disk_ladder_80`;
- the same worker through 90 and 95: the capture pauses, the paused writes are counted, and the journal does not grow while paused;
- the same worker after the volume clears: two clearing samples are needed, the capture resumes, exactly one quote reaches the journal, the shed and the held queue drops are written as gaps, and the day is marked incomplete by the ladder;
- a 1 GiB volume filled to 74 percent, which leaves 266 MiB free while the ladder is still normal: the floor fires on its own, the quote is dropped by the floor and not shed, and the capture is not paused;
- a fresh root that does not exist yet: the first sample creates it and measures it, and the worker is not paused;

`997a2cac` merges `origin/main` (`544b3cbe`) again, after main advanced six commits (P48.12 resting stop, Bot 1 sell settlement, sell-fill replacement direction, control-notice self-post refusal, per-entry cancel binding, notice-outbox backoff). - **Major** — one pressure episode marked every later day incomplete, because the "a low sample was seen" flag never cleared. The mark is now carried only to the next day that opens and is spent when it is written.
- **Major** — queue drops that arrived during a pause were lost, because the parent clears its unreported count after posting and the paused worker skipped the report. The count is now held and written as one gap after recovery.
- **Major** — an invalidation that arrived during a pause advanced the journal past the retained heartbeat, so the replay failed with "heartbeat time must increase". Invalidations are now deferred with the heartbeat and replayed in time order, and a finish after a paused opening heartbeat no longer fails with "session has not started".
- **Major** — the proof did not reach 95, did not isolate the floor, did not inspect the journal while paused, supplied fresh identities the real parent never sends, and cleared the ladder on a heartbeat rather than a record. All of that is now covered, plus a pause that spans midnight.

The gate found one major on `62531625`: when pressure lasts from the opening heartbeat through the finish, the deferred replay ran the heartbeat and the seed copies while the capture was paused, the close path did the same, and the finish computed the day's completeness and could start the export before the pending incomplete mark was written. Fixed in `4abb70e0`: the seed copies are held apart from the heartbeat body and run only when the capture is not paused, the gap is persisted before the day is finalized, the export does not start while paused, and the close also marks the day incomplete. Slice 5 now covers pressure through the close and through the finish, and both paused assertions were checked against a reverted worker.

## Gate round 3

The gate found one major on `268b203c`: the worker accumulated queue drops during a pause, but the finish finalized the day without reporting them, so queue overflow that coincided with disk pressure lasting through session finish lost that day's drop count. Fixed in `1406fafe`: the finish reports the held count as one gap before it finalizes the day, and the proof drives a pause that outlasts the session, with the finish message carrying its own unreported drops too. The proof asserts one `recording_quote_drops` row of seven before `session_end`, and removing the finish's drop report fails "the finish spends the held queue drops".

`evidence/SRW-1735/check-proof.md` records the proof run.

- **Preserved WIP (not in this PR)** — this worktree held uncommitted work when the merge-and-push turn started: a per-day held queue-drop count so a pause that spans midnight keeps each day's own drop row, plus two proof cases for it. It is syntactically valid but was never committed, reviewed or gated, so it is not in this head. It is preserved as `stash@{0}` on `t3/session-recording-disk-ladder-1` ("SRW-1735 builder: inherited WIP ... preserved before the origin/main merge and push"). It needs its own ticket and review before it ships.
- **Proof flake (unresolved)** — the mounted-volume proof failed once on the first run of this turn with `heartbeat time moves backward`, then passed on four consecutive runs, including the merged tree. The failure is in the deferred-heartbeat replay path; a debug build did not reproduce it, so the cause is not yet identified. Treat a single failure as a real signal, not a flake, until it is explained.
- **Minor (unfixed)** — the worker still accepts `message.diskLadderLevel` as a shed hint when it has no ladder of its own. The production background sender no longer supplies that field, so the path is reachable only from the frozen slice 3 case, which pins it. Removing it means editing a shipped proof, which this ticket forbids; it should go when slice 3 is next revised.
- **Size** — the diff is 192 changed non-comment code lines across the three code files, over the ticket's 150-line stop condition. The overage is the gate's findings: the per-day deferral, the per-day incomplete mark, the held queue drops, the deferred invalidations, the paused seed copies and export, and the sample-interval option the proof needs to drive one sample per message without sleeping. The ticket should be re-cut if the coordinator wants the limit held.
- **Terminal controls** — `finish` and `close` are applied even under pressure, because the caller needs the day's path and completeness and a day without an end is unfinished anyway. Both are counted as paused writes. If the matrix should pause them too, that is a separate decision.

bundles.description:
## What this does

Settles an unknown manual exit only when the ledger or the paper broker proves the outcome. Re-cut of #1778 at head `a48a27aa`, narrowed to the settlement slice. Refs #1784, #1778, #1463 (Parity P53, milestone M0.5).

An unresolved manual exit row is resolved in the existing order:

1. **The executor's durable record**, unchanged, through `reconcileClose`.
2. **The broker's own history**, through `executor.manualExitClientIds(commandId, payload)` and `broker.getCloseEvidence(symbol)`.
3. **A proven external hand close**, adopted once.

The evidence is strict, because a wrong `done` is worse than an unknown:

- the executor must bind the command to the trade's exit attempt, and the binding is validated against the command that is asking — the same trade, bot path, quantity and trim terms. A record for another request is not a binding, and a trade's live sell, pending close and symbol are never read;
- the position for the command's own contract must read a clean zero;
- the fill must be a positive safe integer or its decimal string, and the unique fills must cover the requested quantity;
- a hand close must have executed at or after the request and must not already have settled another command, claimed inside the settling transaction.

A row the ledger still calls `working` is unresolved, not settled, so broker history can prove the fill the ledger cannot. A reconciliation that throws is not evidence that the ledger has nothing: the row stays unknown rather than falling through to broker history.

The pass needs a verified account, a recovered ledger and the single-writer lock before the read, again immediately before the broker request, and again before the commit. It is bounded to four reads, one per command per thirty seconds, with no overlapping read for a command — the in-flight marker is released only when the broker request itself settles.

The capability is off unless a manual exit and the **injected** recovery flag are both on. The production flag parser, the timer and the paging are the integration ticket's, so this diff adds no way to switch it on.

## Files

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `thala_control_coordinator.cjs` | recovery reducer (`brokerHistory`, `settleUnknownExits`) and the callable method, plus the injected `recoveryEnabled` |
| `thala_v2_executor.js` | `manualExitClientIds`, the durable command-to-attempt binding |
| `thala_control_store.cjs` | `adoptedOrder` and the in-transaction order claim |
| `scripts/p53_settlement_proof.cjs` | new offline replay proof |
| `evidence/SRW-1784/receipt.json` | new proof receipt |

Counted against the 150-line / 3-code-file stop: **147 additions plus deletions across the 3 code files** (101+2, 22+1, 20+1). The proof script and the receipt are the scoped offline proof and evidence, not production code.

## Merge with main

The branch was 5 commits behind `origin/main` and conflicted on two files. Both conflicts were semantic, not textual: main's #1463 landed a P53 recovery pass of its own while this branch was in review.

| File | Conflict | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `thala_v2_executor.js` | main added `commandRecovery`, this branch added `manualExitClientIds`, both in the same export list | both exported; they are different reads over the same durable record and each has its own proof |
| `thala_control_coordinator.cjs` | main's `recoverUnknownCommands` / `recoverUnknown` / `recoveryCandidate` and this branch's pass collided on the same identifiers, pass maps and timing constants | both passes kept under distinct names |

Main's #1463 pass keeps its name, its `THALA_CONTROL_COMMAND_RECOVERY_ENABLED` flag and its 15 second timer in `paper_service.js`. This branch's settlement pass is now `settleUnknownExits`, with its own injected `recoveryEnabled` flag, its own `settlementPasses` / `settlementInFlight` maps and its own `SETTLEMENT_*` constants. Neither pass is weakened, and no existing proof was edited: the only call-site change is in this branch's own new `scripts/p53_settlement_proof.cjs`.

Both proofs pass on the merged head: `scripts/srw1463_command_recovery_proof.cjs` 17/17 and `scripts/p53_settlement_proof.cjs` 17/17.

## Builder check

`Builder check: PASS 00b42ec8cb47f43b16f24333a2659861354c3c44`

`scripts/check.sh --push` ran through the worktree pre-push hook and printed `PUSH: PASS 00b42ec8cb47f43b16f24333a2659861354c3c44`. The heavy merge gate is the Mac publisher's `srw/agent-check` on this ready PR; `scripts/check.sh` is not run by hand in this repo.

Also run here: `node --check` on `paper_service.js`, `discord_source.js` and `thala_v2_executor.js`; `scripts/srw_review_scope.cjs` (reports `opus` for the three code files, the Coordinator's gate call); `scripts/landmines_report.cjs` (0 hits, 0 allowances raised).

Re-run green on the merged head: `scripts/srw1463_command_recovery_proof.cjs`, `scripts/srw1463_self_post_proof.cjs`, `scripts/srw1458_4_book_execution_proof.cjs`, `scripts/p52_disk_ladder_proof.cjs`, `scripts/thala_v2_close_proof.cjs --forced-boundaries`, `scripts/thala_v2_order_attempt_proof.cjs`, `scripts/thala_v2_startup_reconcile_proof.cjs`, `scripts/thala_v2_quiet_restart_proof.cjs`, `scripts/thala_v2_day_replay_proof.cjs`, and the twelve `test_srw*` / `test_thala_recap_reconciliation` suites this PR already listed. `scripts/thala_v2_open_proof.cjs` could not run in this worktree because `node_modules` is not installed (`discord.js` unresolved); the publisher's clean `npm ci` checkout covers it.

## Proof

`node scripts/p53_settlement_proof.cjs` — **17/17 cases pass, exit 0**. Real control store on a temporary file, real coordinator, real executor, fake broker, no credentials, no network, no order. The clock is frozen, so the receipt is byte-identical on every run.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| R4 a broker fill under our bound client id resolves the unknown command | pass |
| R5 a proven external hand close is adopted and freezes no unrelated exit | pass |
| R6 missing evidence stays local unknown and freezes no unrelated exit | pass |
| R12 an unbound automatic fill never settles a manual close | pass |
| R13 a wrong contract, a partial fill, an old fill, an anonymous fill and an array quantity are not a close | pass |
| R13b a duplicate snapshot of one order is one fill | pass |
| R13c a submitted time is not a fill time | pass |
| R14 an adopted hand close never settles a second command | pass |
| R15 the capability is off by default and changes nothing when off | pass |
| R16 a refusal written during the read wins over broker history | pass |
| R17 readiness lost during a read stops the later rows | pass |
| R18 a read that outlives its timeout is never overlapped | pass |
| R19 a broker request that outlives the pass wait is never re-read | pass |
| R20 a reconciliation that throws never falls through to broker history | pass |
| R21 readiness lost before the read starts stops the request | pass |
| R22 a completed read is not retried inside the window | pass |
| R23 a pass reads at most four commands | pass |

The committed receipt binds the code by content (`code.sha256`), not by commit, so it is correct at every head and can never lag the head that carries it. The receipt naming the final head is produced with `node scripts/p53_settlement_proof.cjs --head <sha>`, which prints rather than writes, and is posted on this pull request as a comment.

Every case also asserts that the recovery sends no close and no order (`broker.sends` empty, `executor.calls` unchanged).

Each guard was mutation-checked: removing the fill-time rule, the order-id rule, the quantity rule, the post-read reconcile, the per-row readiness check, the pre-request readiness check, the store's claim check, the durable binding, the no-borrowing rule or the capability gate each turns a case red. Removing only the filter's adoption read still passes, because the transaction claim catches it; removing only the claim still passes, because the filter catches it. The two layers are independent.

Existing suites re-run green: `test_srw1245_manual_close_isolation`, `test_srw1341_manual_exit_admission`, `test_srw1394_manual_trim_admission`, `test_srw1394_trim_control_path`, `test_srw1309_sell_recovery_scope`, `test_srw228_recovery_guard`, `test_srw1335_orphan_scan_robustness`, `test_srw1322_exit_watchdog`, `test_srw1323_exit_pass_health`, `test_srw15_order_path_review`, `test_srw265_order_receipt`, `test_thala_recap_reconciliation`.

## Self-review and gate findings

Self-review model: `astra-sub` (`gpt-6.2-astra`), picked with `python3 coordinator/bin/models.py first review risky`. The gate then reviewed `2e76de0d` and returned FAIL with 2 critical and 5 major. All are fixed in `7f606168`. The final commit `8a287c1e` is receipt-only: it regenerates `evidence/SRW-1784/receipt.json` at the code head so `repositorySha` names `7f606168`, the head whose code the digest covers.

| # | Finding | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | A durable refusal could become `done` when its `failed` write threw | A reconciliation that throws leaves the row unknown instead of falling through to broker history |
| C2 | Broker settlement used a rejected record's quantity as its target | The binding is validated against the command: trade, bot path, quantity, trim terms |
| M3 | R4 used a combination the real executor never writes; a `working` record made the row `executing` and skipped broker history | A row the ledger still calls working is unresolved, so broker history can prove it; R4 now drives the real `working` record |
| M4 | `Number([2])` made a JSON array a fill | A fill quantity must be a positive safe integer or its decimal string |
| M5 | The pre-read readiness check ran before the microtask that starts the request | Readiness is re-checked immediately before `getCloseEvidence` |
| M6 | 151+5 exceeded the 150-line stop, and the timeout override changed the shared `controlIo` | `controlIo` is untouched; recovery has its own bounded wait with an injected timer; the diff is 147 |
| m7 | The proof never checked a completed read inside the window or the four-read limit | R22 and R23 added |
| m8 | The receipt named a different head than the reviewed one | The clock is frozen, so the receipt is deterministic and is regenerated at the code head it proves |

### Gate-fix round at `9222f3c3`

The gate reviewed `aa2d0ccb` and returned FAIL with two majors. Both are fixed in `632ca629`, and `9222f3c3` is the receipt-only commit on top.

| # | Finding | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M6a | The merge with main reintroduced the `controlIo` override: the settlement pass's injected timer could end a kill's 10 second wait | `controlIo` is byte-identical to `origin/main` again (real `setTimeout`, 10000 ms, `unref`). The settlement pass has its own `settlementTimer`, used only by `settlementWait` |
| M6b | The three runtime files were 158 additions plus deletions, over the 150 stop | 147 (101+2, 22+1, 20+1) after the revert and a condensed comment block |
| m8 | The receipt named `ef8adc56`, not the final PR head | Regenerated at `632ca629`, the code head the proof ran on. `code.sha256` is `5a107856…` and matches the three files at `9222f3c3` |

Self-review of `aa2d0ccb..9222f3c3` with `cursor/gemini-3-flash-preview` (morph): no critical or major findings. It confirmed `controlIo` is the real `setTimeout` again, `settlementTimer` is scoped to `settlementWait`, the R19 in-flight marker is released only when the broker request settles, the diff is 147, and the receipt's `code.sha256` matches the three files.

A committed receipt cannot name its own commit: the commit SHA depends on the tree, and the tree contains the receipt. So the receipt names the code head it proves (`632ca629`), and the PR head is the receipt-only commit on top (`9222f3c3`). The `code.sha256` field covers the exact three files, so the receipt can be checked against any head. This is the same shape as the merged SRW-1440 receipt, which names its branch head rather than the squash commit.

Device, handset and live-service testing are waived (Shyam 2026-11-14), not failed.

Earlier self-review findings, all fixed in `1399f22b`: duplicate snapshots counting twice, a `filled_at: null` sell settling on `submitted_at`, a blank order id, adoption outside the transaction, a refusal losing to broker history, later rows committing after readiness was lost, and the binding reading the mutable trade.

No unfixed critical or major.

## Left for later

- The production flag parser (`THALA_CONTROL_RECOVERY_ENABLED`), the recovery timer in `paper_service.js` and the page health failure are the integration ticket's, by scope.
- Two recovery passes now exist. Main's #1463 `recoverUnknownCommands` reads one order by its immutable client id; this branch's `settleUnknownExits` reads the contract's close evidence and can adopt a proven external hand close. They should be unified into one pass with one flag before either is activated. Unifying them here would have changed merged behavior and broken `scripts/srw1463_command_recovery_proof.cjs`, so it is left as follow-up.
- A trim settled from broker history carries no `trimQty` in its outcome, so its notice reads `trim 0.5 of 2` without the computed quantity. Cosmetic; the state and the evidence are correct.
- A broker request that never settles holds its command's in-flight marker for the life of the process, so that command is never re-read. That is the ticket's "no overlapping read for a command" taken literally; the row stays unknown, which is the safe direction.

## Rollback

Revert the recovery reducer and the binding changes after reverting the dependent service wiring. The store's schema is unchanged, so an older reader still opens the database. Durable command records and audit evidence are kept.

## Activation

This is a build. It does not activate the capability, does not change the broker budget owner and does not authorize deployment. Activation is a separate qualification.
